en.name: Great Mosque
description:
The Great Mosque of Sousse was built by the Aghlabid Prince Abu al-‘Abbas Mohamed in 236/851. It is quadrilateral in form (59 m. x 51 m.) and is composed of a prayer hall which is preceded by a courtyard. The latter, greater in width than in depth (41 m. x 26 m.) bordered by porticoes along three sides, also dates from the Aghlabid period. The fourth portico, situated on the outside of the prayer hall, is a later addition which probably dates back to the 5th/11th century, but which was completely restored in 1085/1675.  
Along the top of the portico’s facade runs a *kufic* inscription mentioning the name of Mudam, the freed slave put in charge by the prince to supervise the work. This inscription is the oldest epigraphic frieze decorating the courtyard of a mosque to survive. Unlike the majority of Tunisian mosquecathedrals, Sousse does not possess a minaret; this absence can be explained by the proximity of the *ribat*’s vigil tower. Nevertheless, the call to prayer was proclaimed from the top of the north-eastern tower, which is surmounted by a domed kiosk dating from the Zirid period (5th/11th century).  
The hypostyle room features 13 naves and six bays. It echoes the T-plan of the ‘Uqba Mosque in terms of its median nave, which is larger than its lateral ones, and in terms of the dome in front of its *mihrab*, but differs from the ‘Uqba Mosque in terms of its architecture. The naves are covered by rubble vaults rather than ceilings, which are reinforced by semi-circular beam arches, supported on robust pillars laid out in the plan of a cross. This prayer hall seems to have developed through three stages. It is probable that Abu al-‘Abbas Mohamed proceeded to extend the oratory of Ziyadat Allah’s *kasbah* in order to obtain a room to accommodate 13 naves and three bays, covered by barrel vaults. The three bays at the back, covered by groin vaults, were added by Ibrahim II in 247/862. The *mihrab*, however, is from the Zirid era, as is attested to by the decoration of the semi-spherical dome, which consists of a series of niches with semi-circular backs and bands covered in flowery *kufic* inscription circling the columns that flank the *mihrab*. These architectural and decorative motifs are taken from the Zirid repertoire. The prayer hall is surmounted by two domes on the same line as the median nave. The Zirid dome, in front of the actual *mihrab*, is simple and austere; it is surmounted by a hemispherical skullcap dome placed directly on top of a square drum. The dome’s interior reveals the use of squinches, devoid of all decoration, encircled by archivolts that are linked together by arcatures. The second dome, which preceded the *mihrab* of Abu al-‘Abbas, and is situated on the same level as the fourth bay, as counted from the actual *mihrab*, echoes the construction principles of the Aghlabid domes of the Kairouanese school of architecture. The circular smooth skullcap sits on top of a an octagonal drum-base on scalloped squinches which fits within two arches resting on small protruding pillars, themselves supported by small corbels. Horseshoe drafted arches, the backs of which are pierced with openings, link the squinches together. An epigraphic band of *kufic* writing unravels itself above it. The entire piece is supported on sculpted tympanum featuring floral decorations inspired by the Kairouanese decorative repertoire.

es.name: Mezquita Mayor
description:
La Mezquita Mayor de Susa fue edificada por el príncipe aglabí Abu el-Abbas Mohamed en el año 236/851. Tiene forma de cuadrilátero (59 x 51 m) y se compone de una sala de oración precedida por un patio. Este último, más ancho que profundo (41 x 26 m), bordeado de pórticos por tres de sus lados, data igualmente de la época aglabí. El cuarto pórtico, situado ante la sala de oración, constituye un añadido que se remonta probablemente al siglo V/XI, aunque fue completamente restaurado en 1085/1675. En lo alto de la fachada del pórtico aparece una inscripción en caracteres cúficos que menciona el nombre de Mudam, esclavo manumitido al que el príncipe encargó supervisar las obras. Esta inscripción constituye el más antiguo friso epigráfico que decora el patio de una mezquita, conservado hasta la actualidad. Contrariamente a la mayoría de las mezquitas-catedrales tunecinas, la de Susa no posee ningún alminar; esta ausencia puede explicarse por la proximidad de la torre-vigía del *ribat*. La llamada a la oración debía hacerse desde lo alto de la torre situada en el ángulo noreste, coronada por un edículo con cúpula de la época zirí (siglo V/XI). La sala hipóstila está compuesta por trece naves y seis tramos. Puesto que la nave mediana es más larga que las naves laterales y posee una cúpula ante el *mihrab*, podemos decir que en esta mezquita se retoma la disposición en T de la mezquita de Uqba, aunque su arquitectura es diferente. Las naves no están cubiertas por techos sino por bóvedas de molduras, que refuerzan los arcos superpuestos de medio punto apoyados en robustos pilares cruciformes. Esta sala de oración parece haber pasado, al menos, por tres etapas de construcción. Es probable que Abu el-Abbas Mohamed hubiera procedido a la ampliación del oratorio de la alcazaba de Ziyadat Allah con intención de obtener una sala de trece naves y tres tramos cubiertos por bóvedas de cañón. Los tres tramos del fondo, cubiertos por bóvedas de aristas, debieron ser añadidos posteriormente por Ibrahim II en el año 247/862. El *mihrab* es de época zirí, como lo testimonia la decoración de la bóveda esférica, compuesta por una hilera de nichos con fondo semicilíndrico, así como por la presencia de anillos con inscripciones de caligrafía cúfica florida sobre las columnas que lo flanquean. Estos motivos arquitectónicos y decorativos están tomados del repertorio zirí.  
La sala de oración está coronada por dos cúpulas en la nave mediana. La cúpula zirí situada ante el actual *mihrab* es simple y austera, y está culminada por un casquete hemisférico situado directamente sobre un tambor cuadrado. El interior del cimborrio deja ver el empleo de trompas desprovistas de toda decoración, aunque su contorno aparece rodeado por aristas unidas entre sí mediante arcos. La segunda cúpula que precede el *mihrab* de Abu el-Abbas, situada en el cuarto tramo desde el actual *mihrab*, es el principio de la construcción de cimborrios aglabíes en la escuela de Kairuán. El casquete circular liso corona un tambor octogonal sobre trompas en forma de concha, inscritas en dos arcos que reposan sobre pequeños pilares en saledizo soportados, a su vez, por unas corbeletas. Los arcos de medio punto emparejados y cuyo fondo queda horadado por aperturas, unen las trompas entre sí. Encima de ellos se desarrolla una banda epigráfica de estilo cúfico.  
El conjunto reposa sobre unos tímpanos esculpidos con decoraciones florales, inspiradas en el repertorio decorativo de Kairuán.

fr.name: La Grande Mosquée
description:
La Grande Mosquée de Sousse fut édifiée par le prince aghlabide Abou el-Abbas Mohamed en 236/851. Elle a la forme d’un quadrilatère (59 m x 51 m) et se compose d’une salle de prière précédée d’une cour. Cette dernière, plus large que profonde (41 m x 26 m), bordée de portiques sur trois côtés, date également de l’époque aghlabide. Le quatrième portique, situé au-devant de la salle de prière, est une adjonction qui remonte probablement au Ve/XIe siècle, mais elle fut complètement restaurée en 1085/1675. En haut de la façade du portique court une inscription coufique mentionnant le nom de Moudam, l’affranchi chargé par le prince de superviser les travaux. Cette inscription est la plus ancienne frise épigraphique décorant la cour d’une mosquée qui nous soit parvenue. Contrairement à la majorité des mosquées-cathédrales tunisiennes, celle de Sousse ne comporte pas de minaret; cette absence peut s’expliquer par la proximité de la tour vigie du *ribat*. Néanmoins, l’appel à la prière se faisait du haut de la tour d’angle nord-est qui est surmontée d’un édicule à coupole datable de l’époque ziride (Ve/XIe siècle).  
La salle hypostyle comporte 13 nefs et 6 travées. Avec la nef médiane, plus large que les nefs latérales, et la coupole devant le *mihrab*, elle reprend la disposition en T de la mosquée de Oqba, mais elle en diffère par son architecture. Les nefs sont couvertes non pas de plafonds mais de voûtes en moellons que renforcent des arcs doubleaux en plein cintre reposant sur des piliers robustes de plan en croix. Cette salle de prière semble être passée par trois étapes. Il est probable que Abou el-Abbas Mohamed ait procédé à l’agrandissement de l’oratoire de la casbah de Ziyadat Allah pour obtenir une salle à 13 nefs et 3 travées, couvertes de voûtes en berceaux. Les trois travées du fond, couvertes en voûtes d’arêtes, furent rajoutées par Ibrahim II en 247/862. Le *mihrab*, quant à lui, est d’époque ziride, comme l’attestent la décoration du cul-de-four par une série de niches à fond semi-cylindrique et la présence de bagues à inscriptions coufiques fleuries sur les colonnes qui flanquent le mihrab. Ces motifs architecturaux et décoratifs sont hérités du répertoire ziride.  
La salle de prière est surmontée au niveau de la nef médiane de deux coupoles. La coupole ziride, au-devant du *mihrab* actuel, est simple et austère; elle est surmontée d’une calotte hémisphérique posée directement sur un tambour carré. L’intérieur du dôme révèle l’emploi de trompes dénuées de tout décor et circonscrites de voussures reliées entre elles par des arcatures. La seconde coupole qui précédait le *mihrab* de Abou el-Abbas, située au niveau de la quatrième travée, partant du *mihrab* actuel, reprend le principe de la construction des dômes aghlabides de l’école de Kairouan. La calotte circulaire lisse coiffe un tambour octogonal sur trompes en coquilles s’inscrivant dans deux arcs reposant sur des petits piliers en saillie, eux-mêmes supportés par des corbelets. Des arcs outrepassés appareillés et dont le fond est percé d’ouvertures relient les trompes entre elles. Au-dessus se développe un bandeau épigraphique de style coufique. L’ensemble repose sur des tympans sculptés de décorations florales qui s’inspirent du répertoire décoratif kairouanais.

en.name: Karpino Monastery
short_description: The Karpino Monastery was the cultural and literary centre of the Kumanovo region throughout the Middle Ages. The Church within the Karpino Monastery is dedicated to the Presentation of the Virgin in the Temple. It was built of crafted stone in the form of a single-nave basilica with an apse forming a triconch. Parts of the 16th and 17th-century edifice and wall paintings have been preserved during its reconstruction in 1892, including the frescoes depicting the Virgin and Child, as well as the effigies of St. Theodore Tyron and St. Theodore Stratylates. The exquisite early 17th-century wooden iconostasis has been preserved in the Monastery Church including seven valuable original icons which were painted by Nikola Zoograf and his students.
history: According to the legends, the monastery was originally built in the 14th century, having been set on fire and reconstructed many times. The present-day edifice of the Karpino Monastery dates from 1892, when it was restored to preserve some portions of the structure and frescoes dating from the 16th and 17th centuries. Throughout the Middle Ages, the monastery was a sanctuary for many Macedonian monks who acquired their education to become priests and serve God and the Church. Extensive literary activities were developed there by monks who used to prescribe various liturgical books, manuscripts and other patristic literature. In the late 19th century, monks from the Karpino Monastery formed a public school for teaching children from neighbouring villages.
keywords: iconostasis; frescoes; icons

ar.name: سيـــف.
description:
تتكون القطعة من سيف من الصلب ذي مقبض من قرن حيوان وغمد مكسو بالفضة المموهة بالذهب. ويزخرف النصل جامات بها كتابات: يوجد في أعلى النصل جامة بارزة تحمل النص "عمل الحاج صنقور"، وأسفلها آية رقم 1 من سورة مريم "كهيعص"، يليها جامة بارزة تحمل النص "سلطان فاتح محمد خان"، وأسفلها الآيتان رقم 1 و 2 من سورة الشورى "حم - عسق". والكتابات والزخارف التي تظهر على النصل منفذة بالتكفيت بالذهب. ويزخرف الغمد رسومات نباتية بارزة. وصاحب السيف هو السلطان العثمانى محمد الثاني الفاتح الذي حكم في الأعوام 855 - 886 هـ / 1451 – 1481 م.  
  
استورد العرب السيوف من بلاد فارس والهند، وكان أجود أنواع السيوف يصنع في خراسان ودمشق وطليطلة.

تفنَّن العثمانيون في صناعة السيوف وزخرفتها، ونافسوا الإيرانيين في ذلك. واستخدموها في السلم والحرب، وحفلات البلاط، وخاصة تلك التي تحمل اسم سلاطين آل عثمان، مثل هذه القطعة التي تحمل اسم السلطان محمد الثاني، واسم صانعها.
keywords: تكفيت؛ خط؛ زخرفة نباتية؛ سيف؛ غمد؛ نصل.
materials: النصل من الحديد الصلب، والمقبض من قرن حيوان، والغمد مكسو بالفضة.  واستخدمت طريقة التكفيت بالذهب والفضة في النقوش والزخارف.
tags: النصل من الحديد الصلب، والمقبض من قرن حيوان، والغمد مكسو بالفضة. واستخدمت طريقة التكفيت بالذهب والفضة في النقوش والزخارف.

en.name: Sword.
description:
A sword composed of a steel blade and a hilt made of animal horn. The scabbard is of gilded silver. The blade has decorative cartouches with inscriptions inside them. On the upper part of the blade there is a prominent medallion, which bears the following text: 'The work of al-Hajj Sanqur', and below this medallion is another inscription of the first verse of the chapter 'Mariam' from the Qur'an: 'Kaf Ha Ya Ayn Sad'. This line is followed byanother cartouche bearing the text, 'Sultan Fatih Muhammad Khan'.Below this cartouche are written verses 1 and 2 from the Qur'anic chapter 'al-Ha Mim', and 'Ain Sin Qaf'*.* The inscriptions and decorations that appear on the blade are executed in gold inlay. The scabbard is ornamented with vegetal decoration carved in high relief. The owner of the sword was the Ottoman Sultan Muhammad II Al Fatih ('The Conquerer').  
The Arabs imported swords from Iran and India. Quality swords were produced in Khurasan (Persia, now Iran), Damascus in Syria and Toledo in Spain.

Ottomans excelled in making swords and their decoration rivalled that of the Iranians. In addition to their military use, swords bearing the names of Ottoman sultans were worn on gala celebrations at the court. This sword bears the name of Sultan Mohammad II and the name of its maker.
keywords: Inlay; inscription; vegetal decoration; sword; scabbard; blade; arms; armours; military object; weapon; weaponry
materials: The blade: iron-steel; the hilt: animal horn. The scabbard: gilded silver. Inscriptions and decorations: gold and silver inlay.
tags: the hilt: animal horn. The scabbard: gilded silver. Inscriptions and decorations: gold and silver inlay.

es.name: Espada.
description:
Espada compuesta por una hoja de acero y una empuñadura de cuerno. La vaina está hecha con plata dorada. En la hoja hay varios cartuchos decorativos que contienen inscripciones. En la parte superior de la hoja sobresale un medallón, en el que figura el siguiente texto: "Obra de al-Hayy Sanqur", y debajo del medallón hay otra inscripción con un texto coránico, la primera aleya de la sura "María", compuesta por las letras *kaf, ha, ya, ayn, sad*. A continuación hay otro cartucho con la inscripción "Sultán Fatih Muhammad Jan" y, debajo, se leen los dos primeros versículos de la sura 42, "La consulta", las letras *ha, mim, ayn, sin, qaf*. Las inscripciones y adornos que presenta la hoja están hechos con incrustaciones de oro y plata. La vaina está ornada con decoración vegetal grabada en relieve. El propietario de la espada era el sultán otomano Mehmed II.  
Los árabes importaban espadas de Irán y de la India. Las espadas de mayor calidad se forjaban en Jurasán (Persia), Damasco (Siria) y Toledo (España).

Los otomanos destacaron en el arte de fabricación de espadas, comparables en su decoración a las iraníes. Las espadas, que llevaban el nombre de los sultanes otomanos, se usaban en batallas y en las celebraciones de gala de la corte. Esta lleva los nombres del sultán Mehmed II y del fabricante.
dates: 848-850 de la Hégira / 1444-46 d. C. o bien 855-886 de la Hégira / 1451-1481 d. C.
keywords: Incrustación; inscripción; decoración vegetal; espada; vaina; hoja.
materials: Hoja: acero; empuñadura: cuerno; vaina: plata dorada; inscripciones e incrustaciones de oro y plata.
tags: inscripciones e incrustaciones de oro y plata.

fr.name: Sabre.
description:
Sabre composé d'une lame d'acier et d'une poignée en corne animale. Le fourreau est en argent doré. La lame est ornée de cartouches décoratifs épigraphiés. En partie supérieure de la lame, un important médaillon contient le texte suivant : “œuvre de al-Hadjdj Sanqour” et, en dessous, le premier verset de la sourate “Myriam”, “Kaf Ha Ya Ayn Sad'.” Cette ligne est suivie d'un autre cartouche au nom du sultan propriétaire de l'arme : “Sultan Fatih Muhammad Khan”, soit Muhammad II al-Fatih (“le Conquérant”). En dessous sont gravés les versets 1 et 2 des sourates “al-Ha Mim” et “Ayn Sin Qaf”. Les inscriptions et le décor sont en incrustations d'or. Le fourreau est orné d'une décoration végétale gravée en haut relief.  
Les Arabes importaient des armes blanches d'Iran et d'Inde. Les armes de qualité étaient produites à Khourassan (Iran), Damas (Syrie) et Tolède (Espagne).

Les Ottomans excellaient dans l'art de la fabrication de sabres dont la décoration rivalisait avec les sabres iraniens. En plus de leur usage militaire, les sabres ornés du nom des sultans ottomans étaient portés aux cérémonies de gala à la cour. Sur ce sabre sont inscrits le nom du sultan Mohammed II et le nom de celui qui l'a fabriqué.
materials: Lame : acier ; poignée : corne ; fourreau : argent doré ; inscriptions et ornementation : incrustations d’or et d’argent.
tags: inscriptions et ornementation : incrustations d’or et d’argent.

en.name: *Dokhla* (wedding dress)
short_description: This tunic is entirely embroidered with gold-plated silver thread. This is the most important element of the marriage ceremony (jelwa) in Nabeul (Tunisia). The rectangular tunic's splendour comes from its incredibly rich embroidery, which is made of various different silk ribbons, all embellished with tal. In fact, the embroidery entirely covers the fabric itself. The breast and belt areas are embroidered with sequins and gold thread. The tunic is calf-length, and a luxurious pair of silk trousers can be seen beneath, covered in gold embroidery to match the sleeves. In addition to this, one of the bride's many items of jewellery is a great chain of golden rings, a rihana, which she wears with a large necklace made of a scented material. Lastly, the bride's head is covered by an embroidered veil made of muslin and silk.
keywords: Embroidery from Nabeul; sequins and gold thread
materials: Embroidered fabric with gold-plated silver thread
partner: Higher Institute for the Study of Contemporary History of Tunisia, University of Manouba

fr.name: Costume de mariage (*dokhla*)
short_description: Tunique toute brodée avec du fil d’argent plat doré. C’est l’élément principal de la cérémonie de la *jelwa* à l’occasion des noces à Nabeul. Il s’agit d’une tunique rectangulaire, sa splendeur réside dans sa broderie qui recèle une étonnante richesse. Elle est faite de l’assemblage de plusieurs rubans de soie brodée de *tal*. La broderie cache entièrement le tissu. Le plastron et la bande médiane sont brodés de paillettes et de cannetille. La tunique descend aux mollets. Au bas, on voit passer les deux larges jambes d’un pantalon d’apparat en satin. Il est couvert de broderie dorée assortie à celle des manches. Parmi les bijoux de la mariée, la grande chaîne d’or aux anneaux plats, la *rihana*, accompagnée d’un grand collier de pâte parfumée. Enfin, la tête de la mariée est couverte d’un voile brodé en mousseline de soie.
keywords: Broderie de Nabeul; Paillettes et cannetille
materials: Tissu brodé avec du fil d’argent plat doré
partner: Institut Supérieur d’histoire contemporaine de la Tunisie, Université de la Manouba

en.name: Ewer
description: The wide base is decorated and fluted. A doughnut-shaped body rises from the base, with eight outward-pointing projections along its upper edge. The body narrows towards the top. The handle is attached to the body and the mouth with double rivets; a clasp at the very top of the handle secures the lid. The handle tapers towards the mouth with a serrated edge. The lid, shaped like a small minaret, incorporates a spout that extends from the body to its top; it is inclined outward, with its surface decorated with a diamond motif. Both the lid and neck are further adorned with fluted decoration.
keywords: Ewer; Ottomans; copper; bronze

en.name: *London-Paris-Constantinople* \[…\] *Orient Express. Paris-Munich-Vienna-Budapest-Belgrade & Constantinople: fast and direct service, without your car and without your passport* \[…\] *Winter 1888–89 ...*
short_description: Founded in 1872, the Compagnie Internationale des Wagons-lits was originally a Belgian company. Its founder (Georges Nagelmackers) had the idea of creating a luxury train line, without the need for changes at each border, in order to allow wealthier tourists a more comfortable journey. The opening of the famous Orient Express between Paris and Constantinople in 1883 was an extremely successful example of this.
keywords: Railways; travelling; Istanbul

fr.name: *Londres-Paris-Constantinople...Orient-Express. Paris-Munich-Vienne-Budapest-Belgrade & Constantinople: service rapide sans changement de voiture, sans passeport... Hiver 1888-89...*
short_description: Fondée en 1872, la Compagnie internationale des wagons-lits est une entreprise française d'origine belge. L'amibition de son fondateur (Georges Nagelmackers) est de créer des trains de luxe, sans changements aux frontières, afin de permettre aux touristes les plus fortunés des voyages confortables. En 1883, la création du grand express d'Orient entre Paris et Constantinople est un véritable succès.
keywords: Chemins de fer; voyages; Istanbul

description: هذه الطاولة المنخفضة المستطيلة ذات الأرجل الأربعة مزخرفة بشكل واسع بمشغولات اللكر/ البرنيق على سطح الطاولة. و حول الإطار الداخلي يوجد أرابيسك مرسوم ومزهر مطلي بالذهب تحيط بنقوش ضمن مستطيلات وعلى سطح هذه الطاولة يوجد شباب وشابات يستريحون ويحتفلون ويصيدون في مشهد طبيعي غني وطراز التصوير يعكس رسوم المخطوطات في الشعر الفارسي المعروف.

en.name: Table (*khwan*) with scenes of princely leisure and inscribed with Persian poetry
description: This low, rectangular wood table on four legs is extensively ornamented with lacquerwork on the table top. Around the interior rim are painted and gilded floral arabesques surrounding inscriptions in cartouches. On the surface of this table, young men and women repose, feast, and hunt in abundant landscapes, and their style of depiction echoes manuscript illustrations of canonical Persian poetry.

en.name: Map of the Hijaz Railway. Designation in Ottoman Turkish and Arabic
description: The map is part of the Pocket Atlas of the Ottoman Lands: The Geographical and Statistical Conditions of the Ottoman State. It represents territories extending from Egypt and the eastern Mediterranean in the west to the Euphrates River in the east, and from Damascus in the north to the Hijaz region in the south. The map identifies regions, towns, ports, deserts, mountain ranges and maritime routes in Ottoman Turkish written in Arabic script. A route beginning in Damascus and continuing through Darʿa and Maʿan toward Medina corresponds to the Hijaz Railway. The map table heading is given first in Ottoman Turkish and immediately below in Arabic, reading: "Map of the Hijaz Railway", with a list of stations underneath. Each location is accompanied by a numerical value expressed in kilometres, indicating cumulative distances measured from Damascus.
keywords: Map; Trainlines; Hijaz; Syria, Türkiye

en.name: Martorelli Inn (C.so Garibaldi 4-6)
description:
Near the Neapolitan Gate on Piazza di Corte there is the formerly named Casino Stazi (after its owner, Giovan Battista Stazi, who restored the building in 1768) which was transformed in the 19th century into the famous Martorelli Inn (Locanda Martorelli), a staging point for those Grand Tourists who travelled from Rome to the Alban Hills or stopped over to continue towards Naples.  
  
The main hall on the piano nobile was decorated in 1770 by the Polish artist Taddeo Kuntze, who executed a pictorial cycle inspired by the history of ancient Aricia: the myth of Diana, Hippolytus and Fedra, the conspiracy against Turno Edornio, the battle of the Regillo Lake, the Egeria Nymph and Numa Pompilio. The inn that hosted artists such as Turner, Corot, Nino Costa, and writers such as Andersen, Gogol, Ibsen, Longfellow and D'Azeglio, is now home to the Grand Tour museum. In a room on the third floor they recently found various drawings – doodles, portraits and caricatures of bourgeois, bandits, priests and even a self-portrait of D'Azeglio – that the artists had sketched on the walls.

it.name: Locanda Martorelli (C.so Garibaldi 4-6)
description:
Nei pressi della Porta Napoletana sorge sulla Piazza di Corte il Casino Stazi, che nell'Ottocento fu trasformato nella celebre Locanda Martorelli, punto di sosta dei viaggiatori del Grand Tour, che da Roma si recavano ai Colli Albani o sostavano per proseguire verso Napoli.  
   
La sala principale al piano nobile della locanda fu decorata nel 1770 dal pittore polacco Taddeo Kuntze, che vi realizzò un ciclo ispirato alla storia dell'antica Ariccia: il mito di Diana, Ippolito e Fedra, la congiura contro Turno Edornio, la battaglia del Lago Regillo, La Ninfa Egeria e Numa Pompilio. La locanda che ospitò artisti come Turner, Corot, Nino Costa, letterati come Andersen, Gogol, Ibsen, Longfellow e D'Azeglio, è oggi sede del museo del Grand Tour. In una sala del terzo piano sono stati ritrovati di recente, erano coperti da carta da parati, vari schizzi e caricature (disegni fantasiosi, borghesi, briganti, preti e un autoritratto di D'Azeglio) che gli artisti di passaggio avevano abbozzato sulle pareti.

cs.name: Čestný dvůr “Amtshof”
description: Požár r. 1719 zničil dosavadní vybavení interiérů zámku. Přestavbu projektoval Ch. A. Oedtl, který komplex budov sjednotil fasádou. Upravil také několik domů ve městě. Míčovna byla přeměněna na zimní jízdárnu a divadelní sál na knihovnu, postavena byla salla terrena s terasou a upraven čestný dvůr, lemovaný bustami antických imperátorů, ozdobený putti a dekorativními vázami. Kované brány jsou původní (H. G. Forster).
artist: Christian Alexander Oedtl (1654 Paznaun – 1731 Vídeň), Ignác Lengelacher (1698 Unter Paissenberg – 1780 Baden), Heinrich Gottfried Forster

en.name: “Amtshof” or the Ceremonial Courtyard
description: In 1719 a fire destroyed the chateau interiors. Reconstruction was undertaken by C. A. Oedtl, who unified the chateau complex with a single frontage. He also rebuilt several other houses in the town. A ballroom was converted into a winter riding hall, and the theatre hall was reconstructed into a library; a *sala terrena* with a terrace was added and the ceremonial courtyard was refurbished, lined with busts of ancient emperors, and further decorated with *putti* and ornamental vases. The wrought-iron gates by H. G. Forster are original.
artist: Christian Alexander Oedtl (1654 Paznaun – 1731 Vienna), Ignaz Lengelacher (1698 Unter Peissenberg – 1780 Baden), Heinrich Gottfried Forster

ar.name: بلاطة جدارية.
description: بلاطة كانت تشكِّل في ما مضى جزءاً من تشكيل زخرفي متكامل من أشجار السرو والمزهريات. أشجار السرو مرسومة بحواف شوكية تحيط برسم فاتح اللون على شكل حراشف السمك؛ أما المزهريات فموزعة بين الأشجار. يمكن رؤية نموذج من البلاط الزخرفي المشابه، إن لم يكن المتطابق (يعود تاريخه إلى القرن العاشر /السادس عشر)، في ضريح الشيخ الصوفي محي الدين بن عربي (560- 637 / 1165- 1240)، الموجود داخل مسجد السلطان سليم الأول في دمشق. إن استخدام أشجار السرو في مبانٍ كهذه يعتبر ملائماً، لأن شجرة السرو، كما يقال، ترمز إلى الكمال الكامن، وأنها تحمل بيولوجياً عناصر الذكورة والأنوثة معاً في داخلها. ويشبِّهون إذعانها للريح بخضوع 'المسلم الأصيل' لإرادة الله.

كانت هذه البلاطة ذات يوم جزءاً من إطار زخرفي موصول، مُؤلَّف من أشجار السرو والزهور. وشجرة السرو هنا، مُنفَّذة بحافة نافرة، وهي معبأة بقالب حرشفة سمكية، بلون أفتح. ثمَّة رسوم مشابهة لا تزال تُزيِّن مزار الشيخ (الولي) الصوفي محي الدين بن عربي، بدمشق.
dates: القرن العاشر- الحادي عشر / السادس عشر- السابع عشر.

en.name: Wall tile.
description: A tile which once formed a part of a continuous decorative scheme of cypress trees and vases of flowers. The Cypress tree is rendered with a spiky border and filled-in with a lighter coloured fish-scale pattern; vases with flowers are positioned between the trees. A similar, if not identical scheme of decorative tiles (dating to the AH 10th / AD 16th century), can be seen in the mausoleum of the famous Sufi Saint, Muhyi al-Din ibn Arabi (AH 560–637 / AD 1165–1240), located inside the Sultan Salim I Mosque in Damascus. The use of cypress trees is appropriate for such a monument, since the cypress is said to symbolise potential wholeness for, biologically, the tree holds both the masculine and feminine principles within it. It is known as the 'perfect Muslim' because of its submission 'Islam' to the wind: 'God's will'.

This tile once formed part of a continuous decorative scheme of cypresses and flowers. The cypress tree here is rendered with a spiky border and filled in with a lighter-coloured fish-scale pattern. Similar ones still decorate the shrine of the Sufi saint Muhyi al-Din ibn Arabi in Damascus.
keywords: Religious art; architectural element; floral decoration; symbol
materials: Earthenware, underglaze painted in cobalt-blue, turquoise, black and manganese purple.

es.name: Azulejo.
description:
Este azulejo formaba parte de un conjunto decorativo compuesto por cipreses y jarrones de flores. La copa del ciprés está dibujada con una gruesa línea dentada y rellenada con escamas de color más claro; entre los cipreses se aprecian jarrones de flores. En el mausoleo del famoso santo sufí Muhyi al-Din ibn Arabi (560-637 / 1165-1240), situado dentro de la mezquita del Sultán Selim I de Damasco, puede verse una composición decorativa similar –si no idéntica– fechada en el siglo X / XVI.  
El ciprés simboliza la posible completitud al aunar biológicamente lo femenino y lo masculino, así que resulta un motivo apropiado para este tipo de monumento. Este árbol es conocido como el “musulmán perfecto” por su sumisión (“islam”) al viento, esto es, a la voluntad divina.

Este azulejo formaba parte de una composición decorativa con cipreses y flores. Aquí, la copa del ciprés está dibujada con una línea dentada y rellena con escamas de tonalidad más clara. En el mausoleo del santo sufí Muhyi al-Din ibn Arabi de Damasco aún se pueden contemplar azulejos similares.
dates: Siglo X o XI de la Hégira / XVI-XVII d. C.
keywords: arte religioso; elementos arquitectónicos; decoración floral
materials: Cerámica pintada en azul cobalto, turquesa, negro y manganeso bajo vidriado.
tags: Cerámica pintada en azul cobalto, turquesa, negro y manganeso bajo vidriado.

fr.name: Carreau mural.
description: Carreau ayant fait partie jadis d'une composition décorative continue de cyprès et de vases de fleurs. Le rendu du cyprès se caractérise par un contour hérissé et une zone centrale à motif d'écailles de poisson de couleur plus claire. Des vases de fleurs sont répartis entre les arbres. Une composition similaire, bien que non identique, de carreaux décoratifs du Xe siècle H (XVIe siècle J.-C.) est visible dans le mausolée du fameux soufi Muhyi al-Din ibn Arabi (560-637 H / 1165-1240 J.-C.) situé dans la mosquée du sultan Selim Ier à Damas. L'utilisation des cyprès est ici appropriée car cet arbre est censé symboliser un état de complétude potentiel puisque il contient biologiquement les principes à la fois féminin et masculin. On lui attribue le qualificatif de “parfait musulman” puisqu'il se soumet (“islam”) au vent, “la volonté de Dieu.”

Ce carreau faisait autrefois partie d’une composition décorative continue de cyprès et de fleurs. Le cyprès est rendu ici avec un contour hérissé et un intérieur rempli d’un motif d’écailles de poisson de couleur plus claire. Une composition similaire décore encore le mausolée du soufi Saint Muhyi al-Din ibn Arabi à Damas.
dates: Xe-XIe siècle de l’Hégire (XVIe-XVIIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: art religieux ; éléments architecturaux ; décoration florale

en.name: The Antara locality
description: The photograph depicts tents beside the railway in an open, arid landscape at the Antara locality, identified by the Turkish State Archives as kilometre 420.320 from Damascus on the Hamidiye Hijaz Railway. This distance places the site approximately 2.4 kilometres north of Uneiza station, assuming the same starting point for the railway measurements. The tents suggest a temporary encampment, although its function and any connection with the nearby station remain unconfirmed.

en.name: Underglass painted calligraphic panel
description:
This underglass-painted panel consists of inscriptions in black *jali thuluth* (calligraphic Arabic script) inside an oval frame of leaves in a chestnut shade of gold. At the top is the word "Allah", below that the word "Muhammad", and in the centre the phrase "Ya aman Ali", all written as symmetric mirror compositions (*müsenna*). Between the two "ya" letters is a picture of a Bektaşi headdress and below it the figure of a submission stone (*teslim taşı*). The lines of the two lams are extended upwards to form two halberds, and the letter "ya" in the word ‘Ali’ forms his double-pointed sword Zülfikar. Around the lower edge of the oval frame appears the signature of the artist written in *riq‘a* script: "Painted by Hafız Ahmed Feyzi from the Demirhan neighbourhood of Bursa." In the lower corners of the panel are medallions formed of leaves painted in chestnut brown tones of gold, and in the upper corners are compositions of leaves and flowers.  
The pictures and scripts under glass are products of folk art. Such works are applied to the back of a piece of glass in reverse. They are dependent on the glass because the work disappears if the glass is broken. Their subjects are mostly illustrations of folkloric myths, stories, beliefs and symbols. Such panels were seen in the homes, small mosques, meeting places of dervishes and tombs in the past.
holder: Vehbi Koç Foundation Sadberk Hanim Museum
keywords: Underglass painting; glass; calligraphy
partner: Vehbi Koç Foundation Sadberk Hanim Museum

en.name: Bab al-Bahr (Gate of the Sea)
description:
Bab al-Bahr, or Gate of the Sea (now called Saracen Gate) is a gateway to the sea. It was built along with the gates of Mahdia in Ifriqiya and that of Honaïne, near Tlemcen, A veritable arch of triumph, it was the maritime entrance to the port. It was built in 460 / 1068, at the same time as the five other gates around Bejaya, under the reign of al-Nasir, founder of the city.  
Ships entering the port passed under its under its pointed arch of solid brick resting on stone masonry pedestals. Above this arch a stone wall displays an arch similar to the first, but forming a wider vault that supported a walkway and guard room. Despite its monumental design, the arch of Bab al-Bahr retained its pure form.

fr.name: Bab al-Bahr
description: De même que celle de Mahdia en Ifriqiya et celle d’Honaïne, près de Tlemcen, Bab al-Bahr, ou porte de la Mer, actuellement appelée porte Sarrasine, est une porte de la mer. Véritable arc de triomphe, elle était l’entrée maritime du port. Elle fut édifiée en 460/1068 en même temps que les cinq autres portes de l’enceinte de Béjaia sous le règne d’al-Nasir, fondateur de la cité. Les navires entrant dans le port passaient sous son arche en arc brisé construit en briques pleines reposant sur des piédroits en maçonnerie de pierre. Au-dessus de cet arc, un mur de pierre porte un arc semblable au premier mais formant une voûte plus large qui supportait le chemin de ronde et la salle de garde. Malgré son aspect monumental, l’arc de Bab al-Bahr a gardé la pureté de son galbe.

en.name: Muhammad Tawfiq Pasha (1852–1892)
short_description: Portrait of Muhammad Tawfiq Pasha (1852–1892). After the deposition of his father Ismail Pasha, Muhammad Tawfiq took over the government in Egypt. The Arabi revolution diminished his power radically. In 1882 he asked for help from Great Britain. British troops suppressed the Arabi revolution and occupied Egypt. Muhammad Tawfiq became ruler at the grace of the British government.
keywords: Muhammad Tawfiq Pasha; Egypt; Arabi (Urabi) revolution; Great Britain

en.name: Panel of gratitude for Dr. Paul Meyer, Berne, Switzerland
description: The wayfarer depicted in the mountains represents the recipient of this gift himself. The stained glass panel was given to Dr. Paul Meyer, the long-standing principal of the Gymnasium (grammar school) in Berne and "deserving supporter of school outings".
artist: Albin Schweri, design, (1885 Ramsen, Switzerland - 1946, Berne, Switzerland); Louis Halter, realization, (1886, Elsass - 1956, Berne, Switzerland)

en.name: Ewer
description: This jug is a rare example of early Islamic glasswork that carried any form of inscription. It is a rich, deep turquoise, a spectacular colour which was extremely unusual for any glass of this period. Made of mould-blown glass, the ewer is a drop form with a short foot, a thistle mouth and an extruded spout. A simple bent handle links the mouth and the body. A broad band of moulded *kufic* inscription that consists of repetitions of the Arabic word *al-Malk* (ownership) runs around its body divided by palmettes. The technique of moulding *kufic* inscriptions is found on glass vessels from Mesopotamia and from northeast Iran.
keywords: Glass; Ewer; Free-blown; Abbasid
materials: Glass; free-blown with applied, impressed and tooled decoration
tags: free-blown with applied, impressed and tooled decoration

ar.name: ورقة مصحف
description: صفحة المصحف هذه مكتوبة بخط بيني الذي يقع بين طراز الخط الحجازي والكوفي. وورقة الرق تظهر الطور الحاسم في تطور نسخ المصاحف. وبحلول نهاية القرن الخامس الهجري فإن الأحرف العربية بدأت تكتب منقطة كما يظهر في هذه الصفحة وبنفس الحبر البني المستخدم للكتابة. وترى علامات التشكيل  بشكل نقاط حمراء وخضراء وتقسيمات الآيات معلّمة باستخدام فواصل مائلة بالحبر البني .

en.name: Qur’an leaf
description: This Qur’an leaf is written in a transitional script that lies between the Hijazi and the *kufic* script styles. This vellum leaf demonstrates a crucial phase in the development of Quranic scripts. Towards the end of the first century Hijra, the Arabic letters started to acquire dots, as shown in this leaf, in the same brown ink used for the writing. Vocalization marks are seen in red and green dots, and the verse dividers are marked by the use of slanting dashes in brown ink.

en.name: Sanayeh Garden
description: This green lung of the city is very popular among the neighbourhood residents. The garden features a large Ottoman fountain and covers a total surface area of 22,000 square metres.
history: The garden is one of the oldest public open-air spaces in the capital. Khalil Pasha (1864–1923), commander of the Turkish Sixth Army during World War I, had the park built in 1907. The park has had many names since its construction in the early 20th century, It was first called the Hamidi Public Garden, but was renamed the René Muawad Garden in honour of President René Muawad, who was assassinated nearby on November 22, 1989. However, it has been referred to as Sanayeh Park by the public for decades.
keywords: Beirut; Sanayeh; Garden; Public; Space; René Muawad

en.name: *Atik Valide Mosque*
short_description: The majority of Turkish painters in the 19th century were Ottoman officers who had studied abroad. Hüseyin Zekai Pasha was one of those painters. Following his education at the Kuleli Military High School, he continued his studies at the Military Academy (*Mektebi Harbiye*), where he had a chance to learn technical drawing and perspective. His first period was realistic and his pictorial representation includes scenes or events from everyday life. In his first works, Hüseyin Zekai Pasha followed the painting tradition of 19th century, including thin paint dough and light colours. He made changes in his techniques through the Galatasaray Exhibition and eventually he turned into an impressionist whose work was dominated by thicker brush strokes.
keywords: Painting; Hüseyin Zekai Pasha; orientalist Turkish painters

en.name: Vác Cathedral
description:
The cathedral is arranged around a central, open, floor plan. Under the organ loft is a section covered by a barrel-vault, either side of which are the Altars of St. Nicholas and St. John of Nepomuk; Kremserschmidt's *Crucifixion* is located in this section as well. The central area of the Cathedral is topped by a cupola without a drum, according to local architectural tradition, and painted with a rendition of the *Triumph of the Holy Trinity*. Either side are copies of paintings by Guido Reni: *St. Michael the Archangel* and the *Assumption of the Virgin Mary*. The extended sanctuary, on both sides of which are entrances to the vestries, is elevated, and the stone statuettes on the balustrade are 16th-century Renaissance works; the frescoes were painted in 1942. The walls of the church are articulated by Corinthian columns, and with its features simple and classical, the combined effect is monumental. The prebendary stalls were completed in 1829.  
The layout of the façade is simple using basic cubic shapes. The monumental portico, guarded by a tower on both sides, consists of Corinthian columns and a 2-1-1-2 “rhythm”. This layout resembles the Church of Saint-Sulpice in Paris, which was designed by Niccolò Servandoni, Ganneval's tutor. Above the dentil mouldings are statues of the Virgin Mary, St. Joseph, St. Peter, St. Paul, St. John and St. Jacob. The inscription on the attic reads: “D. O. M. / IN. HONOREM. ASSUMTAE. IN. COELUM. VIRGINIS. / ET. S. MICHAELIS. ARCHANGELI”. (“D\[eo\]. O\[ptimo\]. M\[aximo\] – The God, The Blessed, The Greatest / In Honour of the Virgin \[Mary's\] Assumption to Heaven and to St. Michael Archangel”). Behind the columns, on the wall of the entrance hall, there are biblical scenes in high relief. Above the three entrance gates is Migazzi's coat-of-arms. Two doors open from the side walls of the entrance hall and bear the first (1761) and final year (1777) of construction. The entrance to the crypt is found behind the sanctuary, built in 1900, after the nave hatch was closed up.

Vác Cathedral was an outstanding building when it was built in the 18th-century. In both Hungary and Central Europe, it was a unique example of early French Neo-Classicism at a time when the Baroque, late Baroque and Rococo styles dominated. Combining Neo-Classical elements and simple geometric shapes, the building appeared exceptionally novel to Central Europeans of the time, and it was for this reason that local artists and craftsmen did not follow the style for decades to come.
artist: Count Károly Esterházy, Bishop of Vác (1757–1761); Bishop Christoph Anton Migazzi (1756–1757; 1761–1785)

Architect: Isidore Ganneval (c. 1730–1786); stonemason: Matthias Chmelik; sculptors: Joseph Bechert, Carlo Adami, Joseph Minich; painters: Franz Anton Maulbertsch (1724–1796), J. M. Schmidt (alias Feigel Georg Kremserschmidt), Balthasar Fischer, Valentin Steiner; Marbling: Martin Karl Keller; Joiner: Joseph Regele; master blacksmith: Johann Georg Birbaum; Bell founder: Adam Wieland; Glazier: Jakob Peziak
history:
In 1760, the Bishop of Vác, Count Károly Esterházy, asked Franz Anton Pilgram to design the new Vác Cathedral. The finished plans were for an extensive Baroque building complex, but in 1761 Esterházy was summoned to Eger to serve as Bishop there and his successor, Archbishop of Vienna Christoph Anton Migazzi, continued with the construction but requested new plans. The new designer was Isidore Ganneval from France (a student of Niccolò Servandoni) and he introduced Neo-Classicism to Migazzi's court. This style was composed of classical elements and simple geometric shapes, which at the time was a novelty in Central Europe. As construction had already begun according to Pilgram's designs, Ganneval incorporated the walls of the sanctuary into his own design.  
The dome over the central building is decorated with a fresco, the *Triumph of the Holy Trinity* by Franz Anton Maulbertsch, painted between 1770 and 1771. The main altarpiece painting, the *Visitation*, was also by Maulbertsch, but at Migazzi's request it was over-painted with a *Crucifixion* by Kremserschmidt; Maulbertsch's painting was only uncovered during renovation in 1942. By 1777, construction was complete with the clock-tower erected by 1792.

Schmidt, Kremserschmidt, Georg Feigel, Balthasar Fischer, Valentin Steiner, Martin Karl Keller, Joseph Regele, Johann Georg Birbaum, Adam Wieland, Jakob Peziak, Count Károly Esterházy, Christop Anton Migazzi, Vác

ar.name: صفحة من القرآن.
description:
كُتِب القرآن على جلد غزال بخط كوفي مذهَّب وإطار بني داكن من حبر السبيدج. يُرى على الصفحة الآية 3 من سورة الإخلاص (رقم 112) والآية 1 من سورة الفلق (رقم 113). دوِّنت الآيتان في قالب ذهبي غني مؤطَّر وموشَّى بحبر بني داكن. لا توجد علامات ترقين، وتظهر علامات التشكيل بصورة نقاط حمر أو سود. الدليل الوحيد على بداية سورة جديدة هو البسملة (الصيغة "بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم"). تنتهي كل آية بثلاثة خطوط مائلة.  
  
تمَّ تأطير صفحات القرآن بحواشٍ عريضة مرسومة بخطوط دقيقة. أما المستطيلات التي صاغتها خطوط الحواشي فتشكِّل أقساماً مترابطة، يملأ فراغاتها الواسعة زخارف على شكل أجزاء لولبية رفيعة من نباتات معترشة ذات أوراق وأزهار. لم يبقَ سوى خمس صفحات من هذا القرآن الذي أنجز في القرن 3- 4 / 9- 10 في العراق أو سورية. لا بدَّ أنه أنجز لصالح مسجد مهم أو حاكم ذي شأن، نظراً لأنه كتب بخط كوفي مذهَّب غني بالزخارف.
تطوَّر فن الخطّ نتيجة النسخ المُتقن للقرآن الشريف، لجعله في متناول الجماهير. هذه الصفحة مكتوبة بالخطّ الكوفي المنسوب إلى مركز الخطّ بمدينة الكوفة، وهو بسيطٌ وفجٌّ، ولكنه جذّاب.
keywords: جلد؛ ذهب؛ رق؛ زخرفة زهرية؛ طلاء بالذهب؛ قطعة دينية.
materials: جلد غزال مطلي بالذهب، كُتب عليه بالحبر البني الداكن (حبر السبيدج).

en.name: Page from a Qur’an.
description:
This Qur'an was written in gilt *kufic* script outlined in brown ink (sepia) on gazelle skin. The verses on the page shown (112: 3– 113: 1) are set in a richly illuminated frame, also gilded and outlined in brown ink. There are no diacritical marks. Vowel marks are shown as red or black dots. The beginning of a new chapter (*sura*) is only indicated by the *basmala* (the formula: 'In the Name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful'). Three diagonal lines are placed at the end of the verses.  
  
The Qur'an page is framed by a wide border delineated by narrow bands. The rectangles formed by the border bands form joining sections. The large spaces within these rectangles are filled with decoration including spiralling tendrils with leaves and flowers.  
  
Only five leaves remain to us from this Qur'an, which was made in the AH 3rd–4th / AD 9th–10th centuries in or . Written in *kufic* script, gilded and richly illuminated, it must have been made for an important mosque or ruler.

Calligraphy developed as a result of careful copying of the Holy Qur'an in order to make it accessible to the masses. This page is written in *kufic* script, named after the calligraphic centre in the city of Kufa, and its character is plain and rigid yet striking.
holder: Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts.
keywords: Floral decoration; gold (gilding); leather; parchment; religious object; religious manuscript
materials: Gazelle skin with gilding, the writing in brown ink (sepia).
tags: Gazelle skin with gilding, the writing in brown ink (sepia).
partner: Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts

es.name: Página de Corán.
description:
Este Corán fue escrito en caracteres cúficos dorados y perfilados con tinta marrón (sepia) sobre piel de gacela. Los versículos de la página mostrada (sura 112, aleya 3; sura 113, aleya 1) se encuentran en el interior de un marco con exquisitas ilustraciones, también dorado y perfilado con tinta marrón. No hay marcas diacríticas. Las vocales están señaladas con puntos rojos o negros. Lo único que indica el comienzo de una sura es la presencia del *basmala* (la fórmula “en el nombre de Dios, el clemente, el misericordioso”). Al final de los versículos se aprecian tres líneas diagonales.  
La página está enmarcada en un borde ancho delimitado por finas bandas que forman rectángulos que se unen en algunos puntos. Dentro de ellos quedan amplios espacios adornados con zarcillos espirales con hojas y flores.  
Sólo se conservan cinco páginas de este Corán, que fue copiado en el siglo III O IV \[IX-X D. C.\] en Irak o Siria. A juzgar por los caracteres cúficos, el dorado y las exquisitas ilustraciones que presenta, debió de hacerse para una importante mezquita o para un gobernante.

La caligrafía se desarrolló a partir de la realización de cuidadosas copias del Sagrado Corán para acercarlo a las masas. Página escrita en letra cúfica, denominada así por los centros caligráficos de la ciudad de Kufa. Se caracteriza por ser plana y rígida, aunque llamativa.
holder: Museo de Arte Turco e Islámico.
dates: Siglos III-IV de la Hégira / IX-X d. C.
keywords: Decoración floral; oro (dorado); cuero (pergamino); objetos religiosos.
materials: Piel de gacela con pintura dorada y escritura en tinta sepia.
tags: Piel de gacela con pintura dorada y escritura en tinta sepia.
partner: Museo de Artes Turcas e Islámicas

fr.name: Page de coran.
description:
Ce coran a été copié sur peau de gazelle en style coufique à l'encre brune (sépia) et orné d'enluminures. Les versets de cette page (sourate XCII, verset 3 et sourate XCIII, verset 1) sont reproduits à l'intérieur d'un cadre richement enluminé délimité par d'étroits bandeaux à l'encre brune et à la dorure formant des rectangles jointifs. Le champ intérieur de cette importante bordure est occupé par un abondant décor de vrilles spiralées, de feuilles et de fleurs. Il n'y a pas de marques de voyelles et les signes diacritiques sont des points rouges ou noirs. Le début d'un nouveau chapitre (sourate) est simplement indiqué par la *basmala* (la formule “Au nom de Dieu, le Clément, le Miséricordieux”). La fin des versets est marquée par des lignes en diagonale.  
Seul cinq folios de ce coran réalisé au IIIe-IVe siècle H (IXe-Xe siècle J.-C.) en Irak ou en Syrie nous sont parvenus. Manuscrit en coufique, doré et richement enluminé, il a certainement été réalisé pour une mosquée importante ou pour un souverain.

Le développement de la calligraphie s’explique par la copie minutieuse du saint Coran afin de le rendre accessible à tous. Cette page est rédigée en écriture coufique, qui doit son nom aux ateliers de calligraphie de la ville de Koufa, et son aspect simple et strict n’en est pas moins remarquable.
holder: Musée des arts turcs et islamiques.
dates: IIIe-IVe siècle de l’Hégire (IXe-Xe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: objets religieux ; cuir (parchemin) ; or (dorure) ; décoration florale
materials: Peau de gazelle, dorure, écriture à l’encre sépia.
tags: Peau de gazelle, dorure, écriture à l’encre sépia.
partner: Musée des arts turques et islamiques

tr.name: Kur’an-ı Kerim Sayfası.
description:
Ceylan derisi üzerine kahverengi (*sepia*) ile tahrirli altın yaldız ve kufi hat ile yazılmıştır. Yine altın yaldız ve kahverengi mürekkep ile yapılmış çok zengin bir tezhibin çerçevelediği sayfada Kur'an'dan CXII: 3- CXIII: 1 ayetleri yazılmıştır. Harf noktaları yoktur. Harekeler kırmızı ve siyah noktalar şeklinde kullanılmıştır. Yeni bir surenin başlaması sadece besmele ile belirtilmiştir. Ayet sonuna diyagonal üç çizgi konmuştur.  
  
Kur'an sayfasını, dört ince banttan oluşan geniş bir bordür çevreler. Bordürdeki bantlar, oluşturdukları dikdörtgenin kenar ortalarında geçmeler yapar. Bantların oluşturduğu çerçevenin geniş boşluğunda kıvrım dallar ve bu dallara bağlı yaprak ve çiçeklerden oluşan süsleme vardır.  
  
9.-10. yüzyıllarda Irak veya Suriye'de yazılmış olan Kur'an'ın bugün elimizde sadece beş sayfası bulunmaktadır: ŞE 43/1-5. Altın yaldız ve kufi hat ile yazılmış, çok zengin bir süslemeye sahip olan bu Kur'an, mutlaka önemli bir cami veya sultan için yazılmış olmalıdır.  
  
Emevi ve Abbasi dönemleri, İslamiyet'in genişleyip yayıldığı, İslam sanatının ise yavaş yavaş karakterini bulmaya çalıştığı bir dönemdir. Bu nedenle de Abbasi dönemi sanatçıları yaratıcı olmaktan çok derleyici izlenimlerle ürünler vermişlerdir. Roma ve Bizans dönemi ürünlerinde kullanılan motif ve desenleri, kitap sanatlarına uyacak ve yakışacak bir sentezden geçirerek uygulamışlardır. Sonuç olarak da tüm kitap süslemelerinde günümüze dek kullanılacak, ancak zaman ve yöresel etkilerle gelişip zenginleşecek olan ana temaları saptamışlardır.

Hat sanatı, Kur'an'ların doğru ve eksiksiz olarak kitlelere ulaşabilmesi için özenle yazılmaları sonucunda gelişmiştir. Kufe şehrindeki yazım merkezlerinden dolayı bu şehrin adını alan Kur'an sayfasındaki Kufi hat, sade, sert ancak çok çarpıcı bir karaktere sahiptir.
keywords: Dini objeler; Deri (parşömen); Altın (yaldız); Bitkisel bezeme
materials: Ceylan derisi üzerine altın yaldız, kahverengi (sepia) mürekkep kullanılarak yazılmıştır.
tags: Ceylan derisi üzerine altın yaldız, kahverengi (sepia) mürekkep kullanılarak yazılmıştır.

en.name: Lamego Museum
description:
"The Museum holds a number of important collections, though only those related to the Manueline era of the Maritime Discoveries are discussed here.  
Some of the most interesting items are the early 16th-century wool and silk tapestries, made in workshops in Brussels that used to hang in the Episcopal Palace. Excellently drawn, they are based on mythological themes: *The Temple of Leto*, *Laius consulting the Oracle*, *Oedipus in Corinth*, *Oedipus in Thebes*, and *Oedipus and Queen Jocasta*, and there is another, perhaps the most spectacular of all, an *Allegory to Music*. The syncretism between classical culture, Paganism and the new humanistic vision of the Catholic Church is evident.  
Five panels by Vasco Fernandes, or Grão Vasco, represent outstanding works in the painting collection in this Museum. The five panels that once belonged to the retable in the chancel of Lamego Cathedral were commissioned by Bishop D. João Carmelo de Madureira in 1506, and were completed in 1511. They reveal some fundamental elements towards an understanding of Vasco’s art and his creative process, in the initial phase of his long career.  
From these five remaining panels, it is not difficult to imagine the sumptuousness of the original retable, which was made up of 20 panels, two of which, along with a sculpture that has since disappeared, occupied the central axis and which were, therefore, larger in size.  
Fernandes’s essential concern with formal harmony and representative rigour are to be noted in the spatial organisation of the compositions, where his use of light to focus on intermediate planes is masterly. An example of this is to be seen in the flooring in the *Annunciation* and the strategic positioning of the stove as a source of light. Also impressive is the balanced distribution of colour and the way in which the figures are wrapped in full drapery and modelled with remarkable plasticity.  
Flemish Realism can also be identified by the form, in the way in which the texture of the fabrics is represented, by the transparency of glass and in the reflections on the surface of metal objects. Recourse to various inspirational sources can be identified by elements such as the Nordic detail of the background landscape with architecture in *The Visitation*, while he opts for the mythical unicorn in *The Creation of Animals*.  
To confirm the importance that painting had at this time as a means of personal and social promotion, the figure holding the child Jesus in the *Circumcision* corresponds to the portrait of the Bishop who commissioned this work. His coat of arms is also included, at his express wish, in the carved structure of the retable."

en.name: Goblet with cover
description:
With the exception of a few square centimetres, the surface of this covered goblet is engraved and polished. On the front side, a small relief bust made of biscuit porcelain is glazed into an oval panel, i.e., covered by glass on both sides. It depicts a profile portrait of King Ludwig I of Bavaria, who held the throne from 1825 to 1848. A silver crown thaler from 1828 may have served as a model for the portrait; a small beard on the lower lip, which is typical for depictions of Ludwig I, is visible on the relief.  
  
In the first half of the 19th century, the Harrach glassworks in Neuwelt, on the Bohemian side of the Krkonoše Mountains, was one of the leading companies in this important glassworks region. It was praised for having produced the finest glassware with glazed inserts around 1830. The porcelain reliefs, like the one on this goblet, were ordered from elsewhere.  
  
The production of portraits of Ludwig for the period from 1830 to 1833 has been proven. Pieces with this kind of decoration were considered luxury objects and probably used exclusively for representational purposes.
keywords: Glass; biscuit porcelain; Harrach; Neuwelt; King Ludwig I of Bavaria; portrait
materials: Colourless glass, biscuit porcelain; footed, engraved and polished

ar.name: قصر بيير الأول، دير سانتا كلارا الحالي.
description:
يشكل قصر ودير أستوديلو أحسن تعبير عن الوحدة بين المَلَكية الإسبانية والدين. يتعلق الأمر بمجموعتين تحددان اشتغال البلاط وهما قصر بيير الأول ومنزل ماريا دي باديلا.  
يتم الولوج إلى الأول عبر باب ذي ساكف من الحجارة المنجورة الذي يذكِّر من حيث الشكل، بالرغم من كونه أكثر بساطة، بحجارة طورديسياس. يُشاهَد فوقه فضاءٌ مستطيل يضم عقداً عاتقاً مبنياً من الآجر، مما أدى إلى النقص من قيمة باب الدخول هذا، مقارنة مع باب القصر. في الواقع، من المحتمل أن تكون التعديلات اللاحقة هي التي غيرت المدخل بهذا الشكل، إلا إذا بقي دون إتمام. جرت تعلية المستوى الثاني بعقد توأم ومفصص من الآجر، مع ألفيز وأعمدة من الحجارة، مما يجعل منه مجموعة في غاية التناسق مقارنة مع غائيته البلاطية.  
تؤدي الكنة إلى بهو وتسمح بالتواصل مع أحد أطراف القاعة الرئيسية والصحن، مروراً تحت عقد منكسر من الآجر مُحَوَّطٍ داخل ألفيز؛ ولازالت هذه القاعة تحتفظ ببعض الأفاريز من الجبس المنحوت، والمرممة من طرف الطائفة الدينية. أما صنعة الجصاص، برايمي، الذي كان صاحب هذا العمل الزخرفي، فتبقى جد مُوثقة. وفي وسط الجانب الأطول، تنفتح القاعة الرئيسية، ذات التصميم المستطيل المنتظم في مستويين، على صحن كان يؤدي إلى جناح آخر ذي مميزات مماثلة. كما أن البوابة التي تفضي إلى الصحن وتنتهي على شكل عقد كامل الاستدارة محاطٍ بألفيز وثلاث فتحات علوية، كانت مزودة في الأصل بشماسيات. تنفتح القاعة العلوية على الصحن عبر فتحة توأم متجاوزة مع عمود أوسط.  
جرى تعديل هذه الفضاءات إلى متحف صغير حيث يتم عرض القطع الجصية المنقوشة والأخشاب المدهونة التي تم الحصول عليها من مختلف أجزاء القصر – الدير، ومن السقوف. وفي القاعة السفلية، جرى الحفاظ على سقف خشبي، بالغ الأهمية، مستوٍ ومدعَّم بعوارض، ومكوَّنٍ من معينات ومستطيلات منقوشة ومتعددة الألوان.  
يمثل "منزل دونا ماري دي باديلا" نوع المسكن المدجن لقشتالة وليون: صحن مكون من مستويين، المستوى السفلي له سواران من الحجارة، والمستوى العلوي ذو حاجز مفرغ وبنية من الخشب؛ وحوله، كانت الغرف مثل " القاعة الملكية" موزعة ومنتظمة في تخطيط مستطيل. لكن العناصر الأكثر أهمية تتواجد، دون أدنى شك، في إطارات الأبواب المزخرفة بالجص المنقوش؛ حيث يُبرز واحد منها في الطابق الأرضي عقداً مفصصاً مع بنيات صغيرة مسننة، وألفيزاً مكوناً بواسطة شريطين متشابكين ومعقودين فوق مفتاح العقد، وفقاً لنمط التقاليد الموحدية. زُخرفت الركنيات بشعارات على أرضيات نباتية، وهي مخطط مدجن نموذجي منذ بداية القرن الرابع عشر، وفي الأعلى ثمة ساكف ذو فقرات على شاكلة واجهة قصر طورديسياس، حيث زُينت الجوانب هنا بشبكة من مثمنات الأضلاع المجدولة، المحفورة مباشرة على الجص، وهي تقنية منحدرة من العقد النصري. كما تعكس شرائط الألفيز تأثيراً إسلامياً بزخارفها الكتابية النسخية التي تكرر الشعار المعروف: "الغبطة واليمن".

شُيد هذا القصر من قبل بيير الأول من أجل العيش مع عشيقته مارية دي باديلا. وكما هو الشأن بقصور طورديسيلاس وقصر إشبيلية، فإن الفضاءات الداخلية والواجهات كانت مزينة وفق الطراز المدجن. وفي الداخل، كان الخشب المتعدد الألوان والجصيات تزخرف الأسقف والعقود. ومن الخارج، تتزاوج الحجارة والآجر من أجل خلق واجهة فاخرة بشكل استثنائي خلال تلك الفترة.

en.name: Palace of Pedro I, now the Convent of Santa Clara.
names: Palace of Pedro I, now the Convent of Santa Clara
description:
The palace and convent in Astudillo represent the best expression of the union between the Spanish crown and religion. The two structures, the palace of Pedro I and the house of Maria de Padilla, epitomise the court system.  
The first is entered through a lintelled doorway with ashlars cut in an undulating pattern formally reminiscent of that in Tordesillas Palace, if somewhat simpler. Above this there is a rectangular space with a relieving arch made of brick, which has been used to suggest that this gateway is inferior to the gateway of the palace mentioned above. However, it seems more likely that it was modified by alterations made later, or that it was never completed. The second level, topped with a twin-lobed arch in brick with an *alfiz* panel and resting on stone columns, make up the structure, which is entirely in keeping with its palatial setting.  
The gateway gives access to the entrance hall, one end of the main room and the courtyard via a pointed brick arch with an *alfiz* panel. This room has retained some plaster friezes that have been restored by the religious community. There is documentary evidence of the work carried out by the plasterer Braymi, who must have been the craftsman responsible for this ornamental work. The twin-level rectangular main room opens out from the middle of its longer side into a courtyard, which may have led to another wing of similar size. The gateway leading to the courtyard is finished with a semi-circular arch framed with an *alfiz* panel and three upper openings, originally containing lattice windows. The upper room opens onto the courtyard through a twin horseshoe aperture with a central column. These areas have been converted into a small museum exhibiting plasterwork from different parts of the palace convent and painted wood from the ceilings. An interesting *alfarje* ceiling with carved and coloured hexagonal tiles has survived in the lower room.  
The House of Doña Maria de Padilla is a typical Mudejar residence from Castile and León: a courtyard with two levels, the lower with stone pillars and the upper made of wood with a handrail. The rooms were situated around it and were all typically rectangular, including the Royal Room. The most interesting parts are two door frames with plasterwork decoration. One of them, on the lower floor, has a lobed arch with small notched structures and an *alfiz* panel made up of two crossed ribbons tied on the keystone, in the Almohad style. Coats of arms on a vegetal background, a typical Mudejar motif from the mid-14th century, decorate the spandrels below a voussoired lintel, similar to the one on the front of the Tordesillas Palace. Unlike this latter, there is a network of intertwined octagons to the sides, carved directly into the stucco, a technique that links them to Nasrid art. There is an Islamic influence in the narrow *alfiz* panels with cursive inscriptions that repeat the well-known blessing 'happiness and prosperity'.

This palace was built by Pedro I to live in with his lover María de Padilla. As in the palaces in Tordesillas and the Seville Citadel, the interiors and façade were decorated in the Mudéjar style. Interior ceilings and arches were decorated with multicoloured wood and plasterwork. On the outside, stone and brick were combined to create a façade that was exceptionally luxurious for its time.
artist: Mudéjar plasterer Braymi (main room of the palace).
keywords: Palace of Pedro I; Astudillo; Palencia; Mudéjar; Pedro I; Maria de Padilla; lintelled doorway; undulating ashlars; lobed arch; twin arch; alfarje ceiling; hexagonal tile
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate General of Fine Arts

es.name: Palacio de Pedro I, actual convento de Santa Clara.
names: Palacio de Pedro I, actual convento de Santa Clara
description:
El palacio y el convento de Astudillo constituyen la mejor expresión de unión entre monarquía española y religión.Se trata de dos conjuntos que definen el funcionamiento cortesano: el palacio de Pedro I y la casa de María de Padilla.  
  
Al primero se accede por una puerta adintelada, con despiece de sillares ondulados, que recuerda formalmente la de Tordesillas, si bien es más sencilla. Sobre ella apea un espacio rectangularen que destaca un arco de descarga construido en ladrillo. Aunque se ha aludido a este elemento para infravalorar la portada con respecto a la del palacio citado, parece más bien que fueron las remodelaciones posteriores las que la modificaron, o quizá no llegó a concluirse. El segundo nivel, rematado con arco geminado lobulado de ladrillo, con alfiz y sobre columnas de piedra, conforma un conjunto sumamente coherente con su destino palaciego.  
  
La portada da paso al zaguán y permite la comunicación con un extremo de la sala principal y con el patio a través de un arco apuntado de ladrillo con alfiz. En esta cámara se conservan algunos frisos de yeserías restaurados por la comunidad religiosa. Está documentado el trabajo del yesero Braymi, que debió de ser el artífice de esta labor ornamental. La sala principal, de planta rectangular con dos alturas, se abre en el centro de su lado mayor a un patio, que tal vez enfrentaría otro pabellón de similares características. La portada que da al patio se resuelve con arco de medio punto recuadrado con alfiz y tres vanos superiores, originalmente con celosías. La cámara superior se abre al patio con vano geminado de herradura sobre columna central. Estos espacios han sido convertidos en un pequeño museo, donde se exhiben yeserías de distintas partes del palacio-convento y maderas pintadas procedentes de cubiertas. En la sala baja se conserva un interesante alfarje con alfardones tallados y policromados.  
  
La denominada “casa de Doña María de Padilla” responde al tipo de vivienda mudéjar de Castilla y León: patio de dos pisos, el inferior con pilares de piedra y el superior con barandal y estructura de madera. Alrededor se disponían las habitaciones, que, como la denominada Sala Real, tendrían la habitual planta rectangular. Lo más interesante son dos encuadramientos de puertas, con decoración de yeserías. Uno, en el piso bajo, tiene arco lobulado con pequeñas estructuras dentadas y alfiz formado por dos cintas cruzadas anudadas en la clave, según fórmulas almohades. En las enjutas campean escudos sobre fondo vegetal, esquema típico del mudéjar desde mediados del siglo XIV, y encima un dintel adovelado, como en la fachada del palacio de Tordesillas. A diferencia de ésta, en los laterales se observa una red de octógonos entrelazados, dibujados por simple incisión sobre el estuco, técnica que los vincula con el arte nazarí. Influencia islámica tienen las estrechas bandas de alfiz con inscripciones cursivas que repiten la consabida eulogia “Felicidad y prosperidad”.

Este palacio fue construido por Pedro I para vivir en él con su amante, María de Padilla. Al igual que en los palacios de Tordesillas y del Alcázar de Sevilla, los interiores y la fachada se decoraron en estilo mudéjar. En el interior, la madera policromada y el yeso ornamentaban techos y arcos. En el exterior, la piedra y el ladrillo se conjugaron para crear una fachada excepcionalmente lujosa para su época.
artist: Yesero mudéjar Braymi (sala principal del palacio).

partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate General of Fine Arts

fr.name: Palais de Pierre Ier, actuel couvent de Santa Clara.
description:
Le palais et le couvent d'Astudillo constituent la meilleure expression de l'union entre la monarchie espagnole et la religion. Il s'agit de deux ensembles qui définissent le fonctionnement de la cour : le palais de Pierre Ier et la maison de María de Padilla.  
On accède au premier par une porte à linteau en pierre de taille à refend qui rappelle formellement celle de Tordesillas, même si elle est plus simple. Au-dessus se voit un espace rectangulaire avec un arc de décharge construit en briques, ce qui a contribué à dévaloriser cette porte d'entrée par rapport à celle du palais en question. En fait, ce sont plus vraisemblablement les transformations ultérieures qui l'ont modifiée de la sorte, à moins qu'elle ne soit demeurée inachevée. Le second niveau, surmonté par un arc géminé et lobé en briques, avec un *alfiz* et des colonnes de pierre, en fait un ensemble extrêmement cohérent par rapport à sa finalité palatine.  
Le porche introduit à un vestibule et permet de communiquer avec l'une des extrémités de la salle principale et le patio en passant sous un arc brisé en briques inscrit dans un *alfiz*. Cette pièce conserve encore quelques frises en stucs, restaurées par la communauté religieuse. Le travail du stucateur Braymi, qui dut être l'auteur de ce travail ornemental, est bien documenté. Au milieu du côté le plus long, la salle principale, de plan rectangulaire à deux niveaux, ouvre sur un patio qui devait conduire à une autre aile aux caractéristiques similaires. Le portail qui donne sur le patio se termine en arc plein cintre à *alfiz* et trois baies supérieures, à l'origine dotées de jalousies. La pièce supérieure s'ouvre sur le patio par une baie géminée outrepassée avec colonne centrale. Ces espaces ont été transformés en un petit musée où l'on expose des stucs provenant de diverses parties du palais-couvent et des bois peints provenant des plafonds. Dans la salle basse, on conserve un intéressant plafond en *alfarje* à base de losanges et de rectangles sculptés et polychromés.  
La “maison de Doña María de Padilla” répond au type de demeure mudéjare de Castille et de León : patio à deux niveaux, le niveau inférieur à piliers de pierre et le niveau supérieur à balustrade et structure en bois. Autour étaient distribuées les pièces qui, telle la “Salle Royale”, devaient être rectangulaires. Le plus intéressant se trouve sans aucun doute dans les encadrements des portes, décorés de stucs. L'un de ces encadrements, au rez-de-chaussée, présente un arc lobé avec de petites structures dentelées et un *alfiz* formé par deux rubans croisés et noués sur la clé de l'arc, selon des formules almohades. Les écoinçons sont décorés d'écussons sur fond végétal, schéma typiquement mudéjar depuis le début du XIVe siècle, et au-dessus, un linteau à claveaux comme dans la façade du palais de Tordesillas – à ceci près qu'ici les côtés sont rehaussés d'un réseau d'octogones entrelacés, incisés directement sur le stuc, technique issue de l'arc nasride. Les étroites bandes d'*alfiz* ont une influence islamique avec leurs inscriptions cursives qui répètent la devise bien connue : “Félicité et prospérité”.

Ce palais fut construit par Pierre Ier pour y vivre avec sa maîtresse, María de Padilla. De même que les palais de Tordesillas et de l'alcazar de Séville, les intérieurs et la façade étaient décorés en style mudéjar. À l'intérieur, le bois polychromé et le stuc ornaient les plafonds et les arcs. À l'extérieur, la pierre et la brique se conjuguaient pour créer une façade exceptionnellement luxueuse pour l'époque.
artist: Stucateur mudéjar : Braymi (salle principale du palais).

en.name: *Puppenfiguren aus Volksmärchen (Puppets from Folk Tales)*
description:
The oblong tapestry shows in its central part a number of characters as they appear in common German fairy tales, the most well-known story collection being Grimm’s *Children’s and Household Tales*. The figures are sewn onto the ground in a patchwork, using fabric of many different colours and patterns. The darker coloured fields above and beneath the figures show flowers and birds.  
The artwork was created by an artist and acquired for the state by the Sekretariat für Kunstausstellungen des Bezirkes Dresden \[Dresden secretary for Fine Art Exhibitions\] in 1980. This was standard procedure in the German Democratic Republic (GDR) since even art production was scheduled in the socialist economy plan and the government took seriously its role as the main supporter of the country’s artists. Government-owned artworks were considered public property and as such were installed in public places for everybody to see. This was the case for the tapestry discussed here, which furnished a kindergarten during the 1980s. One can imagine that the children might have guessed the figure’s names and the corresponding fairy tales. Furthermore, the figures resemble the typical hand puppets from the GDR, which could have been a prop in retelling the figures’ stories.  
The artist Agathe Böttcher was born in Bautzen in 1929. She studied textile design beginning in 1947 in Dresden and later on in Berlin-Weissensee (post-graduate study from 1954–57). In 1954, she married the painter and film maker Jürgen Böttcher (Strawalde). Through her husband, she became acquainted with artists of the Dresden artist group *Erste Phalanx Nedserd*. In 1958 she took up a job as lecturer at the Technical University of Dresden, which she held more than 20 years. Since 1979, she has been working as a freelance artist with temporary lectureships. Agathe Böttcher lives in Dresden (2017).
keywords: figurative decoration; wall hanging; GDR; Dresden; human figure

partner: Dresden State Art Collections, Kunstfonds (Art Fund)

en.name: Dragon Rug
description: This 18th century Dragon Rug is a unique expression of artistic achievement. This is the only known Dragon carpet that is woven in the Persian style of *Sehna* knotting. It was made by what is assumed to be a migratory craftsman. This assumption stems from the fact that the last 12 inches of the carpet were woven in the opposite direction than the rest, suggesting that it was taken off the loom before completion and then placed back on later. It features the standard dragon carpet layout with decadent patterns of symmetrical floral and leaf motifs. The frame consists of an interlaced pattern, while the field of the carpet includes dragon, animal, and floral motifs.
keywords: Carpet; Rug
