en.name: Mosque lamp
description: This mosque lamp belongs to a well-established group of glass lamps probably made for the Mamluk Sultan (al-Nasir Nasir al-Din) Hasan (AH 734-763/ AD 1334-1361). An unusual feature of this lamp is the panel of stylised pseudo-Kufic script alternating with *thuluth* inscriptions and reads: “What was made for his Excellency, the Elevated, the Servant of the Lord, the Great Amir, the Possessor”; around the body and its underside are six repeating inscriptions of "The Learned"
keywords: Lamp; Calligraphy; Glass; Mosque; Mamluk; Egypt
materials: Glass, Enamel, Gold; Gilding, Enameling, Blown-glass, Applying

ar.name: قارورة زجاجية.
description:
القطعة عبارة عن قارورة زجاجية ذات قاعدة مقعرة وعنق صغير مزين بنموذج زخرفي متداخل الألوان يتكون من أشكال ملتفة على القارورة صُنعت بتمرير أداة تشبه المشط على سطح القارورة. يظهر نفس هذا النموذج على كل بدن الزجاجة باللونين البنفسجي الغامق والأبيض.  
  
كان هذا الأسلوب شائعاً في زخرفة الأواني الزجاجية في مصر وسورية في الفترتين الأيوبية والمملوكية. وعُرف في فترات سابقة في سورية، وخاصة في الفترة الرومانية. استخدم في صناعة مثل هذه القوارير تقنية النفخ والتمشيط، حيث تلف الخيوط الزجاجية الملونة حول الزجاج المنفوخ الساخن، وهو عادة من اللون الأخضر أو الأزرق أو البنفسجي الشفاف، وتمشط لتشكل مجموعة من الحبال التزينية التي تثبت على سطح الزجاج بضغطها بواسطة عصاً من الحجر.

قارورة عطر زجاجية، من قلعة عجلون، بقالب رخامي تمَّ تحقيقه بسحب أداة شبيهة بالمشط، لإحداث الثقوب. غير أن هذا الأسلوب لم يصبح شائعاً في مصر، إلا خلال الحقبتين الأيوبية والمملوكية، على الرغم من أنه كان معتمداً في سورية، منذ الفترة الرومانية.
place: ربما تكون قد صُنعت في سورية.
keywords: آنية زجاجية؛ تمشيط الزجاج؛ خيوط زجاجية؛ زجاج مشكل بالنفخ؛ عطر؛ نفخ حرّ؛ زجاج منفوخ

en.name: Bottle or perfume sprinkler.
description:
A disk shaped bi-coloured bottle with a concave base and a small neck decorated with a marbling pattern achieved by dragging a comb-like tool that forms the loops. The same pattern in dark purple and white has been used all over the vessel.  
  
The 'combing' and blowing technique used on this vessel became popular in Egypt and Syria during the Ayyubid and Mamluk periods, but had been practiced in Syria since the Roman period. The marbling technique used here entailed winding opaque glass threads (usually green, blue or purple) around the blown bubble of glass while it was still hot. The threads were then pressed on to the surface by means of a stone rod and then combed to form a series of parallel festoons, or white trails, that were tooled into festoons or feather-like patterns.

A glass perfume bottle from Ajlun Castle, with a marbling pattern achieved by dragging a comb-like tool to form the loops. This technique became popular in Egypt during the Ayyubid and Mamluk periods, although it had been practised in Syria since the Roman period.
keywords: Marbling; perfume; blown glass

es.name: Botella o perfumador
description:
Botella bicolor en forma de disco, con base cóncava y cuello pequeño; está totalmente decorada con un veteado morado oscuro y blanco que se consiguió pasando un utensilio similar a un peine para producir las curvas.  
Las técnicas de soplado y “peinado” aplicadas en este recipiente fueron populares en Egipto y Siria durante los periodos ayyubí y mameluco, pero venían practicándose en Siria desde época romana. La técnica del veteado consiste en enrollar hilos de vidrio opaco (normalmente verdes, azules o morados) alrededor de la burbuja de cristal soplado cuando ésta está aún caliente. En este caso, los hilos se presionaron contra la superficie con un rodillo de piedra y después se peinaron para componer una serie de estelas blancas paralelas a las que se dio forma de festones o plumas.

Perfumero de cristal del castillo de Aylun, con un efecto veteado que se logró arrastrando un instrumento similar a un peine para producir as curvas. Esta técnica fue popular en Egipto durante los periodos ayyubí y mameluco, aunque se practicaba en Siria desde época romana.
dates: Siglo VII de la Hégira / XIII d. C.
place: Hallado en Aylun, quizá fuera fabricado en Siria.
keywords: Veteado; perfume; vidrio soplado

fr.name: Bouteille ou aspersoir à parfum.
description:
Bouteille en forme de disque bicolore à base concave et col de faible hauteur décoré d'un motif marbré obtenu grâce à un outil en peigne qui produit l'effet de boucle. Un même motif violet foncé et blanc décore la totalité de l'objet.  
Les techniques de “peignage” et de soufflage utilisées ici se répandirent en égypte et en Syrie pendant les périodes ayyoubide et mamelouke, mais étaient pratiquées en Syrie depuis les Romains. Cette technique de marbrage consistait à entourer de fils de verre opaque (généralement vert, bleu ou violet) la boule de verre soufflé encore chaude que l'on pressait ensuite sur la surface au moyen d'un rouleau de pierre puis que l'on “peignait” pour obtenir une succession de motifs parallèles de festons ou de plumes.

Bouteille à parfum en verre du château d’Ajloun, décorée d’un motif marbré obtenu grâce à un outil en peigne qui produit l’effet de boucles. Cette technique devint populaire en  Égypte pendant les périodes ayyoubide et mamelouke, bien qu’elle ait été pratiquée en Syrie  dès la période romaine.
dates: VIIe siècle de l’Hégire (XIIIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: parfum ; marbrure; verre soufflé

en.name: Jug with a monochrome yellow glaze and three handles
description:
Discovered in a house during the 1959 excavations in Murwab, northwest Qatar, this partially reconstructed jug must have had a striking and shiny appearance.  
  
It originally had three rounded handles on the shoulder, two of which are preserved, and is entirely covered with a monochrome yellow glaze. The small size of this jug and its decoration make it a delicate piece of tableware. It could have been a 'table vinegar jar' used to hold sweet and sour sauces that were very popular in the 9th century, as shown in ancient
dates: AH late 2nd to late 3rd century / AD late 8th to late 9th century
keywords: earthenware, storage, transportation, jar

en.name: Churchyard and doorway
description: The churchyard and stone doorway follow a precise architectural design, which is significant in the architectural context of this Church. By using an elegant Baroque design, the anonymous architect added a special status to a vernacular building.
partner: Institute for the Administration of Architectural and Archaeological Heritage -  IGESPAR

pt.name: Adro e Portal
description: O portal e o adro da igreja, em pedra, seguem um desenho arquitectural preciso significante no contexto desta igreja. Usando um elegante desenho barroco, o anónimo arquitecto adicionou um *status* especial a um edifício vernacular.

ar.name: بيت القهوة

en.name: Coffee-house
description: Traditionally, social life in the Islamic world revolved around the tea-house or coffee-house, where men would gather to drink tea and coffee, eat sweet pastries or savoury food, and to smoke flavoured tobacco in water pipes (*narghile* or *qalian*). There they would play board games, listen to music and poetry recitations or discuss current events. This scene of a Turkish coffee-house would originally have been part of an album of images.

ar.name: إبريق.
description:
عُرِف الخزف ذو البريق المعدني في مدينة الرقة في القرن 6 / 12 والنصف الأول من القرن 7 / 13. ويتميز هذا النوع من الخزف عن غيره من الأنواع باللون الذي اشتهر به وهو البني الغامق. القطعة تمثل هذا النوع من الخزف. وهي عبارة عن إبريق ذي قاعدة عمودية، وجذع كروي، ورقبة أسطوانية طويلة، وشفة منفرجة نحو الخارج. الإبريق مزوّد بمثعب أنبوبي طويل وعروة موازية للشفة تنعطف عمودياً نحو الجذع وتلتصق بطرفه.  
  
زيِّن الإبريق بالبريق المعدني البني من أعلى الشفة والمثعب والعروة والرقبة حتى أسفل البطن. معظم الزخرفة موضوعة بنطاقات متتالية بشكل أفقي، قوامها زخارف كتابية وشبه كتابية ونباتية وهندسية محوَّرة. التباين في حدّة اللون وعرض النطاق أيضاً يشكلان عنصراً زخرفياً. نفذت جميع الزخارف بالطلاء ذي البريق المعدني بلون بني فوق طبقة زجاجية خضراء فاتحة جداً وشفافة.

اشتُهرت منطقة الرقة، قبل غزو المغول لها، بإنتاجها الغني للفخار الأنيق ذي الجودة العالية، والمصقول، يُستنتج التشابه ما بين اللون البني لهذه القطعة، مع المواد البنية التي تستخدم في الصناعات نفسها، في الرقة، وبذلك تمَّ تصنيف وتحديد مكان الصنع.
keywords: إبريق؛ بريق معدني؛ خزف؛ الرقة؛ فخار.
materials: خزف مزين بطلاء ذي بريق معدني.
tags: خزف مزين بطلاء ذي بريق معدني.

en.name: Jug with spout.
description:
Earthenware ceramics with a dark-brown metallic lustre glaze were produced in the city of Raqqa during the AH 6th–first half of the 7th / AD 12th–first half of the 13th centuries. What distinguishes these ceramics from those made in other places and periods are the types of colours used, particularly distinctive is the dark-brown.  
This jug represents a ceramic of this type. It has a columnar base, a globe-shaped body and a long cylindrical neck with an outward flaying lip. It is outfitted with a long tubular spout and a handle that juts out parallel to the lip and which curves perpendicularly downward to attach at the periphery of the body.  
The jug is decorated with dark-brown lustre glaze from the top of the lip, spout, handle, and neck all the way down to the bulk of the globular body, applied in a series of horizontal bands portraying calligraphic, pseudo-calligraphic, stylised vegetal and geometric patterns. Contrasts in colour intensity and band width are also part of the decorative scheme. The transparent, dark-brown metallic lustre is covered with a layer of very light-green glaze.
The region of Raqqa was a prolific producer of fine-quality underglazed lustre ceramics just before the Mongol invasion. The brown colour of this lustre is typical of Raqqa-ware.
dates: Hegira 6th–first half of the 7th century / AD 12th–first half of the 13th century.
keywords: Earthenware; jug; metallic lustre; ceramic; Raqqa
materials: Earthenware decorated with metallic lustre glaze.
tags: Earthenware decorated with metallic lustre glaze.

es.name: Jarro con pitorro.
description:
En la región de al-Raqqa, a finales del siglo VI / XII y en la primera mitad del VII / XIII se producía cerámica de reflejo metálico en color marrón oscuro. Los colores, sobre todo el marrón, distinguen esta cerámica de la de otros lugares y periodos.  
Este jarro constituye un ejemplo de este tipo de cerámica. Está compuesto por un pie recto, un cuerpo globular, un cuello largo y cilíndrico, y una boca exvasada. Incorpora también un pitorro tubular largo y un asa que nace paralela a la boca y se curva perpendicularmente para unirse con la panza.  
El recipiente está decorado en reflejo metálico marrón oscuro en toda su superficie salvo la parte inferior de la panza y la base; la decoración está dispuesta en varias bandas horizontales con motivos caligráficos, pseudocaligráficos, vegetales y geométricos. También forma parte del esquema decorativo el contraste entre la intensidad del color y la anchura de las bandas. El reflejo metálico marrón oscuro translúcido está cubierto por una capa de vidriado verde muy claro.

En la región de al-Raqqa, justo antes de la invasión de los mongoles, se dio una prolífica producción de cerámica de reflejo metálico bajo vidriado de gran calidad. El color marrón de esta pieza es típico de Raqqa.
dates: Primera mitad del siglo VI–mediados del VII de la Hégira / primera mitad del XII–mediados del XIII d. C.
keywords: Barro cocido; jarra; reflejo metálico; cerámica; al-Raqqa.
materials: Barro cocido decorado en reflejo metálico.
tags: Barro cocido decorado en reflejo metálico.

fr.name: Jarre à bec.
description:
Des céramiques à décor lustré brun foncé furent produites dans la ville de Raqqa au cours du VIe siècle et de la première moitié du VIIe siècle de l'Hégire (XIIe siècle-première moitié du XIIIe siècle J.-C.). Les couleurs utilisées, et en particulier un brun foncé caractéristique, distinguent cette production de celle d'autres centres.  
Cette jarre appartient à ce type ; elle repose sur un piédouche en forme de colonne et possède une panse sphérique, un long col cylindrique à lèvre évasée, un long bec tubulaire et une poignée qui part de la lèvre, se recourbe et descend à la verticale vers la panse à laquelle elle se rattache.  
Elle est décorée au lustre brun foncé sur toute sa surface, sauf sur la partie basse de la panse et le piédouche. Le décor est appliqué en bandeaux horizontaux à motifs calligraphiques, pseudo-calligraphiques, géométriques et végétaux stylisés. Le contraste entre l'intensité des couleurs et la largeur des bandeaux participe à la composition. Le lustre brun foncé translucide est recouvert d'une glaçure d'un vert très léger.
Avant l'invasion mongole, la région de Raqqa fut un lieu de production prolifique de céramiques à décor de lustre sous glaçure. La couleur brune de ce lustre est typique de cette production.
dates: VIe siècle-première moitié du VIIe siècle de l'Hégire (XIIe siècle-première moitié du XIIIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: Terre cuite ; jarre ; décor lustré ; céramiques ; Raqqa

en.name: Qur'an
description: This manuscript is *juz’* (section) eleven of a thirty-part Qur’an. Each section was separately bound and each would have begun, as does this one, with an illuminated roundel known as a *shamsa* (‘sun’) containing a Qur’anic inscription. The first lines of text are surrounded by a frontispiece and, as is usual in all fine Qur’ans, the beginning of each chapter is indicated by an illuminated heading. Other sections of this same manuscript are now in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston and the Ethnography Museum in Ankara, Turkey.

en.name: Court Square (Piazza di Corte)
description:
After a long economic and social decline, Ariccia underwent a new golden age under the Chigi and was completely redesigned by Gian Lorenzo Bernini on behalf of Pope Alexander VII Chigi (1655–1667).  
  
Bernini worked in Ariccia between 1662 and 1673, assisted by Carlo Fontana, Mattia de Rossi, his younger brother Luigi Bernini, and Giovan Battista Contini. Not only did they build Chigi Palace, but they oversaw the redesign of Chigi Park, the city road system and the infrastructural network, as well as the restoration of the Complex of Saint Nicholas, of the Sanctuary of Galloro, and the construction of the Roman Gate. Moreover, they designed the Piazza di Corte (Court Square) which was to resemble a sumptuous and spectacular Baroque court. At the end of the work, Piazza di Corte hosted the complex of the Collegiate of the Assumption with the two lateral guest houses (Casini), the Chigi Stallions, two fountains with basins and the Neapolitan Gate. This makes Chigi Palace and the Court Square one of the most exceptional and unitary architectural complexes of Roman Baroque.  
  
The chronology of the restoration work in Piazza di Corte is very well-documented and precise: the Collegiate of the Assumption was built between spring 1662 and spring 1664. The construction of the two Casini, symmetrically placed on the two sides of the Church, Casino del Ministro (House of the Minister) and Casino del Governatore (House of the Governor), was carried out in the same period and at a rapid pace, since it would have hosted not only the families of senior officials, but offices for administration of justice and prisons as well. The two buildings are introduced by an elegant arcade of massive coupled columns, inspired by Michelangelo's arcades of the Campidoglio in Rome and connected to the church through a theatrical exedra behind the church itself.  
  
In 1664 the architects levelled the square and enriched it with decorative elements such as the two fountains in front of the Casini facades. By demolishing older buildings and using clever architecture to support the Piazza, Bernini managed to transform a steep surface into a plain square.  
  
In 1665 the renovation of the Fountain of the Three Spouts and the Stallions’ (the stables) construction began.  
  
The last monuments to be finished were Chigi Palace and the Neapolitan Gate, which were completed in August 1673 and remained the main access to the town until the Monumental Bridge was built in the 19th century. The Gate also offers a spectacular view of Vallericcia, the site of ancient Aricia.  
  
Near the Neapolitan Gate one can also see the Casino Stazi, which was transformed in the 19th century into the famous Martorelli Inn, and the 18th-century Antonini Palace with its facade framed by pilasters with impressions of ionic capitals, a smooth ashlar base and a trapezoidal three-arched portico housing the Fountain of the Three Sprouts.

it.name: Piazza di Corte
description:
Dopo una lunga decadenza economica e sociale, Ariccia fu completamente riprogettata da Gian Lorenzo Bernini su incarico di Alessandro VII Chigi (1655-1667).  
   
Bernini tra il 1662 e il 1673, coadiuvato da Carlo Fontana, Mattia de Rossi, Luigi Bernini, Giovan Battista Contini, non si limitò alla costruzione del Palazzo Chigi, ma si occupò della riprogettazione del Parco Chigi, della viabilità cittadina, della rete infrastrutturale, della sistemazione del Complesso di San Nicola, del Santuario di Galloro, della costruzione della Porta Romana e progettò la Piazza di Corte che assurse alla dignità di sfarzosa e scenografica corte barocca  
   
La spettacolare metamorfosi fu attuata con la costruzione del complesso della collegiata dell'Assunta con i due Casini laterali, degli “Stalloni” ex scuderie, delle due fontane a tazza e infine della Porta Napoletana. Il Palazzo Chigi con la frontistante Piazza di Corte costituisce ancora oggi uno dei più eccezionali ed unitari complessi architettonici del Barocco Romano.  
   
La cronologia delle sistemazioni nella Piazza di Corte è molto ben documentata e precisa: dalla primavera del 1662 alla primavera del 1664 fu realizzata la Chiesa collegiata dell'Assunta. L'edificazione dei Casini posti simmetricamente sui due lati della Chiesa, Casino del Ministro e Casino del Governatore, fu portata avanti contemporaneamente alla collegiata e a ritmi elevati, perché oltre ad ospitare la famiglia degli alti funzionari preposti, dovevano ospitare gli ambienti per l'amministrazione della giustizia e le prigioni. I due edifici sono fronteggiati da un elegante porticato scandito in ordine binato gigante, di notevole originalità, ispirato ai portici michelangioleschi del Campidoglio e si collegano alla chiesa attraverso una teatrale esedra che cinge in abbraccio l'edificio nella parte retrostante.  
   
Nel 1664 si procedette allo spianamento della piazza e alla sua sistemazione negli elementi di arredo con le due armoniose fontane a tazza poste in asse con le facciate dei Casini. Bernini mise in piano uno spazio scosceso, demolendo altri edifici e avvalendosi di cantinoni per sostenere la Piazza.  
   
Nel 1665 si iniziò la ristrutturazione della fontana delle tre cannelle e i lavori per le scuderie, gli Stalloni.  
   
L'ultimo cantiere posto in opera fu proprio il Palazzo Chigi e infine la Porta Napoletana consegnata nell'agosto del 1673 che costituì il principale accesso al paese fino alla costruzione ottocentesca del Ponte Monumentale. Dal piazzale adiacente la porta si gode una spettacolare panoramica su Vallericcia, sito dell'antica *Aricia*.  
   
Nei pressi della Porta Napoletana sorge anche il Casino Stazi, che nell'Ottocento fu trasformato nella celebre Locanda Martorelli ed il settecentesco Palazzo Antonini con facciata inquadrata da lesene con capitelli ionici compressi, basamento bugnato liscio e un porticato trapezoidale a tre fornici che ospita la Fontana delle Tre Cannelle.

en.name: Castle of Mount Bonifato
description:
Mount Bonifato with the tower of the homonymous castle, which still rises majestically with its height of 20 m., presented a truly excellent view over the city of Alcamo. It developed on the mountainside, over the entire gulf of Castellamare to the north, and the inland territories to the south, apart from being a place that was easily defensible. The perimetral masonry was made of stone hewn from the same rock on which it was founded. Apart from the surviving north-west tower, which must have been the keep, the remains of the other three square towers, sited in the south-west, north-east and north, emerge. At ground level the keep was divided by a transversal wall into two sections, of which the first could presumably have been a cistern, being accessible by a trap door and shown by residual fragments of ducts of clay for the adduction of rain water. Access to the first floor of the tower was from the outside, across a removable staircase, while a stone staircase built into the masonry permitted of access to the upper floors; these also being divided into two rooms by transversal walls. The bare architecture of the complex and the presence of the remains of a few homes and a chapel in the parade ground, along the south side of the walled city, lead to the belief that the castle had been inhabited and used as a fortified town. Although in origin it was used solely for military functions, refuge and defence, especially in the neighbouring conquered territories such as Segesta and Selinunte.  
Some local historians (De Blasi, 1880) maintained that this was the castle of the Saracen Captain ‘Abd Allah al-Qam, later called Alcamuk who, having disembarked at Lilibeo as the emissary of the Caliph of Egypt (11th century), provided Mount Bonifato with a defensive structure, which today is shown as the Castle of the Counts of Modica, situated in the residential area of Alcamo. Besides which, the act of concession shown to the Peralta family on the part of Pedro IV of the territory of Alcamo in 1337, cites the castle of Bonifato as already existing. Therefore, when in 1397 Gualtiero Ventimigla declared that he had built the castle of Bonifato at his own expense, this must have been a fortalice in ruins, and the intervention by Ventimiglia must have been limited to the restoration of an already existing building. The rediscovery of ceramics dating back to the 12th and 13th centuries in the dump under the south wall of the castle leads to the endorsement of the hypothesis of the Muslim foundation of the fortress.

es.name: Castillo de Monte Bonifato
description:
El monte Bonifato, con la torre del castillo homónimo que se yergue aún majestuosa con sus 20 m de altura, representaba una auténtica atalaya sobre la ciudad de Alcamo, crecida en sus laderas, sobre el golfo entero de Castellammare al norte y sobre los territorios del interior al sur, además de ser un lugar fácilmente defendible. El muro del perímetro estaba hecho con piedras de la propia roca sobre la que se alza. Además de la torre noroeste superviviente, que sería la torre maestra, afloran los restos de otras tres torres cuadradas, situadas en el suroeste, el noreste y el norte. En su planta baja, la torre maestra estaba dividida por un muro transversal en dos espacios, de los cuales el primero sería, presumiblemente, una cisterna a la que se entraba por una trampilla y en la que se ven restos de conductos de arcilla para recoger el agua de lluvia. El acceso al primer piso de la torre se hacía por el exterior, con una escala móvil, mientras que una escalera de piedra en el muro permitía subir a los pisos superiores, también divididos en dos salas por muros transversales. La arquitectura desnuda del conjunto, la presencia de restos de unas pocas viviendas y de una capilla en la plaza de armas, a lo largo del flanco meridional de la muralla, inducen a suponer que el Castillo, en origen con funciones exclusivamente militares de refugio y defensa, sobre todo de los cercanos territorios de conquista como Segesta y Selinunte, estuviera habitado y sirviera de burgo fortificado.  
Algunos historiadores locales (De Blasi, 1880) han sostenido que el Castillo que el capitán sarraceno ‘Abd Allah al-Qam, llamado después Alcamuk, desembarcado en Lilibeo como enviado del califa de Egipto (siglo XI), hizo construir sobre el monte Bonifato con varias obras de defensa, fuese el hoy identificado como Castillo de los Condes de Modica, situado en el centro habitado de Alcamo; por lo demás, el acta de concesión a la familia Peralta por parte de Pedro II del territorio de Alcamo, de 1337, cita como ya existente el Castillo de Bonifato. Por tanto, cuando en 1397 Gualtiero Ventimiglia declaraba haber edificado el Castillo de Bonifato a su costa, debía de ser un fortín en ruinas, y la intervención de los Ventimiglia se limitaría a la restauración de un edificio anterior. El hallazgo de cerámica de los siglos XII y XIII en el vertedero que hay bajo el muro sur del Castillo anima a avalar la hipótesis de la fundación musulmana de la fortaleza.

en.name: Précis Historique de la Traite des Noirs et de l'Esclavage Colonial
short_description: This illustration, taken from the Précis Historique de la Traite des Noirs et de l'Esclavage Colonial  had didactic objectives. It attempted to show the inhuman treatment slaves were subjected to (yoke, chains, whipping) by traders. In this image, a mother is begging King Charles X of France to spare her son this dark fate and abolish slavery. However, even though the National Convention did abolish slavery in 1794, Napoléon Bonaparte then reintroduced it to most of the territories under French control.
keywords: Slavery; Africa; France

fr.name: Précis historique de la traite des noirs et de l'esclavage colonial
short_description: Cette illustration tirée du *Précis historique de la traite des noirs et de l'esclavage colonial* a une visée « pédagogique ». Il s’agit de montrer les traitements inhumains infligés aux esclaves (joug, chaîne, coups de fouet…) par les « négriers ». Une mère implore le roi Charles (le roi français Charles X) afin que ce sort funeste soit épargné à son enfant, grâce à l’abolition de l’esclavage. En effet, si l’esclavage avait été aboli en 1794 par la Convention, Napoléon Bonaparte l’avait rétabli en 1802 dans la plupart des territoires sous domination française.
keywords: Esclavage; Afrique; France

en.name: *Khettaras*
description:
*Khettaras* are an old and clever way of bringing underground water to the surface without using machines or electricity. Found mostly in dry or semi-dry areas, they manage water sustainably. They work using gravity, so no energy is needed, making them perfect for desert regions. A *khettara* has a wellhead at the highest point, a gently sloping underground tunnel, and vertical shafts every 10 to 30 metres for ventilation and maintenance. Water flows naturally to the surface, entering irrigation canals, séguias, pools, or fountains, and is shared by communities according to traditional rules. Some *khettaras* are 10–15 kilometres long, showing the skill of their builders.  
Beyond their design, *khettaras* shaped life in Morocco’s deserts. They allowed oases to grow, influenced farming, settlement, and local governance. Control over them was linked to political power. Over centuries, these systems helped shape not just the land but the way of life in Morocco’s driest regions.
history:
*Khettaras* began in ancient Persia (modern-day Iran) as *qanats*, an underground tunnel system that taps into groundwater from an aquifer and carries it across long distances to the surface. As Muslim empires expanded, this technique spread to North Africa, especially Morocco, during the Islamic conquests. They became more common in the 11th century under the Almoravid dynasty. The first *khettaras* in Morocco were built in the central Haouz region near Marrakech, a politically and economically important area that needed water for farming and its residents.  
Khettaras brought water from underground aquifers to the fields without pumps. By 1987, over 650 existed in this region. Later, during the Saadian and Alaouite dynasties, *khettaras* spread further south, to oasis regions like Errachidia, Figuig, Tinghir, and Skoura, where they supported farming and palm trees.

en.name: Register listing 'all of the subjects of the Grand Duke of Tuscany [Italy] residing in Tunisia'
names: *Stato nominativo di tutti i Sudditi di Sua Altezza Reale il Gran Duca di Toscana residenti in Tunisi*
short_description:
The names appearing in this list are mostly Jewish, including that of Giacomo Castelnuovo (Livorno, Italy, 1819 – La Goulette, Tunisia, 1886), a medical doctor who had to flee Italy because of his liberal ideas and his support for Italy’s national unification. Initially he went to Egypt, where he founded two Italian newspapers, *Lo Spettatore Egiziano* and *Il Progresso d’Egitto*.  
The author of many medical publications, in Tunis Castelnuovo became the Bey’s personal physician. He served as president of the Tunisian branch of the Alliance Israélite Universelle, and promoted the construction of a synagogue, on a plot of land granted by the Bey.  
A Freemason, he fought in Italy in the wars for Italy’s unification. He was awarded honours by both the Italian King (who ennobled him) and by the Bey of Tunis.

ar.name: الطيفور (صحن مقعّر).
description:
طيفور ذو فوهة دائرية، وحواف مقلوبة للخارج مع جناح صغير أفقي. الجسم نصف كروي، والقاعدة محدبة، والساق حلقية عمودية. غُطِّي الخارج بطلاء مزجج يميل إلى الأبيض الشفاف تقريبا؛ وزُيِّن الداخل بطلاء مزجج متعدد الألوان يضم الأبيض والأخضر والبنفسجي والأصفر، وبأسلوب خاص في تصوير الأشكال. يتشكل الموضوع الزخرفي المركزي من مشهد صيد ديناميكي، يبدو فيه كلب صيد سلوقي وطائر (قد يكون صقراً أو نسراً) يهاجمان في وقت واحد غزالة. يحمل الطائر في فمه شيئاً له شكل حلزوني، يمكن أن يكون ثعباناً أو غصن شجرة. وتجري على الحافة القصيرة من الصحن أكاليل تتكون من أقواس صغيرة سوداء مملوءة بالطلاء المزجج الأخضر.  
  
في الفترة التي كان مستخدماً فيها، تم تصليح الصحن بمشابك. كما أننا نجد فيه ثقوباً في القاعدة تدفع إلى التفكير بأن الإناء ربما كان مخصصاً للتعليق على جدار. قطعة مرمّمة.

طبقٌ يمثل مشهدَ صيد يُهاجم فيه كلبُ صيدٍ سُلوقي وصقرٌ غزالةً؛ ويحملُ الطيرُ في منقاره قطعةً ذات شكل حلزوني. إن هذه القطعة المؤرخة في النصف الثاني من القرن 5 الهجري / القرن 11 الميلادي مماثلة لقطع أخرى يرجعُ أصلُها إلى غرب البحر الأبيض المتوسط؛ وتم استيرادها من القيروان (تونس).

en.name: Glazed bowl.
description:
Glazed bowl with everted rim with small horizontal edge, circular mouth, hemispherical body and convex base with vertical foot-ring. The exterior is coated in an almost transparent whitish glaze. The interior is decorated with a polychrome glaze in white, green, purple and yellow, with an unusual schematic figurative style. The central motif consists of a lively hunting scene in which a hound and a bird (perhaps a hawk or eagle) are simultaneously attacking a gazelle. The bird carries in its mouth a spiral-shaped object which may be a snake or a branch. The rim has a scalloped pattern of black arcs filled with green glaze.  
When it was in use, the object was repaired with clamps. There are also holes in the base which were probably used for hanging the bowl on the wall. The object has been restored.

Bowl depicting a hunting scene in which a greyhound and a falcon attack a gazelle. There is a spiral-shaped object in the bird’s mouth. This piece, dated to the second half of the AH 5th / AD 11th century, is similar to others from the western Mediterranean and was imported from Kairouan (Tunisia).
dates: Hegira second half of 5th century / AD second half of 11th century.
keywords: ceramic; zoomorphic imagery; trade; hunting; animal decoration; bird
materials: Glazed ceramic made with coarse-grained straw and paste mix, modelled on a wheel, fired in an oxidising atmosphere and decorated in green and purple.
tags: Glazed ceramic made with coarse-grained straw and paste mix, modelled on a wheel, fired in an oxidising atmosphere and decorated in green and purple.

es.name: Ataifor.
description:
Ataifor de borde extrovertido con pequeña ala horizontal, boca circular, cuerpo hemisférico y base convexa con pie anular vertical. El exterior fue revestido de un vidriado blancuzco casi transparente. El interior fue decorado con vidriado policromo en blanco, verde, morado y amarillo, con un peculiar estilo figurativo esquemático. El motivo central consiste en una dinámica escena de caza en la que un galgo y un ave (tal vez un halcón o un águila) atacan simultáneamente a una gacela. Esta lleva en la boca un elemento en forma de espiral que podría ser una serpiente o una rama. En el borde encontramos un festón de arcos negros rellenos de vidriado verde.  
  
En su período de uso, el objeto fue reparado con lañas. Encontramos también orificios en la base que se destinaban, probablemente, a colgar el objeto de la pared. Pieza restaurada.

Ataifor con escena de caza en la que una gacela es atacada simultáneamente por un galgo y un ave. Esta última lleva en la boca un elemento espiral, quizá una serpiente o una rama. La pieza, con paralelos en el Mediterráneo occidental, habría sido importada de la zona de Kairuán.
dates: Segunda mitad del siglo V H. / XI d. C.

fr.name: Ataifor (plat creux).
description:
*Ataifor* à bouche circulaire, bord extraverti avec une petite aile horizontale, corps hémisphérique, base convexe et pied annulaire vertical. L'extérieur est recouvert d'une glaçure blanchâtre presque transparente. L'intérieur est décoré d'une glaçure polychrome en blanc, vert, violet et jaune, dans un style figuratif particulier. Le thème décoratif central consiste en une dynamique scène de chasse dans laquelle un lévrier et un oiseau (peut-être un faucon ou un aigle) attaquent simultanément une gazelle. L'oiseau porte dans la bouche un élément en forme de spirale qui pourrait être un serpent ou une branche. Sur le rebord court un feston de petits arcs noirs remplis de glaçure verte.  
À l'époque où il était utilisé, le plat fut réparé avec des agrafes. Nous trouvons également des trous dans la base qui font penser que l'objet était probablement destiné à être accroché sur un mur. Pièce restaurée.

Plat représentant une scène de chasse dans laquelle un lévrier et un faucon attaquent une gazelle. Il y a un objet en forme de spirale dans le bec de l'oiseau. Cette pièce, datée de la seconde moitié du Ve siècle H (XIe siecle J.-C.), est semblable à d'autres originaires de l'ouest de la Méditerranée et fut importée de Kairouan (Tunisie).
dates: Seconde moitié du Ve siècle H (du XIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: céramique ; zoomorphe ; commerce

pt.name: Tigela.
description:
Tigela de bordo extrovertido com pequena aba horizontal, boca circular, corpo hemisférico e base convexa com pie anular vertical. O exterior foi revestido com um vidrado esbranquiçado quase transparente. O interior foi decorado com vidrado polícromo em branco, verde, manganés e amarelo, com um peculiar estilo figurativo esquemático. O motivo central consiste numa dinâmica cena de caça em que um galgo e uma ave (tal vez um falcão ou uma águia) atacam simultaneamente uma gazela. Esta leva na boca um elemento em forma de espiral que poderá ser uma serpente ou um ramo. No bordo encontramos um festão de arcos negros cheios com vidrado verde.  
O objecto foi reparado com gatos durante o seu período de uso. Encontramos também orifícios na base, que se destinavan, provavelmente, a pendurar o objecto na parede. Peça restaurada.

Tigela onde se representa uma cena de caça em que um galgo e um falcão atacam uma gazela. Esta segura na boca um elemento em forma de espiral. A peça, datada da segunda metade do século V H./XI d.C. e com paralelos no Mediterrâneo Ocidental, terá sido importada da zona de Kairouan.
dates: Segunda metade do século V AH / XI AD.

en.name: Itala 35/45 HP
description: After the proposal of a Peking-Paris race, a team made up by driver Scipione Borghese, mechanic Ettore Guinizzardi and journalist Luigi Barzini participed the 16,000km race and crossed the finish line 20 days ahead the other four competing teams. The Itala "Peking-Paris" in 1989, after careful restoration, repeated the same trip on a longer route (25,000km) without any mechanical problems and in 2007 repeated the victory route again on the centenary of the race. The four-cylinder engine displaces 7,433 cubic centimetres to provide 45 horsepower at 1,250 revolutions per minute to give the car a top speed of 95km/h.

en.name: Konya Prayer Rug
description: This rug is known as the “prayer rug with a high estrade”.It was woven specifically for the midday religious service in mosques on Fridays. The Kaʽba and its surrounding  buildings are portrayed. Kaʽba  motifs and foot marks at the bottom side indicate the direction of the prayer, as one must turn his/her face to the Kaʽba during prayer. There are hanging candle motifs symbolizing the holy (eternal) lights of the prophet along the right and left side of the Kaʽba motifs. The floral decoration on the borders are typical for its origin and date.

en.name: Sculpture of Dounreay Power Station
description: Glass artist Kate Williams’s practice explores the scientific, cultural, and artistic elements of glass and light. In her collaborative Glass Nuclear Power Station Project with the artist John Lloyd, three real, and one fictional nuclear power station were memorialised in cast uranium glass. The use of uranium glass for these sculptures represents society’s complicated relationship with nuclear power. Lit from underneath with ultraviolet light, which excites the particles of uranium dioxide; they emit a bright acid lime green colour. The use of uranium has been used as a safe colorant in glass since the mid-19th Century. However, here it suggests the vitrification of nuclear waste as a way of dealing with the nuclear legacy. The Dounreay site was opened in 1955 for the development of fast reactors. Three reactors were built on the site, the Dounreay Fast Reactor (DFR), Prototype Fast Reactor (PFR) and the Dounreay Materials Test Reactor (DMTR). All three are now closed.
artist: Kate Williams (1971, United Kingdom) and John Lloyd (1965, United Kingdom)
keywords: Contemporary Glass; Studio Glass; Art Glass
materials: Uranium glass; lost wax process; kiln cast

ar.name: نظام كنجوي (كنجافي) أو جمال الدين أبو محمد إلياس بن يوسف بن مؤيد نظام الدين، مؤلف خمسة.
description: ألف  نظام كنجوي الشهير الخمسة (الخماسي)، واسمه الكامل جمال الدين أبو محمد إلياس بن يوسف بن مؤيد نظام الدين (تاريخ. 605هـ / 1209م). كُتبت هذه النسخة بخط النستعليق على يد الناسخ شمس الدين بن غياث الدين الحافظ الكِرماني. وقد أتمّ نسخ المخطوطة — باستثناء الإقبال‌نامه — في سنتي 905–906هـ / 1500م، بحسب ختمي النسخ الواردين في الصفحة 42b, والصفحة 152a، ويُرجَّح أن ذلك تمّ في شيراز، إيران. وتجسّد اللوحات التسع والعشرون، التي تتراوح بين نصف الصفحة والصفحة الكاملة، مرحلة الانتقال من الأسلوب التركماني المتأخر إلى الأسلوب الصفوي المبكر. غير أنّ تعديلات وترميمات قد تكون أُجريت بالفعل خلال القرن السادس عشر. وبعد قرن من ذلك، اقتُنيت المخطوطة لصالح المكتبة الوطنية النمساوية على يد بيتر لامبيك في القسطنطينية سنة 1677م.
keywords: بهرام; هفت بيكار; اسكندر; خمسة; خسرو; ليلى; مجنون; معراج; نظامي; شيرين

en.name: Nizami Ganjavi, or Jamal ad-Din Abu Muhammad Ilyas b.Yusuf b. Mu’ayyad Nizam ad-Din, *Khamsa* ('Quintet')
description: The *Khamsa* (‘Quintet’) was written by the famous Nizami Ganjavi, whose full name is Jamal ad-Din Abu Muhammad Ilyas b. Yusuf b. Mu'ayyad Nizam ad-Din (died 605 AH / 1209 AD). This copy was written in *nasta’liq* script by the scribe Shams ad-Din b. Giyath ad-Din al-Hafiz al-Kirmani. He finished the manuscript (excluding the *Iqbalnama*) in 905-6 AH / 1500 AD according to two colophons on fol. 41b and fol. 152a, possibly in Shiraz, Iran. The 29 half- to full-page paintings represent the transition from the late Turkmen to the early Safavid style. However, alterations and restorations may have already been carried out in the 16th century. One century later, the manuscript was acquired for the Austrian National Library by Peter Lambeck in Constantinople in 1677.
keywords: Bahram; Haft Peykar; Iskandar; Khamsa; Khosrow; Layla; Majnun; mi'raj; Nizami; Shirin

en.name: Treaty of the French Protectorate, 12 May 1881
short_description: This drawing shows an important moment in modern Tunisian history: the signing of the treaty of the French Protectorate over the Tunisian regency, at the Palais Kassar Saïd, in Bardo, on 12 May 1881. The main players are featured in this drawing, namely Sadok Bey who ruled Tunisia from 1859 to 1882, with his hand resting on the table, and to his right the general Jules Aimé Bréart, the leader of the invading French troops.

cs.name: Plán zámku a zahrady
description: R. 1650 byl Jan Rottal jmenován císařským tajným radou, současně byl i vrchní válečný komisař, nejvyšší zemský sudí moravský i biskupského manského soudu, nejvyšší správce sirotčího jmění, předseda královského tribunálu a zemský hejtman. Neustále udržoval nejužší styky s vídeňským dvorem. Luchese, činný v císařských službách, proslulý jako inženýr vodních staveb, zde navrhl široké kanály kolem květinového parteru a členění na obvyklá čtyři pole. Na ně navazovala užitková zahrada a štěpnice. Rozvrh zahrady organicky souvisel se stavbou zámku, ve své době označovaném za nejkrásnější na Moravě.

en.name: Plan of the chateau and garden
description: In 1650 Jan Rottal was appointed Imperial Secret Councillor. He was also the Supreme War Commissioner, Supreme Provincial Judge of Moravia and the Episcopal Court, Supreme Administrator of Orphans' Property, Chairman of the Royal Tribunal and Provincial Governor! Unsurprisingly, he maintained very close contacts with the court in Vienna. Luchese, in imperial service, made his reputation as a hydrological civil engineer. In Holešov, he designed broad canals along the flower parterre and divided it into four sections. These were adjoined by a kitchen garden and an orchard. The layout of the garden, in its time considered the most beautiful in Moravia, matched that of the chateau.

en.name: Talismanic shirt
description:
The front and back of the shirt are covered with Qur’anic verses, prayers and invocations to God, written in a variety of scripts and arranged into variously shaped panels and cartouches. Two cartouches on the front carry depictions of the Masjid al-Haram (‘Holy Sanctuary’) at Mecca and the Masjid al-Nabawi (‘Prophet’s mosque’) at Medina, each within a decorative frame enclosing minute depictions of other holy sites in the surrounding areas.  
  
Representations of the two holy sanctuaries on talismanic shirts are rare. Among known examples are a shirt with a depiction of the Meccan sanctuary, and a cap with an embroidered depiction of the Prophet’s mosque, in the Topkapi Saray Museum, and views of both on an Indian shirt in the Khalili Collections. All, however, are schematic and unlike the views on this shirt which are more realistically portrayed.

en.name: Marina Square, Reem Island
description: This image of Marina Square on Reem Island (Abu Dhabi) reflects the transformation of modern Arab cities, where architecture and urban planning increasingly embrace blue spaces: areas designed around proximity to water. Alongside residential towers, these coastal developments integrate museums, cultural centres, promenades, and commercial hubs, merging urban living with leisure and cultural life. In many contemporary Arab cities, waterfront development symbolises progress, prosperity, and global connectivity, echoing the historic relationship between water and civilisation in the region. Just as ancient settlements flourished near rivers and coasts, today’s skylines continue to grow along the shores, redefining how water shapes identity, lifestyles, and the rhythms of urban experience.

de.name: Deckenfresko: *Der hl. Gallus heilt eine Besessene*
description: In der Tradition Andrea Pozzos ist das östliche Langhausfresko angelegt, doch bleibt die monumentale Scheinarchitektur der Kuppel nicht geschlossen, sondern eröffnet einen Ausblick in eine ganze Folge von überkuppelten Räumen. Die prachtvollen, äußerst monumentalen Architekturkulissen überhöhen die dargestellte Szene aus der Gallus-Legende mit der Heilung einer Besessenen zum Triumph von Kirche und Heilsgeschichte.

en.name: Ceiling fresco: *St. Gall heals a demoniac*
description: The eastern nave fresco is designed in the tradition of Andrea Pozzo (1642–1709), however the cupola’s monumental illusionistic architecture is not closed, instead it opens up to reveal a view of a whole series of vaulted rooms. The grand, highly monumental architectural backdrop elevates the scene from the legend of Gall healing a demoniac to that of the triumph of the church and the history of salvation.

en.name: Prayer rug
description: At the centre of this prayer rug there is a *mihrab*, which indicates the *qibla* ‒ the direction of the Kaʽba in Mecca. The Kraków example is especially attractive because of its vivid colours: a warm-red niche, closed with an arch of bizarre shape, contrasts with yellow borders. Inside the white spandrels is a black arabesque ornament. In the cross-panel there are rosettes inscribed in lozenges. The most striking feature is a wide border with a pattern of rhythmically turned rosettes and pomegranate motifs. Such a border reflects the style of Ottoman court rugs attributed to Bursa. Similar rugs can be found in many churches in Transylvania.

en.name: Sickle (*mijaz*)

ar.name: قلادة صندوق الدعاء

تُحقّق التمائم الورقية الملفوفة داخل هذه الصناديق الأمنيات وتخفف الألم وتقي من الحسد. لكن من غيرالمؤكد ما إذا كان الناس يفتحون الصناديق لقراءة الأمنيات أم ستظل هذه الأمنيات مجهولة إلى الأبد !  
  
من خلال اقتناء الصندوق أوحمله، يمكن للشخص أن يُحوّل قوة التميمة لنفسه، أو لشخص يحبه، أو حتى ضدّ أحد ما لإلحاق الضرر به. تماما كما الأمنيات المنقوشة على المجوهرات الحديثة، يمكن للرموز السحرية حسب بعض الموروثات الشعبية أن تُحدث تأثير قوي مع عبارات وكلمات دينية غالبا ما تُكتب بطريقة معكوسة.

en.name: Prayer Box with Cover
description:
This silver prayer box encompasses rich engravings suspended from a neck chain. In Iranian, Omani and Yemeni tradition, these types of necklaces treasure a secret wish.  
  
Rolled paper amulets would fulfil wishes, alleviate pain and defend against the evil eye. It remains uncertain whether people wear the prayers on their chest to be read or locked away forever.  
  
By holding or handling the box, a person enacts the power of the amulet for themselves, a loved one, or even against someone as a curse. Like engraved charms in modern jewellery, magical signs may cast a mystical aura, with Islamic phrases often written in reverse.

en.name: Beit Nizam
description:
Beit Nizam is located in the Maazanat al-Shahm quarter of Old Damascus. An inscription dated AH 1172 (1758–59 AD) provides evidence of its eighteenth-century history. The residence developed through successive architectural phases, with its elaborate interiors reflecting the changing artistic tastes of wealthy Damascene households during the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. The complex is organised around three courtyards. The fountain and walls of the first reception hall include busily colourful paintings, carving, and gilding. Sparkling brilliantly to this day is the so-called 'Qa'at al-'Inab' ('Hall of Grapes'), which represents a masterpiece of wealth and style. The extravagant use of gilded applications and mirrors reveals a very heavy European Baroque influence. One of the many ceiling mirrors shows the influence of European Baroque with its outward radiance. The Crescent and Star motifs are symbols of the Ottoman Empire and are thus evidence of the marriage between imperial and European taste in this Damascene house incorporated into established local architectural traditions.  
  
The house witnessed significant changes in Damascus during the nineteenth century, including the period of Ibrahim Pasha's rule (1832–1840). It also served as the seat of the British Consulate until 1883. According to the historical account, the residence was subsequently occupied by the al-Quwaydi family until 1926, followed by the al-Qabbani and al-Abbas families. It eventually became associated with the Nizam family, its last private occupants during the first half of the twentieth century, from whom the house acquired its present name after the family undertook renovations to the property. It was acquired by Damascus Municipality in 1974; it underwent restoration between 1987 and 1994 and was subsequently opened to visitors. Further conservation work was initiated by the Aga Khan Trust for Culture in 2008, contributing to the preservation of its historic architectural fabric and decorative interiors.
keywords: Damascus; Beit Nizam;  Courtyard houses; Residential architecture; Iwans; Painted wooden ceilings; Baroque influence; Architectural decoration
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate General of Museums and Antiquities

en.name: Kula prayer rug
description:
This prayer rug was probably made in Kula. It is decorated with a terracotta-red *mihrab* closed with a stepped arch, the spandrels of which are light blue. The bordure, which consists of 23 thin stripes, is divided into three colouristic areas of green and yellow, ivory and dark-brown, and red and blue. Every space of the carpet is filled with minute motifs: four-petal rosettes in the niche, upside down tulips in the spandrels, and flowers on leafy stalks in the bordure. The big red, yellow and ivory carnations in the cross-panels beneath and above the niche, contrast with the other flora. The colouristic and ornamental composition gives an impression of delicacy and lightness.  
Carpets made in Kula were strongly influenced by the Gördes production, but the multi-striped borders can be more often found in Kula rugs. In addition, the choice of minute floral motifs is very characteristic of this production centre. It is worth noting just how differentiated the floral motifs used to decorate the carpet are, especially in terms of the colour scheme.  
Prayer rugs were very popular among the 17th- and 18th-century nobility in Poland. Taste for Oriental art was one of the characteristic features of Polish culture at the time, and prayer rugs were widely used for interior decoration.  
The Kula rug was obtained by the very famous Polish collector Feliks Jasieński ‒ called Manggha (1861–1929) ‒ and formed part of his extensive and precious collection. Part of this collection was donated to the National Museum in Kraków in 1929, according to Jasieński’s last will and testament.
keywords: Kula; Anatolia; Prayer rug
materials: Wool (warp, weft, pile); symmetrically knotted pile (Turkish knot)

ar.name: دليل مسافات.
description: مَعْلم أو دليل مسافات، غالباً ما يُنصَب لتحديد المسافة بين محطتين على امتداد رحلة الحج أو طريق التجارة.  تعود هذه القطعة إلى عهد الخليفة الأموي الخامس، عبد الملك بن مروان (حكم في الفترة 66- 86 / 685- 705).  تحمل القطعة نقشاً يتألف من ثمانية أسطر مكتوبة بالخط الكوفي، ولا يمكن قراءة كامل النص لأن الجزء العلوي من الحجر قد تحطَّم وضاع.  أما الجزء الواضح من النقش فيقرأ: "نصب هذا الحجر عبد الله، أمير المؤمنين، عبد الملك، رحمة الله عليه. المسافة من هنا إلى دمشق 109 أميال."  لم يبقَ اليوم من النقوش الأموية إلا عدد قليل جداً.  كذلك، فإن دليل المسافات هذا ذو أهمية نظراً لأنه يرينا تطور الأسلوب في النقش الكوفي على الحجر خلال العهد الأموي.

في سنوات الإسلام الأولى، كانت مُؤشِّرات المسافات تُنصب على امتداد طرق التجارة والحج، لبيان المسافات للمسافرين. وهذه العلامات أو المُؤشِّرات تحمل التواريخ، وأسماء المسؤولين ذوي العلاقة في المنطقة، بما يجعلها ذات أهمية وثائقية.
keywords: دليل مسافة؛ رخام.

en.name: Distance marker (milestone).
description:
A distance marker or milestone usually erected to indicate distance between two stations along a pilgrimage or trade route, this one belonging to the period of the fifth Umayyad caliph, 'Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan (r. AH 66–86 / AD 685–705). The milestone is nearly square and has an inscription incised on its surface. The inscription consists of eight lines of *kufic* script. It cannot be read in its entirety because the upper section of the milestone has broken off and is missing. The legible portion reads: 'The slave of God, the commander of the faithful 'Abd al-Malik – may God's mercy be upon him – erected this stone. From here to Damascus is 109 miles'.  
  
Very few inscriptions have survived from the Umayyad period to the present. In addition, this milestone is significant because it shows the stylistic development of *kufic* script on stone during the Umayyad period.  
  
How was object obtained by museum: The inventory states that the object was transferred from the ruins of Khan al-Hatrura at Eriha (Jericho) to the Tiled Pavilion (Çinili Köşk) in 1884 as part of the 19th-century initiative to collect artworks from across the country. The object was transferred to the Museum in 1941.

In the early years of Islam, distance markers were erected on important trade and pilgrimage routes in order to show the distances to the travellers. These milestones bear date, patron names and toponyms related to the region, and are thus of documentary importance.
holder: Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts.
keywords: Distance marker (milestone); marble
partner: Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts

es.name: Mojon.
description:
Hito o piedra miliar que solía colocarse para indicar la distancia entre dos estaciones de una ruta de peregrinaje o comercio; esta pieza pertenece al periodo del quinto califa omeya, Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan (r. 66-86 / 685-705). Es prácticamente cuadrada y presenta una inscripción grabada, compuesta por ocho líneas en caracteres cúficos. No puede leerse en su totalidad porque la parte superior de la piedra se rompió y se perdió. La parte legible reza: “El esclavo de Dios, el comandante de los fieles Abd al-Malik –que la misericordia de Dios esté con él– levantó esta piedra. De aquí a Damasco hay 109 millas \[175 kilómetros\]”.  
Son muy escasas las inscripciones del periodo omeya que se conservan. Además, está piedra miliar reviste importancia porque demuestra la evolución estilística de la escritura cúfica en piedra durante dicho periodo.

En los albores del Islam se erigían hitos en las rutas de comercio y peregrinación importantes para indicar las distancias a los viajeros. Informaban de la fecha, el nombre del patrocinador y los topónimos de cada región, por lo que son relevantes desde el punto de vista documental.
holder: Museo de Arte Turco e Islámico.
keywords: hito; mármol.
partner: Museo de Artes Turcas e Islámicas

fr.name: Borne.
description:
Borne du type généralement utilisé pour marquer les distances entre deux étapes sur une route commerciale ou de pèlerinage. Elle date de la période du cinquième calife omeyyade Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan (r. 66-86 H / 685-705 J.-C.). De forme presque carrée, elle présente sur toute sa surface une inscription incisée en huit lignes rédigées en écriture coufique. La partie supérieure ayant été brisée, seul un texte partiel reste lisible : “L'esclave de Dieu, le commandeur du fidèle Abd al-Malik – que la miséricorde de Dieu descende sur lui – a érigé cette pierre. D'ici à Damas 109 milles.”  
Peu d'inscriptions omeyyades nous sont parvenues. Cette borne est d'autant plus intéressante qu'elle montre le développement de l'écriture coufique sur pierre au cours de cette période.

Dans les premiers temps de l’islam, des bornes étaient érigées sur les grandes routes de commerce et de pèlerinage pour indiquer les distances aux voyageurs. Ces bornes en pierre portent une date, le nom de leur commanditaire et des toponymes relatifs à la région, tous ces éléments étant d’une grande importance documentaire.
holder: Musée des arts turcs et islamiques.
keywords: Bornes de distances ; marbres
partner: Musée des arts turques et islamiques

tr.name: Mesafe taşı (Miltaşı).
description:
5\. Emevi Halifesi Abdülmelik ibn Mervan (66-86 / 685-705) zamanına ait mesafe taşıdır. Genellikle Hac ve ticaret yolları üzerine iki merkez arasındaki uzaklığı belirlemek için dikilen mesafe taşlarındandır. Kitabe, kareye yakın miltaşı üzerine oyma tekniğinde işlenmiştir. Taş üzerindeki sekiz satırlık kitabe kufi hatla yazılmıştır. Üst bölümü kırık ve eksik olan mesafe taşının kitabe metni tam olarak okunamamaktadır. Okunabilen satırlarda, “Allah'ın kulu, müminlerin emiri Abdülmelik, Allah'ın rahmeti üzerine olsun, bu taşı diktirdi. Şam ile burası arası 109 mildir,” yazılıdır.  
  
Emeviler döneminden günümüze çok az sayıda kitabe ulaşmıştır. Bununla birlikte günümüze gelebilmiş bu kitabeler, Erken İslam Döneminde kullanılan kufi yazının taş üzerindeki gelişimini göstermesi bakımından büyük önem taşır.

Mesafe taşları, İslamiyet'in ilk yıllarında, önemli ticaret ve hac yolları üzerinde yer alan merkezler arasındaki uzaklığı belirtmek amacıyla dikilirlerdi. Bu taşlar, tarih, kimin adına diktirildiği ve bölgenin adı hakkında bilgi veren yazıtlar içerdiğinden, birer belge niteliği de taşımaktadırlar.
keywords: miltaşı; mesafe taşı; mermer

en.name: Street Language
description: Faraj Daham’s Street Language (2011) can be used to address the social dimension of Doha’s rapid urban transformation by foregrounding the construction workers who made this development physically possible. The dominant yellow and orange tones evoke Qatar’s intense climate, while the workers’ covered faces and direct gaze draw attention to issues of labour, migration, visibility, and anonymity. Rather than presenting modernisation only through architecture and urban growth, the work invites viewers to consider the human bodies behind these processes. For this reason, Street Language is especially useful for discussing Gulf modernity as a social, economic, and human phenomenon, not merely as a visual narrative of progress.
holder: Qatar Museums, Mathaf: Arab Museum of Modern Art
keywords: urban transformation; construction workers; labour; migration

en.name: Pedestal bowl or tazza
description: A deep bowl, decorated in blue and white, with a sloping rim and supported on a pedestal base. The rim has been embellished with a pattern of rocks and waves, whilst the cavetto is decorated with floral sprays with a medallion surrounded by palmettes at the very centre. The base is also decorated with floral sprays.

en.name: The artists' tools
description: Calligraphy tools. Chinese calligraphy employs the brush, while Arabic calligraphy employs the *qalam* (reed pen). Haji Noor Deen uses both in addition to spatulas of different widths and materials. For writing, he prefers traditional Chinese ink, obtained by rubbing an inkstick on a surface with a little water so that it liquifies. The red seals are another element typical to Chinese calligraphy. The metal weights seen in the green box secure the paper and prevent it from slipping during the writing process.
partner: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums

ar.name: قطعة نسيج.
description: قطعة نسيج، رسم في وسطها مزهرية فيها ورود،  يحيطها إطار مسنن مرفوع على عامودين، وعلى قاعدتهما شجرتا سرو. نجد في القسم السفلي رسماً يمثل " مدخلاً" على طرفه هلال، يخرج من نقوش عربية. وعلى طرفي القطعة شجرتا سرو كبيرتان، زخرف جانباهما بنجوم. ويحيط بذلك كله نباتات ملتوية الأغصان ومتشابكة، ولها أوراق متطاولة الشكل، وورودها من أربع أو خمس وريقات. وقد نفذت الزخرفة كلها بواسطة التطريز بخيوط فضية أو ذهبية.
ينتمي هذا الثوب إلى إنتاج يعود إلى الوسط التركي خلال الفترة العثمانية المتأخرة، والتي تميزت باستعمال أشكال زهرية ذات الذوق الطبيعي؛ ويقدم بجلاء تأثيرا قويا للعناصر الزخرفية الغربية.

en.name: Textile.
description: The fabric is decorated in the centre with a large motif of a vase of flowers inside a pointed frame that rests on two small columns, at the base of which there are two cypress trees. The lower part of the fabric depicts a gated entrance crowned with a crescent moon beneath an epigraphic motif in Arabic characters. On either side there are large cypress trees beside star motifs. The entire piece is framed with plant volutes with lance-shaped leaves and four- and five-petal flowers. The decoration consists of gold- and silver-plated wire embroidery.
This fabric is of Turkish origin produced in the late Ottoman era and is characterised by naturalistic floral motifs, in which the influence of Western decorative trends can be clearly seen.

es.name: Tejido.
description: El centro del tejido está ocupado por un gran jarrón con flores dentro de un marco que termina en punta, sostenido por dos pequeñas columnas en cuyas bases aparecen dos cipreses. En la parte inferior aparece una cancela rematada por una media luna y, por encima de ella, un motivo epigráfico en caracteres arábigos. La cancela está flanqueada por dos grandes cipreses guarnecidos por motivos estrellados. Todo el tejido está enmarcado por volutas vegetales con hojas lanceoladas y flores de cuatro y cinco pétalos. La decoración está bordada con hilos metálicos plateados y dorados.

Este tejido se encuadra en una producción de ambiente turco de época otomana tardía, caracterizada por el uso de motivos florales di inspiración naturalista en que queda patente una marcada influencia de elementos decorativos en puridad occidentales.

fr.name: Tissu.
description: Ce tissu est orné, au centre, d'un grand motif de vase avec fleurs, à l'intérieur d'un cadre surmonté de flèches et soutenu par deux colonnettes ; au pied de celles-ci sont représentés deux cyprès. Dans le registre inférieur figure un motif de “porte à grille” surmontée d'une demi-lune, elle-même dominée par un motif épigraphique en caractères arabes. De part et d'autre, deux grands cyprès flanqués de motifs en forme d'étoile. Des rinceaux à feuilles lancéolées et fleurs à quatre et cinq pétales encadrent ces motifs. Le décor est obtenu au moyen d'une broderie avec fils de métal argentés et dorés.

Ce tissu se situe dans une production de milieu turc d'époque ottomane tardive, caractérisée par l'utilisation de motifs floraux de goût naturaliste ; il présente, de toute évidence, une forte influence d'éléments décoratifs plus nettement occidentaux.

it.name: Tessuto.
description: Il tessuto è decorato al centro da un grande motivo di vaso con fiori, all'interno di una cornice cuspidata sorretta da due colonnine, alle cui basi figurano due cipressi. Nella parte inferiore è presente un motivo di “porta a cancellata” con, alla sommità, una mezzaluna sormontata da un motivo epigrafico in caratteri arabi. Ai lati due grandi cipressi affiancati da motivi a stella. Tutto il tessuto è incorniciato da girali con foglie lanceolate e fiori a quattro e cinque petali. La decorazione è ottenuta mediante ricamo con filati metallici argentati e dorati.

Il tessuto si inquadra in una produzione di ambiente turco di tarda epoca ottomana, caratterizzata dall'uso di motivi floreali di gusto naturalistico, ove è molto evidente una forte influenza di elementi decorativi più propriamente occidentali.

en.name: Bowlegarnitur
description: An essential association for the foundation and development of Czech modern art was the one of Artěl – an initiative that was founded by two men: Alois Dyk, an art enthusiast, and banker. and Vilem Štech, an art theoretician and art historian also responsible for endorsing young Czech modernism. Several artists joined in the beginning, such as Pavel Janak, Jan Konupek and Helena Johnova. The name of the association was taken from Tolstoy’s novel *Anna Karenina* and meant a merely verbally agreed-upon community of people who work together and jointly vouch for each other, as well as have an equal share of the income. Since they lacked the finances, the Artěl could not afford their own workshop, and therefore performed manufacturing in different factories, such as the Rydl and Thon Company in Svijany-Podoli in Northern Bohemia for ceramics and porcelain, and the Pryl glass factory in Růženin in Central Bohemia for glass. Among the various artists that participated in Artěl, Josef Rosipal, even though he was an architect, was of particular importance for the implementation of the association’s ideas in the medium of glass. Rosipal’s most famous pieces are his cut services, created in simple shapes, commonly overlayed in red or blue with cut geometric decorative motifs. Additionally, since the sentiment of the Artěl association was oriented more towards expressionism, and, even more, cubism, these tendencies can be seen most clearly in the decorative motifs of the glass. The lid presented is a part of a complete set, composed of a punch bowl with a spoon and this lid, along with a set of six glasses. The handle of the lid is overlaid with ruby red glass and serves as a central point for the triangular decorative motifs that spread across the surface of the lid. The triangular and other geometric decorative motifs demonstrate the tendencies of the Artěl association in the fields of glass art.

description: Beirut Port Train Station was established in 1903 when the railway infrastructure of Beirut was extended to reach the harbour docks during the expansion of the D.H.P. network. The port station was created to facilitate the transfer of goods arriving by sea into the railway system. This connection formed part of a wider phase of railway expansion following the renewal of the company’s concession in 1900. Construction in Rayak began in 1902 and then reached Hama. In 1903, Beirut Station was connected directly with the Beirut quay through this station. The project subsequently extended the network from the Mediterranean to the interior by the Hama–Aleppo and Homs–Tripoli branches between 1905 and 1911.

en.name: Bowl with two facing peacocks
description: Birds were a popular subject in the Abbasid period, as artists working in many media transformed the creatures’ beaks and wings into increasingly abstracted designs. The symmetrical pattern of two peacocks facing each other finds iconographic precedents in examples dating from the late antique and Byzantine periods, where it often carried paradisiacal connotations. Monochrome lustre examples such as this were characteristic of the second phase of Abbasid lustreware, which developed in centres in Iraq in the tenth century. The word blessing appears in Arabic on the glazed underside of this bowl.
dates: Hegira mid-4th century / AD second–third quarter 10th century

en.name: Church of San Gil
names: Church and Bell Tower of San Gil (option)
description:
The Baroque transformations carried out between 1719 and 1725 by the masters Manuel Sanclemente and Blas Ximénez affected the original Mudéjar building here more than in the case of Santa María Magdalena or of San Miguel de los Navarros mentioned above. So much so, in fact, that the original Mudéjar traces in the monument can only be distinguished from the outside.  
The Mudéjar building was a typical fortified church (a typology visited in the next itinerary and analysed in depth). The most interesting feature of what remains is the bell tower, built on a rectangular ground plan and profusely decorated in brickwork in relief, and already mentioned in the chronicles of 1356. The rubble used for the shafts and capitals of the columns of the belfry, both here in this tower and in the Magdalena already mentioned above, was probably from the Great Mosque of the city. The architect Joaquín Soro restored the tower in 1999.

es.name: Iglesia de San Gil
names: Iglesia y torre-campanario de San Gil (opción)
description:
Las transformaciones barrocas realizadas entre 1719 y 1725 por los maestros Manuel Sanclemente y Blas Ximénez afectaron a la fábrica mudéjar original en mayor medida que en los casos anteriores de Santa María Magdalena y de San  
Miguel de los Navarros, de modo que tan solo desde el exterior se pueden apreciar los restos monumentales mudéjares de la fábrica original.  
La fábrica mudéjar correspondía al tipo de iglesia-fortaleza, que se visita en el  
recorrido siguiente, donde la analizaremos. Lo más interesante de lo conservado es la torre-campanario, de planta rectangular, profusamente decorada con labores en ladrillo resaltado y mencionada ya en las crónicas de 1356. Para los fustes y capiteles de las columnas del cuerpo de campanas, tanto en esta torre como en la de la Magdalena ya mencionada, se utilizaron materiales de derribo, procedentes  
probablemente de la mezquita *aljama* de la ciudad. La torre ha sido restaurada en 1999 por el arquitecto Joaquín Soro.

en.name: Castellaccio
description:
The castle, called “Castellaccio” (“Rotten Castle”), was built between 1174 and 1200, at the top of Monte Caputo. It provided for the Benedictine monks of the town of Monreale, a fortified lookout post against aggression from the Muslims living inland. At that time, in fact, the Muslim district settled on the mountainous relief of Val di Mazara had become independent, and so Monreale up to 1246, became a frontier town exposed to Saracen aggression.  
The fortalice stands on a structure in the form of an irregular parallelogram. Along the western front there are four rectangular-based towers, two at the corners and two in the centre, while along the opposite front there is a corner keep; to the north-west are the median turret and the apsidal area of the chapel.  
Inside the walls, the area is divided into two zones, one westerly in which a series of rooms are flanked along the wall forming an internal courtyard, and one eastern, more markedly monastic, which goes into a square courtyard recognisable as a cloister. A narrow corridor connects both areas, while the church of the complex stands at the end of the cloister, along almost the whole of the south side, erected in part over a cistern.

es.name: Castillote (Castellaccio)
description:
El castillo de la cima del monte Caputo, llamado *Castellaccio* (“castillote”), fue erigido entre 1174 y 1200. Constituía, para los monjes benedictinos de la villa de Monreale, el emplazamiento fortificado de vigilancia contra las agresiones provenientes de los burgos musulmanes del interior. En aquel periodo, en efecto, el distrito musulmán de los relieves montañosos de Val di Mazara se había hecho independiente y, así, Monreale se convirtió hasta 1246 en una localidad fronteriza, expuesta a la hostilidad sarracena.  
La pequeña fortaleza se alza sobre una planta en forma de paralelogramo irregular. A lo largo de la fachada occidental hay empotradas cuatro torres rectangulares, dos en los ángulos y dos intermedias, mientras que en el muro opuesto sobresalen un torreón de esquina, una torreta intermedia y el ábside de la capilla.  
En el interior de la muralla, el espacio está dividido en dos zonas, una occidental con una serie de habitáculos pegados al muro que dan lugar a un patio interior, y una oriental, de carácter marcadamente monástico, que da paso a un patio cuadrangular identificable como el claustro. Las dos áreas están comunicadas por un estrecho corredor. Al fondo del claustro, casi tan largo como todo el lado sur, se alza la iglesia del conjunto, construida en parte sobre una cisterna.

en.name: Armchair of Krste Petkov Misirkov
short_description: Krste Petkov Misirkov (1874–1926) was an imposing figure that contributed to the standardization of the modern Macedonian language. He lived and worked in St. Petersburg, Russia. Misirkov’s book “On Macedonian Matters” is a starting point in explaining Macedonian distinctiveness, having served as an intellectual and contemplative engine for generations of Macedonians fighting in the battlefield and in literature alike.

en.name: Lancia Lambda
description: The skeleton of the body, instead of wood, is made of 2 mm thick stamped sheet steel (‘emboutie’), surrounded on the outside by thin sheet steel as well, while on the inside the padding and cushions are movable; the two front ends close in a frame enclosing the radiator. Lengthways, the bodywork is crossed by an arched profile, a tunnel shape – which seems to divide it into two equal parts – in which the cardan transmission shaft runs. This shaping, which acts almost like a reinforced bridge, contributes to the car’s rigidity and cohesion by lowering its centre of gravity. The car can reach 125km/h thanks for a four-cylinder narrow-V engine that displaces 2,570 cubic centimetres and produces 69 horsepower at 3,500 revolutions per minute.

ar.name: قطعة من طبق.
description:
قطعة من طبق خزفي، مزيّنة بتمثيل حيواني وكتابي مرسوم بالريشة باللون البنّي على طلاء زجاجي مرصّص. يتضمّن الشريط الدائري الذي يحيط بالرسم الزخرفي الحيواني نقيشة خطيةً بأحرف كوفيّة، رُسم محيطها باللون البنّي. كما طُلي المجال الموجود بين الأحرف بنفس اللون. تتألّف النقيشة الكتابية من كلمة واحدة مكرّرة مرّتين، وهي "اليُمن". ويسبق الكلمة الأولى الحرف الأخير من نفس اللفظة، كما أنّ الحرف الأوّل يتبع الكلمة الثانية ممّا يوحي بأنّ الكلمة كانت مكرّرة على الشريط كله. تظهر الزخرفة الحيوانيّة في وسط الطبق وتحيط بها دائرة، وهي عبارة عن بقايا أسد ممثَّل بالرّأس وجزء من الكتف فقط. الرّأس موجّه بشكل أمامي، العينان محملقتان، بينما العفرة كثيفة ومتموّجة. ينقص القسم السفلي من الوجه، غير أنّ الصورة الضوئيّة الأولى لهذه القطعة التي نشرها غولفان تُظهر هذا القسم الناقص من الوجه: يبعث الخطم، و"الشاربان"، وجزء من عفرة الأسد المنسدلة الانطباع بأنّ الأسد يتحرّك. وزُين الفراغ بين الأسد والدائرة بشكلين ثلاثيّي الفصوص، أحدهما مكتمل والآخر ناقص ممّا يدلّ على أنّ هذا الشكل كان يتكرّر على كامل محيط الأسد. وعلى ظهر القطعة، لازال قسم من القاعدة الحلقيّة الشكل موجودا. وقد تمّ حفظ قطعتين أخرويتين من الطبق ذاته في متحف سيرتا الوطني، تحمل إحداهما الرسم الذي يحدّد ظهر الأسد وذيله الملتوي، كما نجد على الشريط لفظة "اليُمن".  
يشكل استعمال اللون البنّي إحدى السمات الخاصّة بالخزف الحمّادي. وتدل رقّة طينة الفخّار ووجود أشكال مرسومة على أنّ هذه القطعة تعود إلى آنية فخمة بالمقارنة مع لُقى فخاريّة أخرى عثر عليها في قلعة بني حمّاد.
كسرة من صحن زُخرف وسطه بتمثيل لأسد، وبنقيشة كتابية خططت بالريشة باللون البني المميز للفخار الحمادي، فوق طلاء زجاجي مرصوص. وتعيد النقيشة المكتوبة بأحرف كوفية كلمة "اليمن".

en.name: Fragment of plate.
description:
Fragment of a ceramic plate, ornamented with an animal and epigraphic representation that has been traced out in brown with a paintbrush on a lead glaze. The circular band surrounding the animal decoration features an inscription in *kufic* characters, the contours of which are traced in brown. The space between these characters is also painted brown. The inscription consists of a word repeated twice, '*al-yumn*' (prosperity). The first word is preceded by the last letter of the word itself, and the second is followed by the first letter of this word, suggesting that the word was repeated around the entire circumference of the band. The animal decoration sits at the centre of the plate, surrounded by a circle, and consists of a fragmented lion represented by a head and a section of shoulder. The head is turned to the front, the eyes are wide open, and the mane is dense and wavy. The lower part of the face is missing, but the first photograph of this fragment, published by Golvin (see Bibliography), shows the missing part of the face: the muzzle, the 'moustache' and a part of the falling mane, giving the impression that the lion is in movement. The space between the lion and the circle is ornamented with two trefoil motifs, one complete and the other incomplete, which suggests that this motif was repeated right around the lion. A remaining section of the circular base can be seen at the back of the fragment. Two other fragments of the same plate are kept at the National Museum of Cirta. One of these features the outline that delineates the lion's back and snake-like tail, and the word '*al-yumn'* on the band.  
The use of brown is one of the characteristics of Hammadid ceramics. The thinness of the paste and the presence of painted motifs indicate that it forms part of an expensive piece of crockery in comparison to other shards found in the Qal'at Bani Hammad.

Fragment of a dish decorated with the representation of a lion in the centre and an inscription brush-painted around the edge in brown, a colour common in Hammadid ceramics, on top of a lead glaze. The inscription in *kufic* characters repeats the word '*al-yumn*' (prosperity).

es.name: Fragmento de plato.
description:
Fragmento de plato de cerámica decorado con una representación animal y epigráfica dibujada a pincel, en color marrón, sobre vidriado plumbífero. En la banda circular que rodea la decoración animal figura una inscripción en caracteres cúficos de contornos trazados también en marrón. El espacio entre esos caracteres está pintado del mismo color. La inscripción consiste en una palabra repetida dos veces, *al-yumn* (“prosperidad”). La primera está precedida por la última letra del mismo vocablo, y la segunda está seguida de la primera letra del mismo, lo que sugiere que la palabra se reiteraba en todo el borde del plato. La decoración animal se sitúa en el centro, dentro de un círculo, y de ella se aprecia aún la cabeza y parte del hombro de un león. La cabeza está de frente, con los ojos abiertos de par en par; la melena es densa y ondulada. Falta la parte inferior de la cabeza, pero en la primera fotografía de este fragmento, publicada por Golvin, se ven el morro con los bigotes y una parte de la melena caída, que permiten suponer que el león está en movimiento. El espacio entre el león y el círculo está decorado con dos motivos trilobulados, uno entero y el otro incompleto, lo que sugiere que este motivo se repetía alrededor del animal. En el dorso del fragmento se ha conservado una parte de la base circular. En el Museo Nacional de Cirta Otros se conservan otros dos fragmentos de este plato, uno de ellos con el trazo del lomo y la cola serpenteante del animal, y en la banda de nuevo la palabra *al-yumn*.  
El empleo del color marrón es una de las características de la cerámica hammadí. La finura de la pasta y la presencia de motivos pintados indican que se trata de un fragmento de vajilla de lujo en comparación con otros encontrados en la Qala'a de los Banu Hammad.

Fragmento de plato decorado en el centro con la figura de un león y en el borde con una inscripción epigráfica dibujada a pincel en marrón –color característico de la cerámica hammadí– sobre vidriado plomífero. La inscripción en caracteres cúficos repite la palabra *al-yumn* (“prosperidad”).
