fr.name: Fragment de plat.
description:
Fragment de plat en céramique, orné d'une représentation animalière et épigraphique tracée au pinceau en brun sur glaçure plombifère. Le bandeau circulaire entourant le décor animalier porte une inscription en caractères coufiques dont le contour est tracé en brun. L'espace entre ces caractères est également peint en brun. L'inscription consiste en un mot répété deux fois, “a*l-youmn”* (prospérité). Le premier mot est précédé de la dernière lettre de ce vocable, et le deuxième mot est suivi de la première, ce qui suggère que le mot était répété sur tout le bandeau. Le décor animalier figure au centre du plat, entouré d'un cercle, et consiste en un lion fragmentaire représenté par la tête et un bout d'épaule. La tête est orientée de face, les yeux sont écarquillés, la crinière est dense et ondulée. La partie inférieure de la face manque, mais la première photographie de ce fragment, publiée par Golvin, montre la partie manquante de la face : le museau, les “moustaches” et une partie de la crinière tombante, et laisse supposer que le lion est en mouvement. Le vide entre le lion et le cercle est orné de deux motifs trilobés, l'un complet et l'autre incomplet, ce qui suggère que ce motif était répété tout autour du lion. Au dos du fragment subsiste une partie de la base annulaire. Deux autres fragments du même plat sont conservés au Musée national de Cirta. L'un d'eux porte le trait qui marque le dos du lion et la queue serpentée, et, sur le bandeau, le mot “a*l-youmn”*.  
  
L'emploi du brun est l'une des caractéristiques propres à la céramique hammadide. La finesse de la pâte et la présence des motifs peints montrent qu'il s'agit d'un fragment de vaisselle de luxe en comparaison avec d'autres tessons trouvés dans la Qalaa des Beni Hammad.

Fragment de plat orné au centre d'une représentation de lion et sur la bordure d'une inscription épigraphique tracée au pinceau en brun, couleur caractéristique de la céramique hammadite, sur glaçure plombifère. L'inscription en caractères coufiques répète le mot “a*l-youmn*” (prospérité).
keywords: plat ; vaisselle ; poterie ; céramique ; décor épigraphique ; décor animalier ; Hammadides

en.name: *Works for the opening of the Corinth Canal*
short_description:
The Corinth Canal being dug, circa 1885. Photographer unknown.  
The Corinth Canal separates the Peloponnesian peninsula from the Greek. The idea of the canal was revived after Greece gained independence but soon abandoned due to economical reasons. The opening of the Suez Canal in 1869 gave an new impetus and the following year, the Zaimis government passed a law authorising the construction of the canal, which was formally inaugurated on 23 April 1882. Zaimis assigned the project to the Hungarian István Türr who set up the Société Internationale du Canal Maritime de Corinthe but the company failed and the project was finished by the company of Andeas Syngros. The canal was designed by the Hungarian engineer Béla Gerster with the assistance of the French Vincent Dauzants, a chief engineer of the Suez canal.
keywords: photo; Corinth

en.name: Amulet case
description: The *Kufi* inscription – the Muslim profession of faith and a blessing on Hasan ibn Ahmad, who must have owned the amulet case – together with the vegetal elements are its only decoration. The square box has three eyes from which to hang it. One short side is loose, so that an invocation or verse from the Koran can be put inside.

en.name: Nossa Senhora do Reclamador (Parish Church) and Pillory
names: Nossa Senhora do Reclamador (Castelo Rodrigo Parish Church) and Pillory
description:
The Parish Church was profoundly remodelled in the 17th and 18th centuries, but its structure is still Manueline in style. Long and low, with six bays, it has the traditional rib arches that characterise this regional group.  
Some of the Flemish sculptures, dating from the early 16th century, are of interest: a *Calvary* and an exceptional *St John the Baptist* are possibly the work of Arnau de Carvalho.  
Behind the church there is a Manueline pillory, with a lantern turret and two small columns set on an octagonal pillar, which in turn stands on a base of five steps.

ar.name: رأس بشريّة.
description: تمثلالقطعة وجه رجل ذو ملامح تبدو دقيقةً جدّاً، إلا أنّه متأذّ بشدّة على مستوى الأنف والفم. الرأس معمّم على الطريقة الشرقيّة، ويذكّرنا ببعض التماثيل البشرية على فخار العهد الساماني في نيشابور. تحتوي العمامة الملفوفة على شكل الحرف اللاتيني "V" في منتصفها على ثلم واضح نوعاً ما. و يغطّي وشاحٌ الوجه كما في العديد من التمثيلات المشابهة من العهد الفاطمي في مصر أو العهد الأموي في الأندلس خلال القرنين4 و 5 الهجريين / 10 و 11 الميلاديين. عينا الشخصيّة جاحظتان قليلاً، وتبدوان وكأنّهما كانتا سابقاً مغطّاتين بقطعتين من الزجاج لتمييز الحدقة، على غرار تماثيل بشريّةٍ أخرى عُثِر عليها في صبرة وفي عين المكان؛. ويؤكّد اكتشاف هذا النوع من التمثيلات في عاصمة الفاطميين الرأي القائل بأنّ الشيعة كانوا يسمحون بنحت الأشكال البشرية، على عكس أتباع المذهب المالكي الذين كانوا من المتشدّدين الرافضين للأيقونات.

قوى اكتشاف هذه الرأس البشرية في صبرة المنصورية الرأي القائل بأن الشيعة، وعلى عكس المالكيين الذين كانوا متشددين جدا، قد كانوا يسمحون بنحت التماثيل الآدمية. ومن الممكن أن نقارن الرسم مع تلك الرسوم التصويرية التي تؤرخ بنفس الفترة والتي يرجع أصلها إلى مصر وإسبانيا.
dates: منتصف القرن 4 - منتصف القرن 5 الهجري/ منصف القرن 10- منتصف القرن 11 الميلادي
place: على هذه القطعة خلال تنقيبات صبرة المنصوريّة.
keywords: زخرفة تصويريّة؛ تماثيل بشرية.

en.name: Human head.
description:
The face is that of an apparently fine-featured man but the damage to the nose and mouth is very serious. He wears a turban in the Oriental manner. It reminds us of certain pictures of human figures on pottery of the Samanid era of Nishabour (Iran). The turban is V-shaped and a deep fold extends right across its width. The face is covered with a veil, like several other images of heads from Fatimid Egypt and Umayyad Spain in the AH 4th and 5th / AD 10th and 11th centuries. The man's eyes are quite prominent and seem originally to have been covered by two pieces of glass indicating the irises, like other images found on site at Sabra.  
The head's discovery in the Fatimid capital gives weight to the opinion that the Shi'ites, unlike the very iconoclastic Malikites, tolerated human representation in their sculptures.

The discovery of this piece in Sabra al-Mansuriyya, the Fatimid capital, supports the idea that Shi'ite Muslims tolerated sculptures of human forms, unlike the very iconoclastic Malikites. This image is similar to others originating from Spain and Egypt at that time.
keywords: Figurative decoration; human figure

es.name: Cabeza humana.
description:
A pesar de estar gravemente dañado en la parte de la nariz y la boca, se aprecia el rostro de un hombre con rasgos aparentemente muy finos. La cabeza, cubierta con un turbante según la tradición oriental, se asemeja a ciertas representaciones humanas sobre cerámica del periodo samaní de Nishabur. El turbante, en forma de V, contiene un pliegue bastante marcado en el medio. Al igual que varias representaciones similares de época fatimí procedentes de Egipto o de la época omeya provenientes de España, siglos IV / X y V / XI, el rostro aparece cubierto por un velo. Los ojos del personaje, levemente prominentes, dan la impresión de haber estado cubiertos anteriormente con dos fragmentos de cristal para señalar el iris, como en el caso de otras representaciones humanas halladas en el emplazamiento de Sabra.  
Su descubrimiento en la capital de los fatimíes refuerza la tesis según la cual los shiíes toleraban las esculturas de figuras humanas, contrariamente a los malikíes, que fueron muy iconoclastas.

El hallazgo de esta cabeza esculpida en Sabra al-Mansuriya, capital de los fatimíes, reforzó la tesis según la cual los shiíes toleraban las esculturas de figuras humanas, a diferencia de los malikíes, que fueron muy iconoclastas. La representación es similar a otras, del mismo período, procedentes de Egipto y España.
dates: Mediados del siglo IV-mediados del V de la Hégira / X-XI d. C.
keywords: Decoración figurativa; figura humana

fr.name: Tête humaine.
description: Le visage est celui d'un homme dont les traits paraissent très fins, mais il est fortement endommagé au niveau du nez et de la bouche. La tête est enturbannée à la mode orientale. Elle nous rappelle certaines représentations humaines sur céramique de l'époque samanide de Nichabour. Le turban, en forme de V, comporte en son milieu une rainure assez marquée. Le visage est couvert d'un voile, à l'exemple de plusieurs représentations analogues d'époque fatimide provenant d'égypte ou d'époque omeyyade provenant de l'Espagne des Xe et XIe siècles. Les yeux du personnage sont légèrement globuleux et semblent avoir été couverts précédemment de deux fragments de verre pour indiquer l'iris, à l'instar d'autres représentations humaines trouvées à Sabra, sur les lieux mêmes. Sa découverte dans la capitale des Fatimides renforce l'opinion selon laquelle les chiites toléraient les sculptures des représentations humaines, contrairement aux malikites qui furent très iconoclastes.

Sa découverte à Sabra al-Mansouriya, la capitale des Fatimides, renforça l'opinion selon laquelle les chiites toléraient les sculptures des représentations humaines, contrairement aux malékites, très iconoclastes. La représentation est comparable à celles, de la même époque, provenant d'égypte et d'Espagne.
dates: Milieu du IVe-milieu du Ve siècle de l’Hégire (milieu du Xe-milieu du XIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: Décoration figurative ; figure humaine
partner: Musée des arts islamiques de Kairouan

en.name: *Execution of Robert Blum on 9 November 1848 in Brigittenau near Vienna*
*Tekke Ensi*
description:
This carpet was made by the Turkoman nomad tribe Tekke. The term *ensi* refers to a decorative *yurt* (tent) door hanging, in which many elements of the ornamental design functioned as protective symbols to ward off evil spirits.  
The central field is divided into three panels along the vertical axis. The upper and lower panels have the same decoration. The central column divides the panels into quarters. The column is decorated with “curled leaf” motifs separated by vertical bands with *bovrek* (bud) motifs. Each quarter is filled with a *gush* (bird) pattern arranged in horizontal rows. The central horizontal panel is decorated with “curled leaf” motifs separated by horizontal bands with *kochak* (ram's horns) motifs. The upper transverse band is intercepted in the middle by the *mihrab* (prayer niche) arch flanked by straight lattice design of oblongs and triangles. Above this transverse band there is another one with the variation of *kelle* (head) motif. The central border is decorated with variation of the *gapyrga* (ribs) motif. The inner border is decorated with *kochak* motifs. The outer border is decorated with the *sainak* motif. This type of border is a very common outer border on *ensi*s. The minor border is the soldat border or guard stripe, a very common minor border. The base panel carries a small geometrical design.
keywords: Turkmenistan; Tekke; engsi

en.name: Church of Santa Ana
description:
One of the gates in the Muslim wall, now called *Arco de la Imagen*, is the entrance to the area occupied by the Church of Santa Ana. Constructed on the site of an old mosque, once it had been consecrated it was used as the Parish Church until 1500.  
On a basilica ground plan, it is divided into three aisles, with a choir loft at the end and an octagonal sanctuary. The supporting arches and those at the entrance to the chapels are Gothic, as are the supports. In the interior, the Mudéjar ceilings are notable with their *armaduras de limas* retained in natural wood, providing a sharp contrast with the brightness of the whitewash, which covers the walls, supports and chapels. The sobriety of its elements and the chromatic contrasts make this church a good place to rest before venturing to the centre of the city where the Muslim *zocos* or marketplaces were, and which are as busy and noisy as is to be expected in a provincial capital.

es.name: Iglesia de Santa Ana
description: Una de las puertas de esta muralla musulmana, ahora denominada Arco de la Imagen, da paso al lugar que ocupa la iglesia de Santa Ana. Fue construida sobre el solar de una antigua mezquita que, una vez consagrada, subsistió como parroquial hasta 1500. Con planta basilical y dividida en tres naves, tiene coro a los pies y presbiterio de planta octogonal. Los arcos formeros y los que abren las capillas, así como los soportes, son góticos. En el interior destacan las cubiertas mudéjares con sus *armaduras de limas* que mantienen el color natural de la madera en contraste acusado con el blanco de la cal que inunda paramentos, soportes y capillas. La sobriedad de elementos y el contraste cromático convierten esta iglesia en un lugar de reposo antes de descender al centro de la ciudad, donde estaban los zocos musulmanes, con el bullicio característico de una capital provincial.

en.name: The lid of a liquorice box by the Fratelli Caflisc steam liquorice factory in Catania, Sicily
Banknote
description: The Iraqi banknote depicting Dukan Dam presents a visual articulation of state-led modernisation and hydraulic sovereignty. Constructed on the Great Zab River in the mid-twentieth century, the dam represents the strategic harnessing of water for irrigation, flood control, and hydroelectric power. Its inclusion in national currency frames large-scale water infrastructure as a symbol of economic progress, territorial integration, and technological advancement within modern Iraq.
keywords: Water; banknote; Iraq

en.name: Loulé Museum
description:
The Loulé Archaeological Museum is housed in the former governor’s residence, a building that was recently restored and which also houses the Municipal Historical Archives. The exhibition, which occupies two rooms, is arranged according to a traditional chronological sequence, which begins with the prehistoric period and ends in the modern period.  
The Islamic period is represented by the remains found at two archaeological sites in the municipality: Salir Castle (to the north of Loulé) and the Roman ruins of Cerro da Vila (at the well-known resort of Vilamoura). These are predominantly ceramic pieces, although it is also possible to see a group of distaffs used for spinning.

es.name: Museo de Loulé
description:
El Museo Arqueológico de Loulé está instalado en el edificio de la alcaidía, un inmueble recientemente recuperado y que alberga también el Archivo Histórico Municipal. La exposición, distribuida en dos salas, sigue el tradicional orden cronológico, empezando por materiales prehistóricos y terminando en los tiempos modernos.  
El periodo musulmán está representado por las piezas provenientes de dos yacimientos arqueológicos del término municipal: el castillo de Salir (al norte de Loulé) y el Cerro da Vila (en el conocido balneario de Vilamoura). Predominan los materiales de cerámica, aunque también es posible apreciar un conjunto de agujas de roca utilizadas en el hilado.

en.name: Necklace
short_description: This silver necklace from Grande Kabylie was traditionally worn on a woman's bosom to hold the *ddill*, a finely woven cloth worn by women of the region. It is made of of two ornate brooches with a coral in the centre, connected by a gold chain necklace to which the jeweller has added various French coins (francs) that were no longer in use. A number of jewellers used coins to decorate their jewellery. They usually used coins which had suddenly gone out of use.
holder: Musée Public National des Arts et Traditions Populaires
partner: National Museum of Popular Arts and Traditions

fr.name: Collier
short_description: Bijou en argent de Grande Kabylie porté sur la poitrine pour retenir le “ddill”, tissage fin porté par les femmes de la région. Il est constitué de deux fibules ornées d’un corail en leur milieu et reliées par un collier constitué d’une chaîne à laquelle le bijoutier a accroché des monnaies françaises (francs) qui n’étaient plus en circulation. Nombre de bijoutiers utilisaient les monnaies pour agrémenter les parures. Souvent, il s’agissait de pièces cachées qui avaient soudain cessé d’avoir cours.
holder: Musée public national des Arts et Traditions populaires
partner: Musée Public National des Arts et Traditions Populaires

en.name: *Conversion of St. Paul* Altarpiece
description:
A Rococo type of *reredos* (retable) with ornamental pilasters instead of columns, and a wealth of Rococo ornamentation in compact form. At the centre is the *Conversion of St. Paul*, flanked by two female saints without attributes. Two angels kneel at the corners of the cornice. The central, upper section of the altarpiece holds the coat of arms of the Halper-Sigetski family.  
Initially, the altarpiece stood in St. Mark's Church in Zagreb, near the triumphal arch. Like most altarpieces in the church, this one was commissioned by a particular guild, the boot-makers' guild. Its production was part funded by a donation from Anna Gerlichich in 1760, as an inscription on the altarpiece details.  
The altarpiece is by an accomplished master, showing a high level of design and technical skill. The influence of Vid Königer (one of the greatest Styrian sculptors of the second half of the 18th century) is apparent, seen in the female saints in particular.  
During restoration of St Mark's at the end of the 19th century, the altarpiece was moved to the chapel of Zajezda Manor in Hrvatsko zagorje, at that time owned by Baron Halper-Sigetski, who placed his baronial arms on it.

A richly carved Rococo altarpiece: two saints stand either side of twisted pilasters and two angels decorate the attic, while the central scene of the *Conversion of St Paul* is in high relief.  
Commissioned for St Mark's Church by the boot-makers' guild in 1760, it was part-funded by a donation from Anna Gerlichich, as an inscription on the altarpiece details.  
During restoration of the church at the end of the 19th century, the altarpiece was moved to the chapel of Zajezda Manor in Hrvatsko zagorje, at that time owned by Baron Halper-Sigetski, who placed his baronial arms on it.
place: Boot-Makers’ Guild altarpiece, Church of St. Mark, Zagreb

en.name: Bag for hauling water with draft animals (*ad-dalū*)
description: This huge leather bag (*ad-dalū*) is designed for lifting water by means of draft animals. An angled pathway allows the animals to walk uphill while lowering the bag into a well or reservoir, and downhill when pulling against the weight of the water-filled bag. A single *dalū* has a capacity of 10 to 40 litres.

en.name: Minaret of the Agadir Mosque
description:
From the 2nd / 8th century, Idriss I, king of the first Berber-Muslim dynasty, founded the city of Agadir and built a mosque there in 173 / 790. Today only a few sections of ramparts remain, notably the famous quadrangular minaret, a symbol of the old city of Tlemcen. It was built next to the original mosque around 678 / 1280 by Yaghmoracen.  
  
The minaret of Agadir, a fine decaying monument with a unique silhouette, dominates the old city, which has since moved west and abandoned its original sites. Remarkably, the minaret still bears inscriptions in Latin.  
  
With a quadrangular shape, 26.60 metres high, it is composed of a base of squared stones (cut in Roman times) six metres high. Above is a brick tower whose four facades are punctuated by shallow carvings in arches and interlaced patterns. Small openings intended to illuminate the interior staircase can be seen. On the platform from which the muezzin made the call to prayer the crowning lantern’s four sides show a network decoration in diamond shapes. Festoon arches in relief and a green tiled frame complete the whole.

fr.name: Minaret d’Agadir
description:
Dès le IIe/VIIIe siècle, Idriss Ier, roi de la première dynastie berbéro-musulmane, fonde la ville d’Agadir et y fait construire une mosquée en 173/790. Aujourd’hui, il ne reste sur le site que quelques pans de remparts, et surtout le célèbre minaret quadrangulaire, l’un des symboles de la vieille ville de Tlemcen, édifié tout contre la mosquée originelle par Yaghmoracen vers 678/1280.  
  
Avec sa silhouette particulière, le minaret d’Agadir, fin monument qui se délabre, domine la vieille ville qui s’est déplacée à l’ouest, abandonnant les premiers lieux de son implantation. Fait remarquable, il comporte des inscriptions en latin.  
  
De forme quadrangulaire, haut de 26,60 m, il est composé d’un soubassement de pierres – un remploi romain – jusqu’à une hauteur de 6 mètres. Au-dessus se dresse une tour en briques dont les quatre façades se voient rythmées de faibles défoncements garnis d’arcatures et de réseaux. On y distingue les petites ouvertures destinées à éclairer l’escalier. Sur la plate-forme d’où le muezzin lançait l’appel à la prière, les quatre faces du lanternon qui couronne l’ensemble présentent un décor de réseau losangé. Des arcs à festons et un encadrement de céramique verte terminent le tout.

en.name: *The sufi saint Mian Mir praying at Medina*
description:
Mian Mir belonged to the Qadiriyya order of Sufism and spent the majority of his lifetime in Lahore. He was known for his religious tolerance and was revered by both Muslims and Sikhs. Prince Dara Shikoh, who was a key follower, is said to have read the oration at Mian Mir's funeral.  
  
He is shown praying in the courtyard of the Prophet’s mosque, in front of the ‘Garden of Fatima’, with the *rawda* and the green dome above the Prophet’s tomb in the background.

en.name: *Two Bookcase Doors Depicting Shelves with Music Books*
description: This extraordinary still life is formed by two paintings depicting the shelves of a bookcase. Music books are casually displayed vertically and horizontally. The books are depicted tidy and dense on the upper level and on the lower levels they are untidy, including books laying down. On the lower shelves there are several writing devices: two pen dryers, an inkstand, a bottle of ink, and a bunch of goose-quills. The original provenance of this painting is uncertain: the first documented information is in 1801 when it was moved from the monastery of St Francis to the Liceo Musicale. For a long time, Father Giovanni Battista Martini was thought to be the patron of this painting. He was a great scholar, specialist in contrappunto, and one of the most significant personalities of XVIII century music. Recent studies (A. Mazza in *Le stanze della Musica*) show that the paintings were probably intended as a present for Father Martini, who was younger than the painter. From a careful analysis the inscriptions on the book bindings appear to be posterior to the date attributed to the painting, perhaps to adapt it to the musical culture of a new owner.

it.name: *Due sportelli di libreria con scaffali di libri di musica*
description: Si tratta di una straordinaria natura morta composta da due tele raffiguranti gli scaffali di una libreria, con diversi libri di musica disposti in un ordine orizzontale e verticale in modo quasi casuale, ordinati e compatti nei ripiani superiori, disordinati, adagiati in qualche caso nei ripiani inferiori. Nei ripiani più bassi tutto l'occorrente per scrivere: due asciugapenne, un calamaio, una boccetta d'inchiostro, un fascio di penne d'oca. Le origini non sono certe: le prime notizie risalgono al 1801 e al trasferimento del dipinto dal convento di San Francesco alla sede del Liceo Musicale. Per lungo tempo ne fu attribuita la committenza a Padre Giovanni Battista Martini, grande erudito e studioso di contrappunto, una delle figure più significative del mondo musicale del '700. Da studi recenti (A. Mazza in *Le stanze della musica*) sembrerebbe che ne fosse invece il destinatario, essendo Padre Martini di gran lunga più giovane del pittore ed avendo accertato con attenta analisi che le iscrizioni sui libri risultano tardive rispetto alla datazione dell'opera, forse per adattare l'opera alla cultura musicale del nuovo proprietario.

ar.name: قناة ( داخل المشفى النفسي).
description:
القناة: هي مجرى مائي، بني لخروج المياه الجوفية من أعماق كبيرة وسحبها الى سطح الارض وتوزيعها على المباني. هذه الاقنية المكتشفة في باليرمو هي الأقنية العربية الفارسية، التي تمتاز عن الأقنية الشرقية بعدم استخدام بئر للتعبئة في بداية القناة.  
وبفضل هذه الشبكة المتفرعة تحت الأرض لعشرات الكيلومترات، تمَّ ضمان جريان الماء بصورة مستمرة وطبيعية من جوف الارض الى سطحها، وتشكيل خزانات ماء وبحيرات ومياه حمامات عامة، وري الحدائق الغنية التي ورد وصفها في العديد من مؤلفات العصور الوسطى.

يحتضنُ المستوى تحت أرضي لمدينة باليرمو شبكة من القنوات الخاصة بتصريف المياه، والتي تلتقط مياه الفرشة المائية، وتنقلها في بعض الأحيان من أعماق هامة إلى بضع أمتار من مستوى الحقول: يسمى هذا الإنجاز ذو الأصل العربي الفارسي قناة؛ وكان يضمن  تدفقا مستمرا  وتلقائيا للماء من الفرشات الباطنية حتى سطح الأرض.

en.name: Qanat (inside the Psychiatric Hospital).
description:
*Qanats* are underground drainage channels that collect aquifer water and bear it from considerable depths to within a few metres of ground level. The *qanats* discovered in Palermo are of the Arab-Persian type, but differ from their Eastern counterparts in that they are not fed by a real well, but by a transversal drainage gallery located upstream.  
This network of underground channels, which extends over tens of kilometres, ensured a continuous and spontaneous supply of water from the underground aquifer to the surface, making it possible to construct fishponds, fountains and public baths and to water the lush gardens described in medieval sources.

In the ground beneath Palermo there is a network of drainage channels that carry aquifer water from significant depths up to ground level. These complex Arabo-Persian-inspired hydraulic engineering works are known as the *qanat*, and they guaranteed the continuous and spontaneous flow of water from underground aquifers to the surface.
keywords: water
partner: Regione Siciliana, Assessorato ai Beni Culturali

es.name: *Qanat*
description:
El *qanat* es una galería subterránea de drenaje que recoge las aguas de los acuíferos de ladera y las conduce desde grandes profundidades hasta pocos metros del nivel de la superficie. Los descubiertos en Palermo pertenecen al tipo de *qanat* arábigo-persas, si bien difieren de los orientales en que carecen de un verdadero pozo de alimentación, que es sustituido por una galería transversal de drenaje ubicada pendiente arriba.  
Este entramado de canales subterráneos, que se extiende a lo largo de decenas de kilómetros, garantizaba un flujo continuo y espontáneo de agua desde las capas subterráneas hasta la superficie, lo que posibilitaba no sólo la construcción de estanques, fuentes y baños públicos, sino también el riego de los exuberantes jardines descritos en los textos medievales.

En el subsuelo de Palermo existe una red de conductos de drenaje que recogen las aguas de ladera y las conducen, incluso desde grandes profundidades, a escasos metros de la superficie. Esta compleja obra de ingeniería hidráulica, de influencia árabigo-persa, responde al nombre de *qanat*. Garantizaba un flujo continuo y espontáneo de agua desde las capas subterráneas hasta la superficie.
dates: Siglo VI de la Hégira / XII d. C.
keywords: agua
partner: Regiona Siciliana, Assessorato ai Beni Culturali

fr.name: *Qanat* (à l’intérieur de l’hôpital psychiatrique).
description:
Le *qanat* est une conduite souterraine de drainage qui intercepte les eaux des nappes phréatiques et les amène, même à partir de profondeurs importantes, à quelques mètres du niveau du sol. Ceux qui ont été découverts à Palerme appartiennent à la typologie des *qanat* arabo-persans, mais, à la différence des *qanat* orientaux, il manque ici un véritable puits d'alimentation ; il est remplacé par une galerie transversale de drainage, située en amont.  
  
Grâce à ces conduites, qui se développent en un réseau de parcours souterrains sur des dizaines de kilomètres, on pouvait assurer un flux spontané et continu d'eau en provenance des nappes souterraines, ce qui permettait la création de viviers, de fontaines et de bains publics, ainsi que l'arrosage des jardins luxuriants décrits par les documents médiévaux.

Le sous-sol de Palerme abrite un réseau de conduits de drainage qui interceptent les eaux de la nappe phréatique et les amène, parfois à partir d'une profondeur importante, à quelques mètres du niveau de la campagne : cet ouvrage complexe, d'origine arabo-persane, s'appelle *qanat*. Il garantissait un afflux d'eau, continu et spontané, des nappes souterraines jusqu'à la surface du sol.
keywords: eau
partner: Regiona Siciliana, Assessorato ai Beni Culturali

it.name: *Qanat* (dentro l’Ospedale Psichiatrico).
description: Il qanat è un cunicolo drenante che intercetta le acque di falda e le conduce, anche da notevoli profondità, a pochi metri dal piano di campagna. Quelli scoperti a Palermo appartengono alla tipologia dei qanat arabo-persiani: a differenza di quelli orientali, però, qui manca un vero e proprio pozzo di alimentazione, sostituito da una galleria trasversale drenante, ubicata a monte. Grazie a queste condotte, che si sviluppano in una rete di percorsi sotterranei per decine di chilometri, era possibile garantire un flusso continuo e spontaneo d'acqua dalla falde sotterranee fino in superficie, consentendo di creare peschiere, fontane e bagni pubblici e di irrorare i giardini lussureggianti descritti dalle fonti medievali.

Nel sottosuolo di Palermo è presente una rete di cunicoli drenanti che intercetta le acque di falda e le conduce, anche da notevoli profondità, a pochi metri dal piano di campagna: questa complessa opera di ingegneria idraulica, di derivazione arabo-persiana, prende il nome di *qanat*. Essa garantiva un flusso continuo e spontaneo d'acqua dalla falde sotterranee fino in superficie.

en.name: Burgonet (*shishak*)
description: This morion (open helmet) belonged to the later Grand Vizir Mehmet Sokolovitsch (AD 1505–79). He was one of the many Christian boys selected for Devşirme (converted to Islam and trained for leadership positions). The sumptuous Oriental helmet is decorated with framed inscriptions containing appeals to Allah and verses from the Qur΄an. Sokolovitsch rose quickly at the court of Sultan Süleiman (AD 1494–66), retaining his position as Grand Vizir under the latter's successors, Selim III (AD 1524–74) and Murad III (AD 1546–95).

de.name: Hochaltar
description: Der mächtige Altaraufbau aus Stuckmarmor bildet den Chorabschluss, die Mitte des Polygons bis zum Gewölbe einnehmend. Opfergangsportale stellen den Anschluss zu den seitlichen Chorwänden her. Das Altarblatt mit dem Martyrium des Kirchenpatrons Andreas wird von mächtigen Gruppen aus freistehenden Säulen gerahmt, die geschwungene Gebälkstücke tragen, aber nicht miteinander verbunden sind. Dadurch besteht ein direkter Übergang zwischen dem Altarblatt (Annahme des Kreuzes durch den heiligen Andreas, Anton Zoller, 1761) und dem Altarauszug, der sozusagen die himmlische Zone bildet. Gottvater thront hier vor dem Durchblick zum Fenster, umgeben von zahlreichen Engeln und Putten. Der Kirchenpatron wird als Mittler zwischen Erde und Himmel inszeniert. Die Statuen links und rechts, Arbeiten von Franz Engele (1765), stellen die heiligen Petrus, Paulus sowie Rupert und Virgil dar (die letzten beiden sind die Patrone des Erzbistums Salzburg).

en.name: High altar
description: The massive altar superstructure from stucco marble occupies the centre of the polygon, extending to the vault. Portals for the offertory procession connect to the side walls of the choir. The altarpiece depicting the martyrdom of the church patron St. Andrew is framed by unconnected groups of free-standing columns supporting curved sections of entablature. This results in a direct transition between the altarpiece (*Acceptance of the Cross by St. Andrew*, Anton Zoller 1761) and the altar crown, which forms the heavenly zone, so to speak. Here *God the Father* is enthroned before the window, surrounded by numerous angels and putti. The church patron is thus staged as the mediator between earth and heaven.

cs.name: Archanděl Rafael
description:
Zábradlí se vějířovitě otevírá do předmostí, kde vstup na most otevírají z každé strany dva andělé – strážci a ochránci. Rafael doprovázející na cestě malého Tobiáše je vedle Sv. Anny vyučující P. Marii jediným sousoším na mostě. Je zosobněním stráženého Ducha, doprovázejícího poutníky a cestující. Jeho jméno znamená “Bůh uzdravuje” a je ztotožňován s andělem, který rozvířil vodu  
v rybníku Bethesda, u nějž lehávali nemocní. Věřilo se, že jeho voda má zázračné léčivé vlastnosti.

en.name: Archangel Raphael
description: The railing opens, fan-like, onto the bridgehead, where the entrance is guarded by two angels on either side. Raphael accompanying little Tobias is, apart from St. Anne teaching the Virgin Mary, the only statue group on the bridge. The angel personifies the guardian spirit believed to accompany pilgrims and travellers. His name means “God heals” and he is identified with the angel who rippled the waters of Lake Bethesda, on the banks of which the diseased used to lie. The water of the lake was believed to have miraculous healing properties.

en.name: Chair seat cover
description:
The whole picture created on this carpet presents a quiet and leisurely scene of a lotus pond in summer with an egret among the large lotus leaves on delicate stems.  
The lotus blossom, when first introduced into the Chinese artistic repertoire, symbolized the Buddhist notion of purity. It is a beautiful, spotless white flower which grows from the muddy bottoms of ponds. This characteristic of growing out of mud unstained would have played a role in the Buddhist meaning of the flower.  
The picture on this small carpet, however, forms a rebus that plays upon the sounds of Chinese written characters. The egret standing in a pond with lotuses can be “read” as “wishing you success in an ever upward path”. Designed to cover the seat of an elegantly carved large wooden chair, the size and format of this rug were determined by its intended use.
holder: The George Washington University Museum and The Textile Museum

en.name: *Bayt Lisbuna, Damascus*
names: Inhabitants in the courtyard demonstrating the new style of decoration and clothing
short_description: The Bayt Lisbuna saw two major construction phases. The existing structures date from the 19th century (around 1810) and were remodelled after 1865 and 1872. This house of a Jewish family like many other houses of Muslim or Christian families underwent major changes in style and plan at the end of the 19th and beginning of the 20th centuries. Several thousand private homes were adopted to the new modern style, with a radical change in techniques and forms of decoration. While still being a Damascene courtyard house these monuments of private taste became witness of a comprehensive urban change in the light of an entangled modernity.

en.name: Rue al-Mokadem
description: Named after a Tétouanese warrior chief, al-Moladem Abu al-‘Abbas Ahmed Ibn ‘Aissa Naqsis, al-Mokadem Street, which links Suq al-Foqui Square to Gharsa al-Kebira Square, was opened in the 11th/17th century. 130 m. in length, this street, the most commercial one in the *medina*, is lined with buildings which rise above 10 m. The interplay of the various sizes of its buildings, the variety of its lights, the whiteness of its walls and the paving of its ground turn this street, together with its numerous ramifications, into an area which defines the urban specificity of Tétouan.

es.name: Calle al-Mokadem
description: Nombrada en honor de un jefe militar tetuaní, al-Mokadem Abu al-Abbas Ahmed Ibn Aissa Naqsis, fue abierta en el siglo XI/XVII. Une la plaza Suq al-Foqui con la plaza Gharsa al-Kebira. Con sus 130 m de longitud, esta calle es la más comercial de la *medina* y está bordeada de construcciones de más de 10 m de altura. Sus juegos de volúmenes, sus contrastes de luces y sombras, la blancura de las paredes y el pavimentado del suelo, hacen de ella y de sus numerosas ramificaciones un conjunto que pone de manifiesto el carácter singular del urbanismo tetuaní.

fr.name: Rue al-Mokadem
description: Du nom d’un chef guerrier tétouanais, al-Mokadem Abou al-Abbas Ahmed Ibn Aïssa Naqsis, la rue al-Mokadem, joignant la place Souk al-Foqui à la place Gharsa al-Kebira, a été ouverte au XIe/XVIIe siècle. S’étendant sur une longueur de 130 m, cette rue, la plus commerçante de la médina, est bordée de constructions s’élevant sur plus de 10 m. Ses jeux de volume, ses variétés de lumière, la blancheur des parois et le pavage au sol font de cette rue, et de ses nombreuses ramifications, un ensemble qui marque la spécificité urbanistique de Tétouan.

en.name: Cup with *merletto* ('lace') decoration
short_description: The Museum of Industrial Arts (M.A.I.) was established in 1872 in Rome as a collection of manufacts (glasses, majolica, sculptures, materials, photographs, metals, casts and other) from antiquity to 19th century, and as a training school for specialising artisans, as part of the process of revaluation of the so-called "minor arts". Venetian glass has a long history, inherited from the Roman, Byzantine and Islamic tradition in the Middle Ages. The tendency of Murano's industries in using bizarre shapes, often of zoomorphic inspiration, gave life to manufacts not so much functional as decorative. It was very successful. The cylindrical cup in green glass with white glaze and “lace” decoration is the result of a combination of common design details in the second half of the 19th century: while it shows a Victorian decoration, the structure of the object recalls a late 14th century model.
holder: Museo Artistico Industriale, National Gallery of Ancient Art in Palazzo Barberini

en.name: Alfaina Tower
description:
The Norman construction consisted of a rectangular turret probably on two levels. The foundations hide a complex system of adduction and distribution of the water that comes from the spring of Gabriele. It uses a canal that runs across the present-day external court over which the façade and 18th century staircase overlooks. It then penetrates inside the edifice near the area to the east, as is often found in literary and poetic descriptions of the 12th century, and it flows into five radiating channels reaching the outside. On the façade, the presence of water is revealed in fact by a catchment, but the characteristics of the system of canalisation of the water leaves the idea of the original existence of a fountain flowing over the ample fornix with an pointed arch which concerns the central axis of the whole lower floor of the front. However, the same fornix seems to have been constructed later. In the basement of the façade, the top of three ogival arcades can be seen, which it could be imagined were the points of the crossing of the canals irrigating the surrounding park, or, possibly, were never confirmed (Valenti, 1932), as adductions of water from a large nearby artificial lake (referring to the systemisation of the complex of Favara).  
The original building was begun during the reign of Guglielmo II and named Cuba Soprana (“Sovereign Cuba”), possibly to distinguish it from the one further, later and bigger, down the valley. In the 15th century, when it was turned into an agricultural fortified tower, it was called Torre Alfaina, by which name it is still known today. The name of Cuba Soprana disappeared when, in 1758, the jurist Don Carlo Napoli acquired the property in order to build his country villa.  
In 1995 systematic restoration of the baroque villa and the surviving parts of the medieval walls was begun, under the direction of the Regional Superintendence of Cultural and Environmental Heritage of Palermo. During this phase of work the Norman masonry came to light, that which had already been discovered in 1920. This allowed once more for recognition of successive enlargements during the 16th, 17th and 18th centuries, up to the time of the changes effected during the second half of the 19th century and also including the modifications to an ornamental garden into an informal one.

es.name: Torre Alfaina
description:
La construcción normanda estaba formada por una torre de forma rectangular, probablemente de dos pisos. La planta de la base esconde un complejo sistema de aducción y distribución de las aguas provenientes del manantial del Gabriele, utilizando un canal que, a través del actual patio externo al que dan la fachada y la escalinata del Setecientos, penetra en el interior del edificio y, en correspondencia con el último espacio del lado este, se ramifica, como tantas veces se lee en las descripciones literarias y poéticas del siglo XII, en cinco canales que llegan al exterior como una corona de rayos. En la fachada, la presencia de agua está evidenciada actualmente por un estanque que la recoge, pero las características del sistema de canalización hacen pensar en la existencia originalmente de una fuente que fluía a través del amplio vano de arco apuntado que determina el eje central de toda la base del frontal. De todos modos, el propio vano parece haber sido realizado después. En el basamento de la fachada se observa el vértice de tres arcos ojivales menores que tal vez fueran puntos por los que atravesaban los canales de riego de la parte circundante del parque o bien, como afirman hipótesis nunca comprobadas (Valenti, 1932), canales que llevaban el agua a un gran lago artificial contiguo (y aquí serviría de referencia la disposición del complejo de Favara).  
El edificio original se comenzó durante el reinado de Guglielmo II, y fue llamado Cuba Soberana (Cuba Soprana) quizá para distinguirlo del situado más abajo, posterior y de mayores dimensiones. En el siglo XV se transformó en torre fortificada con terreno agrícola y tomó el nombre de Torre Alfaina, con el cual es conocido hoy. El nombre de Cuba Soberana se perdió cuando el jurista don Carlo Napoli adquirió, en 1758, el complejo para la construcción de su villa extramuros.  
En 1995 empezaron trabajos sistemáticos de restauración de la villa barroca y de las partes supervivientes de mampostería medieval bajo la dirección de la Superintendencia Regional de Bienes Culturales y Ambientales de Palermo, durante los cuales se han vuelto a sacar a la luz los muros normandos, ya redescubiertos en 1920, lo que ha permitido una vez más ver las sucesivas ampliaciones del siglo XVI que conllevaron también la modificación en clave informal del jardín ornamental.

en.name: Bowl with a lustreware decor
description: This complete table bowl was discovered during the Murwab excavation by the Qatari-French Mission in 2009. This bowl has an open wall and was used to present food prepared at the table. It has a horizontal rim with a rounded end (16cm in diameter) and a flat annular base (8cm in diameter). The glaze is quite damaged and the painted decoration can only be seen in a few places with brown touches of lustreware.
dates: Hegira late 2nd to late 3rd century / AD late 8th to late 9th century

ar.name: علبة مغطاة بتصميم أشخاص ، نباتات وأشكال هندسية
description: القطعة عبارة عن صندوق نحاسي أصفر ذو اثني عشر ضلعا مع تطعيم بالفضة والذهب و له غطاء ذو قبة نصف كروية مركزية على السطح.والغطاء مزين بشكل نافر بنماذج هندسية متداخلة ونباتية مفصولة بواسطة عصابات مستوية / بسيطة متعرجة.والشريط عليه أشخاص راكعين والقبة محاطة بمنطقة متدرجة ملتوية ومحاطة ثانية بدرجة ملتوية أعرض ونقاط الالتواء متقابلة في الموقع. وهذه الدرجة الأعرض لها نفس التزيين المحزز والغطاء يستدق بشكل طفيف حول شفة القعر المستوية السفلية ويتصل بالعلبة عند عصابة رقيقة من ضفيرة ذات طراز خاص والشفة العليا لها نفس نوع تزيين الخلفية النافر والشرائط مفصولة بعصابات من التعرج.والحلقات تحتوي أشخاص جالسين وواضعين رجلا على رجل وتستند العلبة على قعر محدب. وهناك نوع من التآكل و السحج فوق كل سطح العلبة . والسطح العلوي للقبة فيه ثقب بارز وبعض المعدن قد تم طويه فوق السطح (هذه كانت نقطة الاتصال للقبضة ويوجد حلقة تظهر في الصور الأقدم للقطعة ولكن قد تم  إزالتها بعد ذلك وأيضا المنطقة في جانب الغطاء يبدو أن فيها سدة معدنية صغيرة يمثل نوعا من الإصلاح.

en.name: Covered Box with Design of Figural, Vegetal, and Geometric Motifs
description:
A twelve-sided brass box with silver and gold inlay has a cover with a central hemispherical dome on the top. The cover is relief decorated with interlocking geometric and vegetal patterning, separated by plain bands of meander. The main register of the dome has circles containing kneeling figures. The dome is surrounded by a stepped, scalloped area, surrounded again by a broader scalloped step, points of the scallops corresponding in location. This broader step has the same incised decoration. The cover tapers in slightly around a plain bottom lip and joins to the box at a thin band of stylized guilloche.  
The box has the same type of background relief decoration, registers separated by bands of meander. The roundels contain seated, cross-legged figures. The box rests on a convex bottom.  
There is some wear and abrasion over the entire surface of the box. The very top of the dome has a notable hole; some of the metal has been folded back over the top \[this was the point of attachment for a handle and a ring that appears in older photographs of the object, but has since been removed\]. Also, one area on the side of the cover seems to have a small metal "plug" type of repair.
dates: Hegira First half 8th century / AD first half 14th century
keywords: Covered; Box; Metalwork; Copper; Alloy; Silver; Gold; Inlay; Iran; Asia; Persian
materials: Copper alloy with silver and gold inlay
tags: Copper alloy with silver and gold inlay

en.name: Daguerreotype by Jean-Gabriel Eynard-Lullin
description: The photographer in this picture is Jean-Gabriel Eynard-Lullin, a pioneer of daguerreotypes and stereo-daguerreotypes in Switzerland, who was a prominent figure in international photographic history. In the successful composition, he is posing with his family in the garden in front of Villa Beaulieu in Rolle on Lake Geneva. As a banker, financial adviser and diplomat, he exerted great influence on politics and culture.

ar.name: الطيفور.
description: طيفور ذو حافة مقلوبة نحو الخارج ومدوّرة، وفوهة دائرية، وجسم نصف بيضوي، وقاعدة مسطحة.غُطيت القطعة من الخارج بطلاء مزجج أحادي اللون عسلي، منفذ بشكل جيد، ومن الداخل بطلاء مزجج متعدد الألوان، يحتوي على الأبيض والأخضر والبنفسجي، مع رسومات لأشكال نباتية تتألف من تكوين شعاعي لثمانِ زهور لوتس مثلثة، تعلوها ثلاث زهور لوتس بيضوية. ويتواجد على حواف الصحن تكوين رباعي الأطراف تتناوب فيه أنصاف الدوائر مع أشكال نباتية الشكل. ويحوي قعر القطعة على عيب يعود لكون هذه الآنية قد ظلت ملتصقة بقطعة أخرى داخل الفرن أثناء عملية التزجيج. قطعة مرمّمة.

طبقٌ مزخرف تحت الطلاء بشكل نباتي، عبارة عن ترتيب شعاعي مكون من ثمانية زهور لوتس مثلثة الشكل؛ تعلو كل واحدة منها زهرة لوتس ذات شكل بيضوي. هذه القطعة مماثلة لقطع أخرى وجدت بمدينة الزاهرة؛ ومن المحتمل أنها آتية من جهة قرطبة.

en.name: Glazed bowl.
description: Glazed bowl with rounded everted rim, circular mouth, semi-oval body and flat base. The object has an exterior finish in honey-coloured monochrome glaze, and a polychrome glaze of white, green and purple in the interior, representing a plant motif consisting of a radial composition of eight lotus flowers topped by another set of eight oval lotus flowers. On the rim is a composition in four parts with alternating semi-circles and phytomorphic motifs. It has a defect at the bottom caused by the glaze coming into contact with another object in the kiln. The object has been restored.

en.name: Castle and Village
description:
Today, Idanha-a-Velha is a small village with only a few dozen inhabitants. And yet, the small country houses have either been superimposed onto the remains of ancient monuments or else they exhibit re-used building materials. This once important Roman City, known at that time as Egitania, was the See of a diocese throughout the period of Visigothic rule from Toledo. According to Ibn Hajjan, the Cordoban chronicler, during the first years of the Islamicisation process the old city was known as N.yani. He relates that it was the refuge for the locally born rebel Ibn Marwan and his clan, who had, for several decades, opposed the centralisation of power in the hands of the *Caliph*s of Cordoba.  
The solid granite masonry walls that still encircle Idanha even today are of the same type as those found at the Conventual in Mérida (built in 219/835). Chronologically, these walls were either slightly earlier than, or even perhaps contemporary with, the defences of Talavera de la Reina, built at the orders of Abd al-Rahman III at the end of 3rd-b. 4th/b. 10th century. As in the case of the latter, the semi-cylindrical turrets found in Idanha are part of a Roman and Byzantine tradition. The city’s northern gate, with its double entrance flanked by two semi-cylindrical towers, also points to a similar chronology.

es.name: Castillo y núcleo urbano
description:
Idanha-a-Velha es hoy una pequeña aldea con algunas decenas de habitantes. Y sin embargo, por todas partes las pequeñas casas campesinas se sobreponen a monumentales vestigios o reutilizan sus materiales. Esta importante ciudad romana, conocida como Egitania, fue sede de un obispado durante el reino visigótico de Toledo.  
Durante los primeros años de islamización —según descripción del cronista cordobés Ibn Hayyan—, la vieja ciudad entonces conocida como N.yani fue refugio del rebelde Ibn Marwan, originario del lugar, y de su clan familiar, que durante algunos decenios se opuso a la centralización califal de Córdoba.  
Las murallas de graníticos y sólidos sillares que todavía hoy cercan Idanha son de la misma familia tipológica que las del Conventual de Mérida (levantado en el año 219/835). Cronológicamente serán poco anteriores o incluso contemporáneas de las defensas de Talavera de la Reina, que mandó construir Abd al-Rahman III a finales del siglo III-p. IV/p. X. Como en este último caso, los torreones semicilíndricos de Idanha entroncan aún con la tradición romana y bizantina. La puerta norte de la ciudad, con su entrada de doble portón flanqueada por dos torres semicilíndricas, remite también a una cronología similar.

de.name: Architektur
description:
Die Dreieinigkeitskirche gilt als Johann Michael Prunners Meisterwerk. Sie ist sowohl in architektonischem als auch in theologischem Sinn eine Schöpfung von höchster Perfektion. Besonders hervorzuheben ist, dass sie als symbolisches Bauwerk mit vielen Anspielungen an die Heilige Dreieinigkeit geplant und errichtet wurde.  
Als Gebäude typisch dem süddeutschen Raum zuzuordnen, sticht es wegen des symbolischen Programms und wegen des italienischen Einflusses unter den süddeutschen Barockkirchen hervor. Francesco Borromini war damals vielen Architekten, wie Johann Michael Prunner, ein künstlerisches Vorbild. Sein Werk war sehr populär und gehörte zum Allgemeinwissen jedes Baumeisters.  
Borrominesk sind zB die vor- und rückschwingenden äußeren Wände und Türme, der Grundriss des Innenraums mit den halbkreisförmigen Altarnischen (in den Türmen), die damit auf den kreisförmigen Zentralraum reagieren. Und das indirekte Licht, das von oben und von den Seiten hereinströmt und die Altargemälde und das kleine Fresko in der Laterne beleuchtet.  
Die Mauerdurchbrüche hinter den Altären, die Verwendung von indirektem Licht und die Kirchenausstattung gehen auf Francesco Messenta in seiner Funktion als Innenraumgestalter zurück (er war aber auch als Architekturmaler tätig, s. unten bei: Kuppel- und Wandfresken). Wie der Architekt hat er sich damit symbolisch vor Borromini verbeugt.
place: Auf einem Hügel in Stadl-Paura nahe des Traun-Flusses

en.name: Church’s architecture
description:
The Trinity Church is considered to be Johann Michael Prunner’s masterwork, a creation of highest perfection in both architectural and theological sense. It is very special because it was planned and constructed as a symbolic edifice with many allusions to the Holy Trinity.  
Being typically South German as a building, it stands out in many ways, with the symbolic program and Italian influence. Francesco Borromini was an artistic idol to most architects of this time, such as to Johann Michael Prunner. His oeuvre was not only very popular but generally acknowledged.  
Borrominesque are the forth- and back-swinging outer walls and towers, and the even floor plan with three semicircular altar niches (in the towers) that respond to the circular central room. And the indirect light, flooding from above and from the sides, illuminates the altar paintings and the tiny fresco in the lantern.  
Breaking through the walls behind the altars, the use of indirect light and the interior design go back to Francesco Messenta in his role as interior architect (he also did the illusionistic painting in the church, s. below: Fresco paintings in the cupola and on the walls) who symbolically bowed, like the architect, to Borromini.
place: On a hill in Stadl-Paura next to the river Traun

en.name: Photograph of Ion Ghica (sitting)
short_description: In 1848, Ion Ghica was the envoy of the Wallachian revolutionaries to Istanbul, where he remained after the suppression of the revolution. He created connections among the Ottoman officials, being appreciated by Reshid-Pasha (Grand Vizier from 1854), and became a supporter of the Romanian Principalities’ union under Ottoman sovereignty. A former journalist, he devised the project (not realized) for an economic and literary periodical, published in all the languages spoken in the Empire. In 1854 he was appointed governor of the island of Samos, where he took measures against piracy and founded several schools (a middle school, an agricultural school, a marine school and a girls’ institute). His activity earned him the title of “prince”(bey) of Samos, which he received from sultan Abdülmecid in February 1856.

ar.name: جزء من شاهدة قبر.
description: جزء من شاهدة قبر شبه مربعة، وقد كَسر الجزء السفلي منها. يحتل الجزء المركزي أربعة أسطر منقوشة بالخط الكوفي المورق وبقايا سطر خامس تحتها، وقد تم تأطيرها بشريط ضيق من لفائف أوراق النخيل المشطورة. تظهر في السطر الأول عبارة "بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم"، والبسملة عادة ما تكون متبوعة باسم المتوفى وتاريخ الوفاة على الرغم من أنه لم تتم قراءة النص بشكل جيد بعد. وعلى الرغم من أن الإسلام القويم يمنع رفع القبور إلا أن أغلب المجتمعات الإسلامية تتجاوز هذه القاعدة، وقد درجت العادة لدى الشيعة بوضع شاهدة على القبر.

مع أن إبراز القبور، ليس مُحبَّذاً في الإسلام، فإن قطع شواهد قبور كهذه، تُبيِّن أن مسلمين كثيرين لم يبالوا بالأمر. وشواهد القبور كانت عموماً تبدأ بعبارة "باسم الله الرحمن الرحيم"، ثم تُورَّد اسم المتوفى، وتاريخ الوفاة.
holder: المتحف الملكي، المتحف الوطني في اسكتلندا NMS.
dates: أواخر القرن الرابع- الخامس/ الحادي عشر.
keywords: خط كوفي مورق؛ شاهدة قبر.

en.name: Funerary stele fragment.
description: A fragment from a funerary stele, nearly square in shape, the lower portion of which is broken off. In the centre are four lines of foliated *kufic* script, with the remains of a fifth line below them, framed by a narrow split-palmette scroll-band. The first line of the inscription reads ‘Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim …’ (‘In the Name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful…’), a standard *bismillah* that is normally followed by the name of the deceased and the date, although the continuation of this text has not been fully deciphered. Although orthodox Islam prohibits the marking of graves, most Islamic societies disregarded this rule, and in a Shi’ite context in particular, it was usual to mark a grave with a funerary *stele*.

In Islam the marking of graves is frowned upon, but gravestone fragments like this one show that many Muslims disregarded this. Generally grave markers started with the *bismillah*, ‘In the Name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful … ’, then named the deceased and gave the date of their death.
keywords: Funerary stele; foliated kufic script; funerary object; funerary inscription; gravestone

es.name: Fragmento de lápida funeraria.
description: Lápida funeraria, casi cuadrangular, a la que le falta la parte inferior. En el centro encontramos cuatro renglones de escritura cúfica adornada con follaje y restos de una quinta línea. El texto está enmarcado por una estrecha cenefa de medias palmetas y roleos. A pesar de que no ha sido descifrado en su totalidad, la primera línea de la inscripción dice: “Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahmin...” (“En nombre de Dios, el compasivo, el misericordioso...”), *basmala* habitual que suele ir seguida del nombre del difunto y la fecha. La mayoría de las sociedades islámicas, en especial las shiíes, hacían caso omiso de la prohibición del Islam de señalar las tumbas y las indicaban con una estela funeraria.

El Islam no ve con buenos ojos que se señalen las tumbas, pero fragmentos como este demuestran que muchos musulmanes han desoído tal norma. Generalmente, las estelas funerarias comenzaban con la *basmala*, “En el nombre de Dios, el compasivo, el misericordioso”, seguida del nombre del difunto y la fecha de su muerte.
dates: Finales del siglo IV o siglo V de la Hégira / XI d. C.
keywords: estela funeraria; escritura cúfica adornada con follaje; objeto funerario; inscripción funeraria

fr.name: Fragment de stèle funéraire.
description: Fragment de stèle funéraire de forme presque carrée dont la partie inférieure, brisée, a disparu. La zone centrale est occupée par quatre lignes gravées en coufique fleuri et le haut d'une cinquième ligne. Elles sont encadrées sur trois côtés par un fin bandeau de volutes et de demi-palmettes. La première ligne de l'inscription se lit : “*Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahmim*” (au nom de Dieu le compatissant, le miséricordieux…), invocation courante, normalement suivie du nom du disparu et de la date de son décès, mais la suite de ce texte n'a pas été complètement déchiffrée. Si l'islam orthodoxe interdit le marquage des tombes, la plupart des sociétés islamiques ont abandonné cette règle et, notamment dans le contexte chiite, il était courant de marquer une tombe d'une stèle funéraire.

Si l’islam réprouve le marquage des stèles funéraires, les fragments de pierre tombale comme celle-ci montrent que de nombreux musulmans enfreignaient ce précepte. Généralement les inscriptions funéraires débutaient avec le *bismillah* “au nom de Dieu, le compatissant, le miséricordieux…”, puis donnaient le nom du défunt ainsi que la date de sa mort.
dates: Fin IVe-Ve siècle de l’Hégire (XIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: stèle funéraire ; coufique fleuri; objet funéraire; inscription funéraire; pierre tombale

en.name: *The Battle on Dealu Spirii*
short_description: In June 1848 revolution broke out in Wallachia. In terms of relations with the Ottoman Empire, Wallachia’s suzerain, revolutionaries claimed the administrative and legislative independence of the country. In the autumn, as negotiations with the revolutionaries proved unsuccessful, the Sublime Porte decided to intervene militarily. On the 13th of September, Bucharest was attacked. The battle that took place on Dealu Spirii between the Ottoman army and the Romanian soldiers helped by a company of firefighters was won by the former. Afterwards, the Ottoman sovereignty over the Romanian countries was re-imposed. The lithograph is entitled *The fight of the Romanian soldiers with the numerous column of the Ottoman army* and below the drawing a short text describes the battle.

en.name: *Apotheosis of King Saint Ladislaus*
names: Oil sketch for the high altar in the Primatial Palace at Pozsony (Bratislava)
description:
This sketch (*bozzetto*) in oil on copperplate was made for the high altar in the chapel of the archbishop's palace in Pozsony (Bratislava), built by Melchior Hefele. The chapel constitutes the last remaining example of fine Late Baroque art associated with the cult of St. Ladislaus in Hungary. The dome fresco, painted in the same year by Franz Anton Maulbertsch, represents the king striking water out of rock. The artist's intention was to revive the memory of the ruler who alleviated the thirst of his people by performing a miracle. The fresco shows the king on horseback as he performs the miracle, while in the altarpiece painting he is ascending to heaven. According to a legend current at the time, the king arranged for a portrait of Our Lady of Hungary, the Virgin Mary, *Patrona Hungariae*, to be painted on his battle flags. Thus, the white flag unfurling above his head bears the inscription “*S. Maria Mater Patrona Regni*” with an image of the Virgin and the Infant Jesus, much as if the flag was intended as a substitute for a more traditional celestial appearance. In other parts of the painting, St. Ladislaus is offering his crown together with the coronation regalia and the battleaxe, the latter being the king's usual attribute.  
Adreas Zallinger worked in Pozsony (Bratislava) from the 1770s; he was a pupil and a follower of Maulbertsch, sometimes assisting him in the execution of his work. The sketch illustrated here shows the influence of the Master's late style, his clear colours, silvery light and realistic representation of historic costumes and objects, all of which gradually dominated his work as his earlier passion and artistic inspiration began to leave him.

Andreas Zallinger was a member of Franz Anton Maulbertsch’s studio and worked on the decoration of the high altar in the Primatial Palace, Pozsony (Bratislava). This painting of the Hungarian Holy King is devoid of the Baroque vision.
place: The artist or the Archbishop of Esztergom
keywords: Allegory; Hungarian Holy Crown; Andreas Zallinger; Melchior Hefele; Franz Anton Maulbertsch; József Batthyány; St. Ladislaus; bozzetto; Virgin Mary; *Patrona Hungariae*; Primatial Palace; Madonna

en.name: Petrie and typology
short_description: In 1890 Petrie carried out a six-week season of excavations at Tell el-Hesy (as he transliterated it), which he identified, wrongly, as the ancient city of Lachish.  This was the first proper archaeological excavation ever carried out in Palestine, and in the course of this single season Petrie established the principle of dating strata by the pottery which they contained, thus establishing the outlines of the archaeological sequence, which continues to be refined to this day. This section drawing was made by Frederick Jones Bliss, who continued Petrie’s excavations from 1892–1894.
keywords: archaeology

Dragon Carpet
description:
A 17th century Caucasian pile carpet, better known as a Dragon carpet for its iconic design. Its red-background is dominated by a lattice system of two wide vegetal stems in ivory and in blue, overlapping each other in a drop-repeat directional layout. Covering each of the intersections of the lattice system are large multi-coloured palmettes of various designs. In the diamond shaped voids, or compartments, enclosed by the lattice are positioned a variety of animals including two rows of yellow “S” shaped dragons (hence the carpet’s name), three rows of pairs of deer fawns, two rows of pairs of flaming lion-and-chi-lin in combat. On the blue lattice branches are illustrated pheasants above ducks. The carpet’s narrow border has an ivory-coloured background decorated with a multi-coloured scroll of flowers.  
  
Considered to be of one of the earliest types of Caucasian carpets, a product of a cottage industry, this carpet’s design is thought to be based on earlier, and much less abstracted, Iranian prototypes. These Caucasian versions were made for the trade and its many routes.
keywords: dragon; animal decoration; leaf lattice; palmette; imaginary animal; bird
materials: Wool warp and weft; wool pile

en.name: Ahmet Gazi Madrasa
description:
This *madrasa*, commissioned by the famous Menteşe *Bey* Ahmet Gazi, is the best preserved of all the buildings of the Menteşe Emirate to have survived until the present day. Restoration work, begun in recent years, still continues. According to the Arabic inscription above the entrance, “the Great Ruler, the Sultan of the Coasts Ahmet Gazi” had this *madrasa* built in the year 1375. Ahmet Gazi’s use of the title “Sultan of the Coasts” proves that efforts to establish sovereignty over the Aegean, which were increased during the time of the Menteşe rulers Mesut Bey and Orhan Bey, came to a successful conclusion. The commercial activities and human traffic revived with the Aegean islands, Italy and southern France during this period, resulted in the first appearance of some foreign elements in Turkish architecture. Although it has all the components of the traditional Seljuq portal, there are important differences in detail on the madrasa’s entrance. From up close, the numerous mouldings that frame the main niche of the entrance recall portals of the Gothic Order.  
The *iwan* of the main entrance is located opposite the main *iwan* of the structure. The *madrasa*'s eight chambers and two *iwan*s open onto a courtyard of lateral rectangular shape. The porticoes that we are used to seeing in most of the *madrasa* courtyards are not present here. The two large chambers on either side of the main iwan are classrooms. There is a fireplace in each of the cells as well as in the classrooms. On the spandrels of the *iwan*’s main arch are two lion figures which are very simply engraved and each holding a banner in its hands; the lion on the left holds a banner that reads “Ahmed Gazi” in Arabic script. We know that some animal figures like the “eagle” and the “lion” were used as symbols of the sultan during the Seljuq period, too; however, none of these were depicted carrying banners in their hands as they do here. Of the two graves in the main *iwan*, the one closer to the courtyard belongs to Ahmet Gazi. It has been suggested that the grave adjoining might belong to another Menteşe ruler, Şücaeddin Bey. The locals, who believe that these are the graves of great religious people, make offerings and pray when they visit the graves.

es.name: Madrasa de Ahmet Gazi
description:
Esta *madrasa*, que debemos al célebre *bey* Ahmet Gazi, es el edificio mejor conservado del emirato de Menteşe de cuantos han llegado hasta nosotros, y los trabajos de restauración emprendidos años atrás continúan. En la inscripción en árabe situada sobre la entrada se lee que la hizo levantar, en 1375, “el Gran Gobernante, el Sultán de las Costas Ahmet Gazi”. El título de Sultán de las Costas es prueba de que los esfuerzos por extender la soberanía menteşí al Egeo, incrementados durante los gobiernos de Mesut Bey y Orhan Bey, habían dado fruto. La aparición de elementos extranjeros en la arquitectura turca vino determinada por el revitalizado tráfico comercial y humano con la Francia meridional, Italia y las islas del Egeo en esta época. Si bien el portal de la *madrasa* tiene todos los elementos tradicionales selyuquíes, hay relevantes diferencias en los detalles. De cerca, las numerosas molduras que enmarcan el nicho principal de la entrada recuerdan los pórticos góticos.  
El *iwan* de la entrada principal está situado frente al *iwan* principal del edificio. Las ocho cámaras y los dos *iwan*s de la *madrasa* dan a un patio rectangular. No hay aquí esos pórticos que suelen verse en la mayoría de los patios de las *madrasa*s. Las dos grandes salas de los lados del *iwan* principal eran aulas. Hay un hogar en cada celda, así como en las aulas. Las figuras de león del arco del *iwan* principal están grabadas y pintadas simplemente, y sostienen entre las garras sendos estandartes: en el del león de la derecha se lee “Ahmet Gazi” en caracteres árabes. Se sabe que también en el periodo selyuquí las figuras de algunos animales, como el león y el águila, eran símbolos del sultán, pero no llevaban enseñas entre sus garras, como en este caso. De las dos tumbas del *iwan* principal, la más cercana al patio pertenece a Ahmet Gazi. Se ha sugerido que la otra podría ser la de otro dirigente menteşí, Şücaeddin Bey. Los lugareños, que creen que se trata de tumbas de grandes personajes religiosos, hacen ofrendas y rezan cuando visitan las tumbas.

en.name: New maps
short_description: Sgt. George Armstrong, R.E., who was a key member of the Survey Party, later made a 3D ‘Raised Contour Map’ of Palestine from the 2D maps originally produced. This was shown all over the western world, and won him a medal at the St. Louis World’s Fair in 1903. It was the first such map ever constructed of Palestine, and served to introduce scholars and the public to the nature of the landscape in a way that no previous maps had done.
keywords: mapping

en.name: Church of Santa María de las Nieves
description:
The Parish Church of Santa María de las Nieves in Benacazón, was originally a Mudéjar church. The building underwent total restructure during the 17th and 18th centuries and now has a square sanctuary and two aisles. The sanctuary has a vaulted ceiling resting on a double system of *trompas*. On the east and south walls there is a steep staircase, covered with stretches of barrel- and cross vaulting, giving access to the walkway on the roof that has a crenellated parapet. The aisles have wooden ceilings, coffered in the main aisle and single-pitched on the side aisle.  
The sanctuary follows the model of the Muslim *qubba*, and, intended as an imposing *atalaya*, it is considerably higher. Originally, there was another aisle adjoining this square structure, which was shorter than the existing ones, but the visual links with the sanctuary would have been unsatisfactory according to this solution, because the reduced-size chancel arch, separating both areas, blocked the view.  
The church building can be dated to the end of the 15th century. There does not seem to be any remains of the older church in what is now the main nave, which must have been constructed in the mid-17th century at the same time as the side aisle.  
The wooden structures that comprise the ceilings of both parts of the nave conform to Mudéjar carpentry models. The building of the new nave, which is higher than the original one, and the remodelling of the chancel arch to make the sanctuary more prominent, made it necessary to alter the *trompas* supporting the vault. In its new configuration, these take the form of diamond points that were popular in the plasterwork decorations in the first half of the 17th century.

es.name: Iglesia de Santa María de las Nieves
description:
La iglesia parroquial de Santa María de las Nieves, en Benacazón, fue originalmente un templo mudéjar. Se trata de un edificio profundamente transformado durante los siglos XVII y XVIII, que presenta en la actualidad cabecera cuadrada y dos naves.  
La cabecera aparece cubierta mediante una bóveda de paños apeada en un doble sistema de trompas. En sus muros oriental y meridional se aloja una empinada escalera que, cubierta por tramos de cañón y arista, permite subir a la terraza de cubierta, dotada de antepecho con almenas de gradas.  
Las naves se cubren con estructuras de madera, con forma de artesa en la principal, y en colgadizo en la lateral.  
El presbiterio responde al modelo de *qubba* musulmana. Fue levantado con carácter monumental y con una considerable elevación para servir de atalaya. En origen, a esta estructura cuadrada se adosó una nave, más corta que las actuales, cuyo enlace visual con el presbiterio no debía resultar fluido, pues debió verse obstaculizado por las reducidas proporciones del arco triunfal que separaba ambos.  
La fábrica de la iglesia cabe establecerla en los años finales del siglo XV. De la nave primitiva no parecen conservarse restos en la que actualmente es la principal del templo, que debió edificarse en la primera mitad del siglo XVII, a la vez que se levantaba la nave lateral.  
Las estructuras de madera que cubren ambas naves se resuelven conforme a modelos de carpintería mudéjar. La construcción de la nueva nave principal, con mayor altura que la primitiva, y la remodelación del arco triunfal, con objeto de hacer más visible el presbiterio, obligaron a recortar las trompas que apeaban la bóveda. En su nueva configuración, tales elementos presentan la apariencia de las puntas de diamantes que se emplearon profusamente en las decoraciones de yeserías de la primera mitad del siglo XVII.
