en.name: Autocar M3 Half-Track
description:
Determined to improve the mobility of its troops in the late 1920s, the American army acquired several Citroën-Kégresse models for a benchmark study. Unmistakably distinct for using tracks instead of rear wheels, these models came into their own on rough terrain, where normal cars struggled. Under the supervision of the US Department of Military Material, several prototypes were built, which later gave rise to the famous M2 and M3 models.  
  
Built by the Autocar Company, Diamond T Motor Company and the White Company, the models were extensively tested on civil roads, to improve service conditions as well as reliability. The engines, the White 160AX and the IHC Red Diamond 450, were coupled to an unsynchronized manual gearbox with four speeds and a transfer gearbox with two ratios.  
  
Boasting a more imposing body than its M2 sibling, the M3 half track was designed for use in multiple war scenarios, but its main function was to transport troops. Measuring 6.52 meters in length with ten seats at the rear and three more in the cabin, the M3 also carried ammunition and weaponry behind the seats. External supports were often added to carry groceries, backpacks and other items out of necessity. Built in July 1943, by the Autocar Motor Company, this M3 half track with registration number USA 4065552/S was one of 43,000 units registered by the US Army. This very M3 saw front line action during the Second World War.

en.name: Villa Sora, fresco decoration of the main hall
description:
The decoration is split into two registers: the lower register showing the standing *Liberal Arts* and *Intellectual Activities* (arithmetic, comedy, tragedy, heroic poetry, lyrical poetry, philosophy, geometry, rhetoric, astrology and dance) as if supporting the entire decoration, between windows decorated with grotesques; the upper register, *Landscapes*, designed as mock tapestries possibly by Vespasiano Strada, which alternate with seated allegorical figures representing the *Nine Muses* (Clio, Euterpe, Thalia, Melpomene, Polyhymnia, Erato, Terpsichore, Urania and Calliope) *and Mnemosyne* (Memory) Mother of the Muses, in accordance with the dictates of Cesar Ripa's *Iconologia.* Between the two parts, garlands of flowers and fruit with heraldic animals (lion and dragon) held up by *putti* link together a series of monochrome medallions with busts of *Illustrious Men* from antiquity. In the centre of the long sides of the hall stand two prominent coats of arms, combining the heraldic symbols of the Boncompagni (dragon) and Sforza di Santa Fiora (lion rampant) families, to which the wife of Giacomo Boncompagni, Costanza, belonged. The hall is completed by a contemporary painted ceiling.  
This is an interesting example of a secular decorative theme following the Counter-Reformation: it is dominated by moral, allegorical subjects through the use of illustrious men and the essential protective role of the intellectual activities exercised by a noble family linked to the papacy, which is naturally, albeit indirectly, celebrated thus. The rich and complex decoration, which lends itself to different levels of interpretation, combines mythological, historical and naturalistic references—all alluding to different commemorative intentions nonetheless harmoniously combined by a single plan—and represents well the moment of transition from the austere spirit at the height of the Counter-Reformation to the more animated, albeit still strictly divided, spirit of early 17th-century Rome; a moment of transition recorded in numerous decorative works undertaken by the school of Cavalier d'Arpino, a genuine artistic entrepreneur in Rome during those years, who was able to call upon a considerable group of pupils from different backgrounds to help him carry out his work.

The decoration is split into two registers: the lower register, showing the standing *Liberal Arts* and *Intellectual Activities* as if supporting the entire decoration, in between windows decorated with grotesques; the upper register, *Landscapes*, designed as mock tapestries, which alternate with seated allegorical figures representing the *Nine Muses and Mnemosyne* (Memory) Mother of the Muses.
artist: Cardinal Giovanni Moroni; Giacomo Boncompagni (1548–1612), Duke of Sora
School of Giuseppe Cesari (1568, Arpino, Frosinone – 1640, Rome) known as Cavalier d’Arpino
history: The villa, located on Via Tuscolana just before the town, was built in the mid-16th century by Cardinal Giovanni Moroni who was an influential prelate of the Council of Trent. Built in a style of a city villa, it has a central courtyard, a covered roof-terrace and arched belvedere tower. In 1600 it was bought by Giacomo Boncompagni, natural son of Gregory XIII (1572–85), who commissioned Giuseppe Cesari (also known as Cavalier d’Arpino) and his studio to decorate the “main hall” with frescos, which was carried out in the first decade of the 17th century. At the end of the 19th century, the villa passed to Tommaso Saulini, who sold it to the Salesiana family, who are the current owners.
keywords: Fresco, *trompe-l’oeil*, illusionistic, muses, liberal arts, sciences, illustrious men, landscape
tags: Fresco, trompe-l’oeil, illusionistic, muses, liberal arts, sciences, illustrious men, landscape
partner: Province of Rome (Città metropolitana di Roma Capitale)

it.name: Villa Sora (decorazione affrescata del salone maggiore)
description:
La decorazione si svolge su due registri: in quello inferiore sono rappresentate le *Arti liberali* e le *Attività intellettuali* (Aritmetica, Commedia, Tragedia, Poema Eroico, Poema Lirico, Filosofia, Geometria, Retorica, Astrologia e Danza), raffigurate in piedi – quasi elemento portante dell’intera decorazione - tra le finestre decorate con grottesche mentre in quello superiore Paesaggi, concepiti come finti arazzi, forse riconducibili a Vespasiano Strada, si alternano a figure allegoriche sedute rappresentanti le *9 Muse* (Clio, Euterpe, Talia, Melpomene, Polimnia, Erato, Tersicore, Urania, Calliope) e *Mnemosine* (la memoria, madre delle Muse) secondo i dettami dell’*Iconologia* di Cesare Ripa. Fra i due registri ghirlande decorative di fiori e frutti con gli animali araldici (leone e drago) sorretti da putti, collegano una serie di medaglioni a monocromo con busti di *Uomini illustri* dell’antichità. Al centro dei lati lunghi della sala campeggiano due stemmi in cui sono uniti i simboli araldici delle famiglie Boncompagni (drago) e Sforza di Santa Fiora (leone rampante), alla quale apparteneva Costanza moglie di Giacomo Boncompagni. La Sala è completata da un soffitto coevo dipinto.  
Si tratta di un interessante esempio di tematica decorativa profana successiva alla Controriforma: vi prevalgono i soggetti morali, in chiave allegorica, attraverso il richiamo sia agli uomini illustri sia al fondamentale ruolo di protezione delle attività intellettuali che compete ad una famiglia nobile legata al papato, che viene naturalmente, anche se indirettamente, così celebrata. La decorazione ricca e articolata, che si presta quindi a diversi livelli di lettura e in cui si mescolano rimandi mitologici, storici e naturalistici - tutti allusivi di volontà celebrative diversificate ma armoniosamente collegate da un progetto unitario - bene rappresenta il momento di passaggio dallo spirito austero della piena Controriforma a quello più movimentato, anche se ancora rigidamente scompartito, del primo Seicento romano, momento di passaggio testimoniato dalle numerose imprese decorative realizzate dalla scuola del Cavalier d’Arpino, vero imprenditore artistico della Roma di quegli anni, abile nel coinvolgere nelle sue opere una nutrita schiera di allievi anche di diversa estrazione.

La decorazione si svolge su due registri: in quello inferiore sono rappresentate le *Arti liberali* e le *Attività intellettuali*, raffigurate in piedi – quasi elemento portante dell’intera decorazione - tra le finestre decorate con grottesche mentre in quello superiore Paesaggi, concepiti come finti arazzi si alternano a figure allegoriche sedute rappresentanti le *9 Muse* e *Mnemosine*, la memoria, madre delle Muse.
artist: Scuola di Giuseppe Cesari (1568, Arpino, Frosinone – 1640, Roma) detto il Cavalier d’Arpino
history: La Villa, ubicata sulla via Tuscolana poco prima del centro abitato, fu costruita alla metà del Cinquecento per il cardinale Giovanni Moroni, influente prelato del Concilio di Trento, secondo una tipologia da palazzo cittadino contraddistinto da cortile centrale, altana e torretta belvedere ad archi. Nel 1600 venne acquistata da Giacomo Boncompagni, figlio naturale di Gregorio XIII (1572-1585) che commissionò a Giuseppe Cesari detto il Cavalier d’Arpino e alla sua bottega la decorazione a fresco della “stanza grande”, realizzata nel primo decennio del secolo XVII. La villa passò poi alla fine dell’Ottocento a Tommaso Saulini che la vendette ai Salesiani, attuali proprietari.
keywords: Decorazione affrescata, Muse, Arti liberali, Scienze, Uomini illustri, Paesaggi
tags: Decorazione affrescata, Muse, Arti liberali, Scienze, Uomini illustri, Paesaggi
partner: Provincia di Roma (Città metropolitana di Roma Capitale)

ar.name: قطعة من مصحف
description:
ينتمي هذا الجزء من المصحف لأحد أقدم المصاحف في العالم: ومن المحتمل أنه نسخة عراقية قديمة جدا منسوخة بصيغة أفقية مستطيلة من الربع الأول من القرن الثامن والتي تم تخطيطها بنوع قديم من الخط يمكن تشبيهه بالخط الحجازي الذي كان معروفا في كل من مكة والمدينة.  
وإن أحكام التجويد تظهر بشكل نقاط حمراء في كل النص بينما الرصائع الدائرية في الهامش تحتوي رقم الآيات المكتوبة بالأخضر والمؤطرة بالأخضر والأحمر. وهذا شاهد نصي مهم على أكثر من 60 قطعة سابقة التي تعود لقبل عام 800 ميلادي وأحد المالكين السابقين يمكن تحديد أنه كايكوباد الأول من سلطنة الروم (1219-1237) ومن المحتمل أنه فقط واحد من عدد قليل من جامعي المخطوطات عالية المستوى حيث كان في حيازته نسخة قديمة من المصحف.
materials: حبر على ورق بارشمان (درجة 8 ) والخط المستخدم هو ربما الحجازي بشكل 15 سطرا على الصفحة.
tags: حبر على ورق بارشمان (درجة 8 ) والخط المستخدم هو ربما الحجازي بشكل 15 سطرا على الصفحة.

en.name: Qur’an fragment
description: This Qur’an fragment belongs to one of the oldest Qur’ans in the world: it is a very early, likely Iraqi, copy in oblong horizontal format from the first quarter of the 8th century, calligraphed in an early type of script relatable to *Hijazi* script in either Medina or Mecca. Vocalisations appear in the form of red dots throughout the text, while the circular medallions in the margin containing the verse count are written in green and framed in red and green. This is an important textual witness of over 60 early fragments that date to before 800 BC. One of the previous owners can be identified as Kaikobad I. of the Sultanate of Rum (1219-1237), likely only one of a handful of high-ranking manuscript collectors with this early copy of the Qur’an in their possession.
keywords: Calligraphy; Hijazi; illumination; Qur’an
materials: Ink on parchment (8°). Calligraphic script (possibly *Hijazi* script) in 15 lines per page.
tags: Ink on parchment (8°). Calligraphic script (possibly Hijazi script) in 15 lines per page.

en.name: "The Beaker Water Clock" from al-Jazari's "Book of Knowledge of Ingenious Mechanical Devices"
description: In the early thirteenth century, a scholar and engineer named Isma‘il Ibn al-Razzaz al-Jazari wrote a famous treatise called Kitab fi ma‛rifat al-hiyal al-handasiyya, or The Book of Knowledge of Ingenious Mechanical Devices. The text offered detailed descriptions of a series of elaborate machines designed to delight and impress the elites at the court where he served, in eastern Anatolia. Al-Jazari’s text and its illustrations belong to a long tradition of studies about these kinds of devices, including Greek compendia on mechanics and mathematics. This page belongs to a copy of the text that was produced in Mamluk Egypt in AH 755 / AD 1354, and was copied by Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Izmiri for a Mamluk ruler.
keywords: Water; Miniature; Folio; Technical manuscript.
materials: Opaque watercolor, gold, and ink on paper
tags: Opaque watercolor, gold, and ink on paper

en.name: San Salvatore, Chiesa del Santissimo Salvatore
names: San Salvatore, chiesa del Santissimo Salvatore
description:
The ancient abbot church with the nearby monastery of the Lateran Congregation of the Holy Saviour, also called Renian, was rebuilt in 1473–78. Between 1605 and 1623 a new plan by the Barnabite Milanese architect Giovanni Ambrogio Mazenta was built by Tommaso Martelli who is described in the documents as the “architect of our church”. The stucco statues and capitals were moulded by Giovanni Tedeschi, while Orazio Provaglia is the author of the bronze statues of the façade.  
The church bears a typical Counterreformation plan with some new ideas, referencing the Roman Jesuit church of the Gesù. The balanced longitudinal nave with its width double its height, has three chapels on both sides; the transept is crowned by a dome hidden outside by an octagonal tiburium. The apse is semi-circular inside and polygonal outside. The two tall symmetrical volumes, corresponding with the transept and central section, are easily recognizable from the outside as they are separated from the smaller volumes of the other two sections. The two sections have lateral chapels with palladian windows alternating with double, rectangular false windows, following the binary sequence of lesene and the wall design. The eight beautiful free standing columns, instead of the more common lesene or half columns, mark the progression of the nave.  
The exterior with its complex articulated prospect on the side of the church, facing via IV Novembre, is also particularly interesting.  
The interior houses memories and works of art coming from the former church. The iconographic and symbolic plan guiding the 17th century renovation culminates in the altarpiece of the high altar, representing the *Holy Saviour* by Guido Reni and Francesco Gessi (1620). This is surrounded by paintings by Giacomo Cavedoni (1622) hanging on the apse walls and representing the *Story of the Beirut Crucifix*, also the subject of one of the side chapels altarpieces, painted in late 16th century by the Florentine painter Jacopo Coppi. In the left transept stands the monumental *Sacred Family* by Alessandro Tiarini (1623). In the lateral central chapels, the *Resurrection of Christ* by Mastelletta faces *The Ascension of Christ* by Carlo Bononi. *The Ascension of the Virgin* by Agostino Carracci (now in the Pinacoteca Nazionale) hung in the third chapel on the left. In this church is buried Giovan Francesco Barbieri, known as il Guercino. He is memorialized by the slab in the middle of the main nave floor.  
After the suppressions the Napoleonic Age and of 1866, the monastery became property of the Italian government and the church is today part of the Fondo degli Edifici di Culto.

This church is a significant example of the architecture of the age of the Counterreformation. The façade is composed of two architectonical orders connected by volutes and is reminiscent of the Roman Jesuit church of the Gesù. The interior, wide and imposing, is a typical example of architectural classicism. Note the use of freestanding columns.
dates: Started in 1605, the church was completed in 1623 by different architects
history:
Work was started in 1605, interrupted in 1607, started again in 1613, and completed in 1623. This church perfectly exemplifies the debate about the doubled axis plan and the use of the free standing column employed by Magenta. While often criticized and opposed by his detractors it anticipates many future developments in architecture.  
In order to make the new church more impressive and imposing, between 1618 and 1622 some houses owned by the Lateran Canons and leaning against the side of the building were pulled down. This created an opening on the church-square, thus emphasizing the façade, standing on a high base. In 1624, in the outer corner of this church-square was built a votive column: the square and the column were both removed during the XIX century.  
Many cultivated tourists, especially foreigners, celebrated the church. Jean Mabillon, visited Bologna in May 1686 and described it as “a beautiful basilica, of modern architecture”. Montesquieu, in Bologna in 1729, wrote that “considering modern architecture, the Holy Saviour is one of most magnificent churches of Bologna”. Charles De Brosses, a passionate lover of Roman architecture, in Bologna in September 1739, described it without hesitation as the most beautiful church in town, comparing it to ancient Greek and Roman architecture.  
The roof was damaged on the 15th of June 1758 when it was struck by lightning. The church had to be restored and at that time its interior was embellished (1759-60).
keywords: Counterreformation; Ambrogio Magenta; Tommaso Martelli; Guido Reni; Francesco Gessi; Giacomo Cavedone; Free standing column; Giovanni Tedeschi; Jesuits; Francesco Barbieri known as il Guercino;  Alessandro Tiarini; Orazio Provaglia; Agostino Carracci
tags: Francesco Barbieri known as il Guercino
partner: Musei Civici d’Arte Antica di Bologna in cooperation with the Province of Bologna

it.name: Chiesa del Santissimo Salvatore
names: San Salvatore, chiesa del Santissimo Salvatore
description:
*Di antichissime origini, la chiesa abbaziale con l’annesso monastero dei Canonici Regolari del SS. Salvatore, detti anche Renani, fu ricostruita dapprima nel 1473-78, poi tra il 1605 e il 1623 su progetto del padre barnabita milanese Giovanni Ambrogio Mazenta, anche se l’esecuzione spetta al bolognese Tommaso Martelli, indicato nei documenti come “architetto della nostra chiesa”. Le statue e i capitelli in stucco furono eseguiti da Giovanni Tedeschi, mentre Orazio Provaglia fu l’autore delle statue in bronzo della facciata.*  
S. Salvatore riprende, discostandosene per alcune significative novità, lo schema di molte chiese della Controriforma, sul tipo del Gesù di Roma. L’aula longitudinale è alta il doppio della larghezza, con tre cappelle sui due lati; il transetto è coronato da una cupola, nascosta all’esterno da un tiburio ottagonale. L’abside si presenta semicircolare all’interno e poligonale all’esterno. I due alti volumi, corrispondenti al transetto e alla campata centrale, sono denunciati all’esterno in modo speculare, separati dai corpi più bassi delle due campate più strette, alle quali si accompagnano le cappelle laterali con le finestre a serliana, alternate a doppie finte finestre rettangolari, secondo il ritmo binato delle paraste e dell’impaginazione parietale. A questa sapiente e composta articolazione, si aggiungono le spettacolari otto colonne libere che, all’interno, segnano il passo delle campate dell’aula, in luogo delle più tradizionali paraste o semicolonne.  
Anche l’esterno riveste particolare interesse, nell’articolata composizione del prospetto che corre sul lato lungo della chiesa, su via IV Novembre.  
All’interno, in cui sopravvivono memorie ed opere d'arte della chiesa precedente, il programma iconografico e simbolico del rinnovamento seicentesco culmina nella pala d’altare con il Santissimo Salvatore di Guido Reni e Francesco Gessi, del 1620, attorniato sulle pareti dell’abside dai dipinti di Giacomo Cavedone, del 1622 che riprendendo il tema già illustrato nel tardo Cinquecento da Jacopo Coppi, con la Storia del Crocifisso di Beirut. Occupa una posizione di rilievo, nel transetto sinistro, la grande pala con la Sacra Famiglia di Alessandro Tiarini, del 1623. Nella cornice delle cappelle centrali ai lati dell’aula, si fronteggiano a sinistra la Resurrezione di Cristo del Mastelletta, e a destra l’Ascensione di Cristo di Carlo Bononi. Nella terza cappella a sinistra si trovava l’ Assunzione della Vergine di Aannibale Carracci, ora alla Pinacoteca Nazionale di Bologna, sostituita dalla Madonna col Bambino di Simone dei Crocefissi, del 1360 ca., detta anche Madonna della Vittoria, originariamente collocata nel Santuario di S. Maria del Monte, qui posta nel 1866. Nella chiesa è sepolto il Guercino, commemorato nella lapide tombale al centro della navata.  
Dopo le confische napoleoniche e le soppressioni post unitarie del 1866, il complesso abbaziale divenne, da allora, di proprietà demaniale e la chiesa appartiene oggi al Fondo Edifici di Culto.

Splendido esempio di architettura di Controriforma. La facciata a due ordini raccordati da volute si collega al prototipo romano del Gesù. L’interno, ampio e maestoso, esprime le ricerche nell’ambito del classicismo architettonico ed è contraddistinto dall’uso delle colonne libere.
dates: Iniziato nel 1605, il tempio fu completato con l’intervento di maestranze diverse nel 1623.
artist: Canonici Regolari del Santissimo Salvatore o Renani
history:
Le controverse vicende che accompagnarono i momenti più difficili nel corso dei lavori, iniziati nel 1605, sospesi nel 1607, poi ripresi nel 1613 e terminati nel 1623, mettono in luce il dibattito sulle scelte compositive dell'impianto biassiale e della colonna libera, perché le soluzioni del Mazenta, antesignane dei futuri sviluppi, non erano in quegli anni comprese ed anche osteggiate.  
Per dare maggiore risalto e imponenza alla nuova costruzione vennero demolite, tra il 1618 e il 1622, le case di proprietà degli stessi canonici, che si addossavano al fianco della chiesa, realizzando un sagrato, che sopraelevava la chiesa  su un alto podio. Sull'angolo esterno del sagrato venne posta nel 1624, a conclusione dei lavori, una colonna votiva: sia quest'ultima che il piazzale vennero rimossi nel corso dell'Ottocento.  
La chiesa venne apprezzata da numerosi e colti visitatori, soprattutto stranieri. Jean Mabillon, a Bologna nel maggio del 1686, la definì “*una splendida basilica, d'architettura moderna*”; secondo  Montesquieu, a Bologna nel 1729, il SS. Salvatore “*per l'architettura è una delle più belle di Bologna …*”, e Charles De Brosses, appassionato cultore delle antichità romane, a Bologna nel settembre del 1739, non esitò a definirla tra le chiese bolognesi “*la più bella chiesa di tutte*”, paragonandola all'antica architettura greca e romana (A. Sorbelli, *Bologna negli scrittori stranieri*, V, Bologna 1933, p. 70).   
Dopo la caduta di un fulmine il 15 giugno 1758, che danneggiò le coperture e le volte, si eseguirono nel 1759–60 consistenti restauri e vari abbellimenti interni.
keywords: Controriforma; Ambrogio Magenta; Tommaso Martelli; Guido Reni; Francesco Gessi; Giacomo Cavedone; Colonna libera; Giovanni Tedeschi; Gesuiti;  Francesco Barbieri detto il Guercino;  Alessandro Tiarini;  Orazio Provaglia; Annibale Carracci

ar.name: المنارة.
description:
أمر عبد المومن، السلطان الموحدي الأول، بحفر بركتين كبيرتين في مراكش، واحدة خارج المدينة، عُرِفت بصهريج البقر، لصالح مربي المواشي في المنطقة، وبركة أخرى داخل بستانه الخاص، اشتهرت بصهريج المنارة، وهي تسمية قد تكون لها صلة بمسجد الكتبية، المعلمة الرئيسية في المدينة. بيد أنه لم تتم الإشارة صراحة إلى بركة المياه باسم المنارة، إلا خلال عهد المرينيين (القرن 7- 9 الهجري / القرن 13 – 15 الميلادي).وفي هذا الصدد، تجب الإشارة إلى أن المؤرخ، خالد الناصري، قد أطلق، في كتاب الاستقصا على منارة الكتبية، اسم صومعةالمنار.  
كان السلاطين السعديون يقصدون، بين الفينة والأخرى، مسكناً مؤقتاً بنوه على طرف البركة. لكن الفضل يعود للسلطان العلوي، سيدي محمد، ابن السلطان المولى عبد الرحمان (حكم في الفترة 1238 - 1276 هجري / 1822 - 1859 ميلادي) الخليفة السلطاني (نائب الملك) في مراكش، في إصلاح البركة الموحدية، وإعادة الاعتبار للمِلْكية المَلَكية الكبيرة. فرمَّمَ الجدار الضخم المكون للسياج الذي يحمي 96 هكتاراً من البساتين (طوله 1200 م وعرضه 800 م)، وحَسَّن من تموينه المائي، وقام ببناء جناح ملكي ومركز حراسة، ومكان للخيول على أطراف بركة المياه الكبيرة الوسطى، والتي يبلغ طولها 200 متر وعرضها 150 متر.  
ويتبدى الجناح الملكي على شكل بناية قليلة الزخرفة، أبعادها متواضعة، وجدرانها المبنية من الحجارة سميكة، وزواياها من الآجر، وسقفها الهرمي المربع ملبس بقرميد أخضر مبرنق.  
وقد بني هذا الجناح على مستويين:  
\- طابق أرضي، عبارة عن قاعة مستطيلة مفتوحة بثلاثة عقود على بركة المياه، وممددة إلى الخلف عبر غرفة انتظار.  
\- طابق علوي (المنزه)، تتواجد به قاعة مربعة منعزلة تحوي شرفة كبيرة، لها درابزين، تطل على بركة المياه، وتتمدد أيضاً إلى الخلف بواسطة غرفة انتظار، تتوفر على ثلاثة نوافذ تنفتح على الجبل.  
زُوِّدتْ الشرفة بباب مربع منخفض بشكل ملفت، ويرجح أن يكون ذلك التصميم قد نُفِّذَ لمنع الأشخاص الموجودين حول البركة من رؤية ما بداخل المنزه، ولتجنب التعرض للشمس والسخونة المفرطين.  
رُكِّبَ هذا الباب الملتصق بقوس مصمت عميق ومزين بعنصر زخرفي من الحجر، ضمن إطار يَحملُ شريطُه العلوي النقيشة الكتابية الخاصة بالتأسيس.  
يزدان داخل المنزه بزخرفة هندسية بسيطة وملونة تنضح بهجة وعذوبة، وتقتصر على خيوط رفيعة من الصباغة، ألوانها زاهية على زوايا القبة الخارجية البارزة وحول النافذة.  
ويمتد الدرج الصغير، الواصل إلى الطابق، حتى مصطبة صغيرة، تستند على غرفة انتظار المنزه، وتقدم منظراً لايُحْجب على البستان الملكي الكبير، وعلى المناطق الداخلية، وعلى جبال الأطلس.  
وبالرغم من بساطته، فقد أضحى جناح المنارة واحداً من رموز مدينة مراكش.

إنه السلطان الموحدي عبد المومن الذي هيأ، بضواحي مدينة مراكش، هذا البستان المجهز بصهريج كبير (200 x 150 متر)، والذي استخدم كموضع للاصطياف للملوك المرينيين والسعديين. يرجع الفضل إلى العلويين الذين قاموا بترميمات سور السياج الحائطي، وإصلاح التزود بالماء وبناء جناح ملكي، ينتظم عل شكل بناية بسيطة ذات أسوار سميكة من الآجر، وسقف هرمي مربع ومغطى بالقرميد الأخضر وشرفة تطل على الصهريج.  
زخرف الداخل بزخرفة هندسية خفيفة وملونة تفوح الطراوة والبهجة.
dates:
الصهريج الأول: القرن 5 الهجري / 11 الميلادي.  
الجناح الأول: القرن 10 الهجري / 16 الميلادي.  
البناية النهائية: القرن 11 الهجري / 17 الميلادي.
artist: الفترة الموحدية: السلطان عبد المومن (حكم في الفترة 524 – 558 هجري / 1130 - 1163 ميلادي).
keywords: منارة؛ بساتين ملكية؛ صهريج؛ حوض؛ بركة؛ سكن ملكي؛ مياه؛ قرميد؛ حجر؛ زخرفة هندسية.
partner: Ministry of Culture,Directorate of Cultural Heritage

en.name: Menara.
description:
The first Almohad king 'Abd al-Mu'min had two large lakes dug in Marrakesh: one outside the town, *sahrij al-bgar* (the lake of the cattle) for use by the stock breeders of the area, and one within his private orchard, *sahrij al-menara* (the lake of the lighthouse, or the lake of the minaret, which may be a reference to the Kutubiya, the town's principal monument). It is worth noting that Al-Nasiri calls the Kutubiya minaret *sawmaat al-manar* (the minaret of the lighthouse) in *al-Istiqsa*. However, the lake was only formally known as the Menara under the Marinids (AH 10th / AD 16th century).  
The Sa'did sovereigns occasionally visited the *pied-a-terre* they constructed on the shore of the lake, but it was the 'Alawid Sidi Muhammad, son of Sultan Mulay 'Abd Al-Rahman (r. AH 1238–76 / AD 1822–59) and the caliphal sultan (viceroy) to Marrakesh who restored the great Almohad lake and the large royal residence.  
He repaired the enclosure wall that protected the 96 ha of orchard (1,200 m by 800 m), improved its water supply and built a royal pavilion, a guardroom and a mare farm by the large central lake, which measured 200 m by 150 m. The royal pavilion is a sober building of modest size. The stone walls are thick, with brick-built corners, and the square pyramid roof is covered with glazed green tiles.  
The pavilion extends over two storeys:  
\- the ground floor, consisting of a rectangular room that opens onto the lake through three arches and extends to the rear into an antechamber;  
\- the first floor (*menzeh*), consisting of a square room, set back, and a large balcony with balusters looking out over the lake, also extending to the rear into an antechamber with three windows that look out upon the mountain.  
The balcony has a particularly low square door, probably designed to prevent people around the lake from seeing into the *menzeh*, and to stop the sun overheating it.  
The door is set in a deep blind arch decorated with a stone motif within a frame whose upper band bears the foundation inscription.  
The inside of the *menzeh* is adorned with delicate coloured geometric decoration that gives a feeling of gaiety and freshness. It is bordered by two brightly coloured painted lines that run over the groins of the vaults and around the windows.  
The small stairway that leads to the first floor continues on to a small terrace on top of the antechamber of the *menzeh*, offering an unobstructed view of the great royal orchard, surrounding area and the Atlas mountains.  
Despite, or because of, its simplicity, the pavilion of the Menara has become one of the emblems of Marrakesh.

The Almohad king 'Abd al-Mu'min planted this orchard, complete with a large lake measuring 200 m by 150 m, on the outskirts of Marrakesh as a holiday destination for Marinid and Sassanid sovereigns. The Alawids were responsible for the repairs to the outer wall, the improvement of the water supply and the construction of a royal pavilion, a sober building with thick brick walls, a pyramid-shaped green-tiled roof and a balcony overlooking the lake. The interior is decorated with faint, coloured geometric designs, creating a cool, bright atmosphere.
dates: Hegira 5th / AD 11th century (first lake); Hegira 10th / AD 16th century (first pavillion); Hegira 11th / AD 17th century (final monument).
artist: Almohad: ‘Abd al-Mu’min (r. AH 524–58 / AD 1130–63); ‘Alawid: Sidi Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Al-Rahman (r. AH 1276–90 / AD 1859–73).
keywords: Royal residence; water; brick; stone; geometric decoration
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate of Cultural Heritage

es.name: Menara.
description:
Abd al-Mumin, primer soberano almohade, mandó cavar dos grandes estanques de agua en Marrakech: uno a las afueras de la ciudad, el *sahriy al-bgar* (estanque del ganado), en beneficio de los ganaderos de la región; otro en su huerto privado, el *sahriy al-menara* (estanque del faro o del alminar, quizás por alusión a la mezquita Kutubiya, el principal monumento de la ciudad). En *Al-Istiqsa*, Ibn al-Jatib llama *sawmaat al-manar* (alminar del faro) al alminar de la Kutubiya. No se designará formalmente como Menara hasta la época meriní (siglo X / XVI).  
Los soberanos saadíes visitaban esporádicamente el apeadero construido a orillas del lago. El sultán de Marrakech, el alawí Sidi Mohamed, hijo del sultán Mulay Abd al-Rahman (r. 1238-1276 / 1822-1859) mandó rehabilitar el gran estanque almohade y restaurar la extensa propiedad real. Se repararon los muros que circundaban las 96 hectáreas de huertos (1.200 x 800 m), se mejoró la canalización de agua y se edificó un pabellón real, un puesto de guardia y cuadras para yeguas de cría junto al gran estanque central, de 200 m de largo por 150 m de ancho.  
El pabellón real es una construcción sobria, de modestas dimensiones. Presenta gruesos muros de piedra con esquinas de ladrillo y un tejado piramidal cuadrada de tajas verdes barnizadas. El edificio tiene dos niveles: en la planta baja hay una sala rectangular, con una antesala, que se abre al estanque por tres arcadas; en el primer piso (*menzeh*), una sala retranqueada con un gran balcón con balaustrada da al estanque y se prolonga también en una antesala con tres ventanas orientadas a la montaña.  
Al balcón se entra por una puerta cuadrada muy baja, probablemente para evitar que se viera el interior del *menzeh* desde el estanque y también para protegerlo del sol y el calor. Esta puerta está inserta en un arco ciego profundo, ornado con un motivo en piedra y enmarcado por un alfiz cuyo friso superior contiene la inscripción fundacional.  
En el interior del *menzeh*, la delicada decoración geométrica coloreada desprende alegría y frescura. Se limita a líneas de pintura de colores vivos que resaltan las aristas de la bóveda y los marcos de las ventanas. La pequeña escalera que conduce al piso desemboca en una terracita sobre la antesala del *menzeh*, desde la que se tienen impresionantes vistas del enorme vergel real, los campos y la sierra del Atlas.  
A pesar de su sencillez (o gracias a ella), el pabellón de Menara se ha convertido en uno de los emblemas de Marrakech.

Fue el soberano almohade Abd al-Mumin quien mandó plantar este vergel en los alrededores de Marrakech y construir el gran estanque (200 x 150 m). Más tarde, el lugar sirvió de morada estival a los soberanos meriníes y saadíes. Los alawíes repararon el muro, mejoraron los canales de agua de agua y construyeron un pabellón real, un edificio sobrio con gruesas paredes de ladrillo, tejado piramidal cuadrado con tejas verdes y un balcón con vistas al estanque. El interior está realzado con una ligera y colorista decoración geométrica, que desprende frescura y alegría.
dates: Estanque, siglo V de la Hégira / XI d. C.; pabellón, siglo X / XVI; monumento definitivo, siglo XI / XVII.
artist: El soberano almohade Abd al-Mumin (r. 524-558 / 1130-1163) y el alawí Sidi Mohamed ibn Abd al-Rahman (r. 1276-1290 / 1859-1873).
keywords: Residencia real, agua; ladrillo; piedra; decoración geométrica.
partner: Ministry of Culture,Directorate of Cultural Heritage

fr.name: Ménara.
description:
Le premier souverain almohade Abdelmoumen fit creuser à Marrakech deux grands bassins : un à l'extérieur de la ville, *sahrij el-bgar* (bassin des bovins), au profit des éleveurs de la région, et un dans son verger particulier, *sahrij al-menara*(bassin du phare – ou du minaret, peut être en référence à la Koutoubiya, le principal monument de la ville). Il y a lieu de noter, à cet égard, qu'al-Naciri, dans *al-Istiqsa*, appelle le minaret de la Koutoubiya s*awmaat al-manar* (le minaret du phare).  
  
Mais le bassin n'est désigné formellement sous le nom de Ménara que sous les Mérinides (Xe siècle H / XVIe siècle J.-C.).  
  
Les souverains saadiens se rendaient occasionnellement dans le pied-à-terre qu'ils construisirent en bordure du bassin, mais c'est à l'Alaouite Sidi Mohammed, fils du sultan Moulay Abderrahman (1238-1276 H / 1822-1859 J.-C.) et alors calife sultanien (vice-roi) à Marrakech, que l'on doit la remise en état du grand bassin almohade et la réhabilitation de la grande propriété royale.  
  
Il répara la muraille d'enceinte protégeant les 96 hectares de verger (1 200 x 800 m), améliora son approvisionnement en eau et fit construire, aux abords du grand bassin central de 200 m de long sur 150 m de large, un pavillon royal, un poste de garde et une jumenterie.  
  
Le pavillon royal se présente sous forme d'un édifice sobre et de dimensions modestes. Les murs en pierre sont épais avec des angles en briques, et la toiture pyramidale carrée est recouverte de tuiles vertes vernissées.  
  
Le pavillon est construit sur deux niveaux :  
  
– au rez-de-chaussée, une salle rectangulaire ouverte sur le bassin par trois arcades et se prolongeant à l'arrière par une antichambre ;  
  
– à l'étage (*menzeh*), une salle carrée en retrait avec un grand balcon à balustres donnant sur le bassin et se prolongeant aussi à l'arrière par une antichambre dotée de trois fenêtres ouvrant sur la montagne.  
  
Le balcon est doté d'une porte carrée particulièrement basse, probablement pour empêcher les personnes se trouvant autour du bassin de voir l'intérieur du *menzeh*, et pour en éviter l'ensoleillement et le réchauffement excessifs.  
  
Cette porte s'insère dans un profond arc aveugle décoré d'un motif en pierre et serti dans un encadrement dont le bandeau supérieur porte l'inscription épigraphique de fondation.  
  
L'intérieur du *menzeh* se pare d'une décoration géométrique légère et colorée, respirant la gaîté et la fraîcheur. Elle se limite à des filets de peinture de couleurs vives sur les arêtes de la voûte et autour des fenêtres.  
  
Le petit escalier menant à l'étage se prolonge jusqu'à une petite terrasse posée sur l'antichambre du *menzeh* et qui offre une vue imprenable sur le grand verger royal, sur l'arrière-pays et sur les monts de l'Atlas.  
  
En dépit (ou à cause) de sa simplicité, le pavillon de la Ménara est devenu un des emblèmes de Marrakech.

C'est le souverain almohade Abdelmoumen qui aménagea dans les environs de Marrakech ce verger doté d'un grand bassin (200 x 150 m) et qui servit de villégiature aux souverains mérinides et saadiens. C'est aux Alaouites que sont dues les réparations du mur d'enceinte, l'amélioration de l'approvisionnement en eau ainsi que la construction du pavillon royal, un édifice sobre à épais murs en brique, toiture pyramidale carrée couverte de tuiles vertes et balcon donnant sur le bassin.  
L'intérieur est rehaussé d'une décoration géométrique légère et colorée, respirant la fraîcheur et la gaieté.
dates: Ve siècle de l’Hégire (XIe siècle. J.-C.), pour le 1er bassin ; Xe siècle de l’Hégire (XVIe siècle. J.-C.), pour le 1er pavillon ; XIe siècle de l’Hégire (XVIIe siècle. J.-C.), pour le monument définitif.
keywords: résidence royale; eau; brique; pierre; décoration géométrique
partner: Ministry of Culture,Directorate of Cultural Heritage

de.name: Antonius-Altar (Hochaltar)
description: Eine für Bayern seltene vollständige Vergoldung hebt den in spätbarocken Formen gehaltenen Hochaltar von den farbig gefaßten Seitenaltären ab. In seinem Zentrum birgt er ein kostbares Altarblatt, das in klarer Zeichnung und gedämpften Farben eine der Hauptvisionen des Kirchenpatrons darstellt: die selige Umarmung des Christuskindes. Der Kunstimport aus Venedig ist bezeichnend für den an einer bedeutenden Alpentransitroute gelegenen Marktort Partenkirchen.

en.name: Altar of St. Anthony (High Altar)
description: With its Late Baroque shapes, the high altar contrasts strongly with the coloured side altars as it is fully gold-plated, a rare occurrence in Bavaria. In its centre, it bears a precious altarpiece. With a clear design and subdued colours, it depicts one of the main visions of the church patron: the blessed embrace of the Christ child. The imported art piece from Venice is characteristic for the market town of Partenkirchen as it is located near an important transit route in the Alps.
partner: University of Munich, Institute of Art History

en.name: 25 Syrian Piastres
short_description: This 25 piastres bank note was printed by Bradbury Wilkinson and Co (BWC) without a watermark.
keywords: Commerce; trade; Currency; Coins; coinage; Numismatics

en.name: Inauguration of the Grande Dixence dam
description: The water level is shown here rising behind the Grande Dixence dam near Sion (Valais), 18/07/1957; image from the feature produced by the Presse Diffusion Lausanne (PDL) photo agency. Constructed between 1950 and 1964, and commissioned between 1961 and 1965, the dam is located in the Valais commune of Hérémence. The crest of the dam lies at an altitude of 2,365 metres above sea level; this makes the dam Switzerland’s highest-lying construction. The dam wall is 285 metres high, making it the world’s tallest gravity dam. A symbol of Swiss engineering excellence, the Grande Dixence dam is the biggest producer of sustainable energy in Switzerland today. The 1950s and 1960s represented a period of economic and social advancement in Switzerland, and press photographers recorded the changes in full and in detail. Those working for the PDL and Actualités Suisses Lausanne (ASL) agencies focused particularly on the construction boom in the energy and transport sectors, and often also on the societal and political debates, conflicts, and repercussions associated with it. The Swiss National Museum acquired the PDL and ASL archives in 2007. Combined they number around six million images in the form of negatives, prints, and slides. Covering the years from 1937 to 1999, they record the most significant developments during the era of analogue press photography.
place: Switzerland, Grande Dixence dam in Hérémence near Sion (Valais)
keywords: Photography; Press Photography; Actualités Suisse Lausanne; Presse Diffusion Lausanne; Dam; Grande Dixence; Hérémence; Sion; Vallais
materials: Gelatin silver film, medium format negative, flexible film carrier
tags: Gelatin silver film, medium format negative, flexible film carrier

en.name: Vessel with tap
description: Made of copper using the forging technique, the vessel has a narrow, rounded mouth, a cylindrical, flattened shoulder, a wide belly, and a flat base. A copper pipe is fitted to the edge of the base. A single-spouted tap made of brass is soldered to the end of this pipe. The vessel consists of three sections, and the forging marks on the surface are distinct. Both interior and exterior are tin-plated, but have darkened over time due to oxidation. The lid is missing, and the rim shows nicks and cracks.
keywords: Water; copper; fountain; tap; Ottomans

en.name: Arab Room
description: The Arab Room shows the collections of the Marquis coming not only from Arabia but also from China, Japan, the Philippines, Turkey, Morocco and New Zealand. He collected and displayed these works, similar to other European palaces of the 19th Century, because his taste ran to oriental, exotic, foreign or ancestral cultures. This room was also known as *fumoir*, associated with smoking, essentially thought for masculine use. The ceiling is decorated with interlacing designs and six-pointed star in the middle, from which hangs a superb Arab lamp. There are kilims on the walls and carpets on the floor and furniture. Among all, we can also find arms and armouries, musical instruments and six scale-model reproducing walls and windows from some rooms of the Alhambra palace.
keywords: Decorations; Design; models; Alhambra

en.name: *Joseph and Potiphar’s Wife*
description:
The painting is a variation of the fresco painted by the artist in the Palazzo Mattei in Rome in 1615. Unlike that work, the figure of Potiphar's Wife is naked and the colours are based on tones of red and ochre. The different hypotheses advanced by scholars include the possibility that it is an approximate replica of the Mettei fresco completed for Scipione Borghese. During the pontificate of Paul V, the artist received a series of extraordinary commissions, including the decoration of the Loggia delle Benedizioni in the Vatican Basilica, and part of the frescos in the Sala Regia in the Quirinal. These were followed by commissions from Cardinal Scipione himself, such as the decoration and fresco at Villa Mondragone in Frascati near Rome, and the vault of the loggia at Villa Borghese.  
The canvas shows a well-known episode from the Old Testament (Genesis, 39, 7–18) extolling the chastity of Joseph, courted by the wife of Potiphar, the head of the Pharaoh's guards. The woman, offended by Joseph's rejection, is left holding his tunic in her hands when he escapes; she accuses him unjustly and has him thrown into gaol. During his imprisonment, Joseph becomes known for his ability to interpret dreams and is freed immediately.  
The highly contrasting *chiaroscuro* and the Caravaggesque ascending layering of colour, associate the painting with the work of the painter Simon Vouet in the 1630s.  
Joseph's almost running pose and the foreshortening of the raised right hand are particularly noteworthy. A contrasting sense of movement is provided by the body of the woman, who will not release him and is pulling in the opposite direction. She is fully illuminated by a beam of light that leaves Joseph's face almost in shadow. Skilful compositional knowledge is evident in the essential nature of the elements, which emerge from the darkness in a notably theatrical style.

It is Lanfranco who carries out one of the first examples of Baroque painting in Rome for Cardinal Scipione: *The Council of the Gods* in the loggia of Villa Borghese. The biblical theme represented in this painting celebrates the virtue of chastity. The canvas, a replica of the fresco in Palazzo Mattei in Rome, is a play of light with, clearly, theatrical inspiration.
keywords: Christian themes; symbol; chiaroscuro; movement; theatre; Simon Vouet; French painting

it.name: *Giuseppe e la moglie di Putifarre*
description:
Il dipinto rappresenta una variante dell’affresco eseguito nel 1615 dall’artista nel palazzo Mattei a Roma. Rispetto a quest’ultimo la figura della moglie di Putifarre è nuda, le tonalità cromatiche giocate sui colori del rosso e dell’ocra. Tra le diverse ipotesi avanzate dagli studiosi, vi è quella che si tratti di una replica variata dell’affresco Mattei eseguita per Scipione Borghese. Sotto il pontificato di Paolo V l’artista ricevette infatti una serie di straordinarie commissioni, tra cui la decorazione della Loggia delle Benedizioni nella Basilica Vaticana e parte degli affreschi della Sala Regia del Quirinale. A questi fecero seguito gli incarichi dello stesso cardinale Scipione, come la decorazione ad affresco di Villa Mondragone a Frascati presso Roma o della volta della Loggia di Villa Borghese.  
La tela raffigura un celebre episodio dell’Antico Testamento (Genesi, 39, 7-18), in cui viene esaltata la castità di Giuseppe, insidiato dalla moglie di Putifarre, capo delle guardie del faraone. La donna, offesa dal rifiuto di Giuseppe, che nel fuggire le lascia nelle mani la sua tunica, lo accuserà ingiustamente facendolo gettare in carcere. Durante la prigionia Giuseppe diverrà celebre per la capacità divinatoria nella lettura dei sogni e sarà in seguito liberato.  
Il chiaroscuro fortemente contrastato e la stesura del colore di ascendenza caravaggesca avvicinano il dipinto alle opere realizzate dal pittore Simon Vouet nel terzo decennio del XVII secolo. Da notare lo slancio della figura di Giuseppe, quasi in corsa, con lo scorcio della mano destra sollevata. Il senso di movimento è impresso, per contrasto, dal corpo della donna che non si rassegna a lasciarlo e agisce nella direzione opposta, illuminato in pieno da un fascio di luce che lascia quasi in ombra il volto di Giuseppe. Una notevole sapienza compositiva traspare nell’essenzialità degli elementi, che emergono dall’oscurità con un gusto spiccatamente teatrale.

Lanfranco è il pittore che realizzò per il Cardinale Scipione uno dei primi esempi della pittura barocca a Roma, *Il concilio degli dei* nella loggia di Villa Borghese. Il tema biblico rappresentato in questo dipinto celebra la virtù della castità. La tela, una replica l'affresco di Palazzo Mattei a Roma, è un gioco di luce con una chiara ispirazione teatrale.
keywords: Tematiche cristiane; simbolo; chiaroscuro; movimento; teatro; Simon Vouet; pittura francese

en.name: Dagger
short_description: Silver knife with silver handle and niello decoration on the front; metal on the backside and four Turkish coins along the edge of the sheath; a name (‘Jomaah Ali’) is inscribed on the blade of the dagger. This object is functional and can be used in everyday activities, but at the same time it is a prestigious object that every Bedouin man must have. The most common types of daggers in Jordan are the Yemeni dagger, the Hijazi and other local types.
holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
keywords: niello decoration; sheath; blade
materials: Silver, iron; casting, incised and niello
partner: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery

en.name: The monuments in the Hippodrome surrounded by protective fences
short_description: Robertson’s Istanbul photographs are concerned primarily with the city’s historical monuments. They reveal the city’s magnificent Byzantine and Ottoman structures from different angles and with close-ups taken in an approach that is usually quite aesthetic. A frequently employed device in Robertson's photographs is the inclusion of the one or more human figures in the foreground – indeed, this is something of a trademark of Robertson’s work. In this photo, the monuments in the Hippodrome are surrounded by protective fences.
keywords: Photography, ?stanbul, History of architecture
partner: Vehbi Koç Foundation Sadberk Hanim Museum

ar.name: جزء من قاع إناء من الزجاج.
description:
القطعة عبارة عن جزء من قاع إناء من الزجاج الشفاف المزخرف بالبريق المعدني البني. وتتكون الزخرفة من رسم لوعل ذي قرنين طويلين يجري متجهاً نحو اليمين، ويحمل في فمه غصناً ينتهي بورقة شجر على شكل قلب. وتزين الأرضية أغصان تشبه تلك التي يحملها الوعل. وتظهر في الرسم تفاصيل صدر وبطن وفخذ الوعل بأسلوب مجسم.  
  
ويعتبر الزجاج المزخرف بالبريق المعدني ابتكاراً جديداً عرفته مصر منذ القرن الثاني الهجري / الثامن الميلادي، وازدهر في العصر الفاطمي حيث نفذت على الزجاج رسومات حيوانات وطيور ونباتات بنفس الأساليب المستخدمة في الرسم على الخزف الفاطمي ذي البريق المعدني. وتوجد قطع من الزجاج في متحف بناكي في أثينا تحمل توقيع " سعد" الخزاف الفاطمي الذي اشتهر في أواخر القرن الخامس وأوائل القرن السادس الهجري / أواخر القرن الحادي عشر وأوائل القرن الثاني عشر الميلادي. وهكذا، فإن الخزافين الفاطميين قد نقلوا أساليبهم الزخرفية في استخدام البريق المعدني إلى القطع الزجاجية.  
  
بالإضافة إلى زخرفة الزجاج بالبريق المعدني، عرفت مصر أنواعاً أخرى من الزخرفة على الزجاج مثل الزخرفة بالخيوط الزجاجية الرفيعة المضافة الملتفة حول الإناء، والزخارف المقطوعة بالحفرالبارز، والزخارف بالختم وبالقطع الزجاجية المضافة. كما عرفت الزجاج السميك الذي يشبه البلور الصخري ويزخرف بالقطع.
هذه قطعة من قاع إناء، من الزجاج الشفَّاف، وتُعتبر نموذجاً للزجاج المزخرف بأسلوب البريق المعدني، وهو ابتكار جديد عُرف بمصر، في بداية العصر الإسلامي، تقليداً للخزف المزخرف بهذا الأسلوب.
keywords: إناء؛ بريق معدني؛ زجاج؛ زخرفة حيوانية؛ زخرفة نباتية.

en.name: Fragment of a glass vessel.
description:
Part of the base of a transparent glass vessel decorated with brown metallic lustre. Its ornamentation consists of the depiction of a mountain-goat or deer with two long horns. The animal is seen running towards the right, and carrying in its mouth a branch that ends in a heart-shaped leaf; branches similar to that being carried by the animal adorn the background. The depiction reveals details of the torso and the shanks of the animal in a naturalistic style.  
Glass decorated with metallic lustre is considered to have been an innovation known in Egypt since the AH 2nd / AD 8th century which flourished during the Fatimid period, where paintings of animals, birds and plants were produced on glass, in the same style as those used on ceramics with metallic lustre. At the Benaki Museum in Athens, there are pieces of glass, which carry the signature of 'Sa'ad', a Fatimid ceramist who was famous during the latter half of the AH 5th / AD 11th century and the beginning of the AH 6th / AD 12th century. Fatimid ceramists had, therefore, transferred styles of decoration in metallic lustre on ceramics to glass.  
In addition to decorating glass with metallic lustre, Egypt was known for other kinds of decoration on glass such as ornamentation with thin glass filaments, which were added and then pressed around the vessel; cut-glass decorations in high relief; stamped decoration and a method of glass-appliqué in high relief. Thick glass, which closely resembles rock-crystal, was also popular and was decorated by cutting the design into the glass in deep recesses.

A piece from the base of a transparent glass vessel decorated in metallic lustre, a new technique that became known in Egypt at the beginning of the Islamic era in imitation of lustre ceramics and which flourished under the Fatimids.
keywords: Vessel; metallic lustre; glass; animal decoration; vegetal decoration

es.name: Fragmento de recipiente de vidrio.
description:
Parte de la base de un recipiente de vidrio transparente decorado en reflejo metálico de color marrón. Está adornado con una imagen de una cabra montés o un ciervo con dos largos cuernos. El animal está corriendo hacia la derecha y lleva en la boca una rama con una hoja cordiforme en su extremo, similar a las ramas que aparecen en el fondo del dibujo. Algunos detalles del torso y las patas del animal están representados con un estilo naturalista.  
El vidrio decorado en reflejo metálico se considera una innovación conocida en Egipto desde el siglo II / VIII y que floreció durante el periodo fatimí, en el que se dibujaba a animales, aves y plantas sobre vidrio con el mismo estilo que se utilizaba en la cerámica de reflejo metálico. En el museo Benaki de Atenas existen piezas de vidrio firmadas por Saad, un famoso ceramista fatimí de finales del siglo V / XI y principios del siglo VI / XII. Los ceramistas fatimíes comenzaron a emplear en objetos de vidrio los estilos decorativos de la cerámica de reflejo metálico.  
Aparte del reflejo metálico, Egipto era conocido por otros tipos de decoración sobre vidrio, como la ornamentación con finos filamentos de cristal que se adherían al recipiente, el vidrio tallado en altorrelieve, la decoración estampada y las aplicaciones en altorrelieve. También se usaba con frecuencia un tipo de vidrio más grueso, parecido al cristal de roca, que se decoraba rebajándolo para grabar dibujos.

Fragmento de la base de un recipiente de vidrio transparente con reflejo metálico, un tipo de decoración que surgió en Egipto a principios de la era islámica emulando a la cerámica de reflejo metálico.
dates: Siglo V de la Hégira / XI d. C.
keywords: recipiente; reflejo metálico; vidrio; decoración animal; decoración vegetal.

fr.name: Fragment de récipient en verre.
description:
Fragment du fond d'un récipient en verre transparent décoré au lustre métallique brun. Le décor représente une gazelle ou un cerf à deux longues cornes, courant vers la droite et tenant dans sa gueule une branche terminée par une feuille en forme de cœur. Des branches similaires ornent le fond. L'animal est traité dans un style réaliste.  
Le verre à décor de lustre métallique est une innovation apparue en égypte au IIe siècle H (VIIIe siècle J.-C)., qui se développa au cours de la période fatimide. La peinture sur verre reprit des thème identiques à ceux des céramiques lustrées : divers animaux, oiseaux et végétaux. Des pièces en verre conservées au musée Benaki d'Athènes portent la signature de Sa'ad, célèbre céramiste fatimide de la seconde moitié du Ve siècle H (XIe siècle J.-C.) et du début du VIe siècle H (XIIe siècle J.-C.), ce qui montre que les décorateurs fatimides utilisant le lustre pouvaient transférer leur technique de la céramique au verre.  
Par ailleurs, l'égypte était connue pour d'autres types de décor sur verre, comme l'application de minces filaments de verre pressés sur le corps de l'objet, décors taillés en haut relief dans le verre, décors estampés, ainsi qu'une méthode d'appliqué en verre en haut relief. Le verre épais, ressemblant au cristal de roche, était également populaire. Il pouvait être décoré de motifs taillés en profondeur.

Fragment de la base d'un récipient en verre transparent avec un décor de lustre métallique, innovation technique qui commença à être connue en Égypte au début de la période islamique en imitation des céramiques lustrées qui fleurirent sous les Fatimides.
dates: Ve siècle de l’Hégire (XIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: Récipients usuels ; lustre métallique ; verre ; décoration animale ; décoration végétale

en.name: Portrait of Hajj Husayn Bayham
short_description: Born in Beirut in 1833, Hajj Husayn Bayham studied under great masters such as Shaykh 'Abd Allah Khalid and Shaykh Muhammad al-Hut. He mainly worked in public posts, including the council of the wilayet of Saida, the tribunal of commerce and the municipal council. He also wrote poetry in his spare time and had a vast collection of works in his private library. In 1878 he was elected to represent Beirut in the Ottoman parliament. He died in 1881.
keywords: Poetry; Commerce; Tribunal; Scientific

en.name: Rich drawing
short_description: Portrait of a standing male Yezidi from Sinjar. Claudius Rich made observations and drawings not only of sites but also of people. Early travellers often studied the customs and costumes of local peoples, as well as drawing landscapes or mapping territories. There was no such thing as a professional archaeologist yet.

en.name: Bergama rug
description:
Bergama is a town in western Anatolia. Rugs woven there are usually square, and their design geometric. Most are decorated with five medallions: square, rectangular or polygonal in the centre and four others near the corners of the central field. Such a composition is a distant reflection of the so-called “Holbein” carpets from the 15th and 16th centuries.  
The Kraków Bergama rug is woven from wool using a very warm colour palette, predominantly shades of ochre and yellow, with the addition of light-orange, yellowish green, dark-blue and greyish violet. The fleece is high and adds an impression of softness to the geometric ornament. In the centre of the ochre field there is an octagonal white medallion surrounded by hook motifs with a colourful rosette inside. The white surface of the medallion is decorated with a meander-like ornament, which looks engraved – an effect achieved by the light-brown fleece being cut lower than the white fleece. In the corners rest smaller medallions with ornamental crosses constructed of triangles. Between the medallions are leafy stalks with tulips. Small roses and other minute designs, difficult to recognise, also appear on the main field. The main border is filled with tulips inscribed inside squares. The Kraków rug is an attractive example of the style typical of the Bergama carpet-weaving centre.
keywords: Bergama; Anatolia; prayer rug; tulip; wool
materials: Wool (warp, weft, pile); symmetrically knotted pile (Turkish knot)

en.name: *Arabs of the Desert*
short_description: The constant movement of large Bedouin confederations regularly impacted on the history of the Middle East, in particular when it affected settled societies and cities.This print provides much interesting detail about the dress of the Bedouin at the time David Roberts visited the Near East in 1838/9. The individual in the foreground wears a white turban and short gown with belt, a dark red jacket and a voluminous, all-enveloping blue cloak. His legs remain uncovered, and he wears simple leather sandals on his feet. A formidable dagger or khanjar in its sheath is secured in his belt, and he carries a long slender gun through a sling. The bullets for the gun appear to be secured in an ammunition belt strapped diagonally across his chest. In the background, four male figures wearing striped headscarfs and cloaks as well as short white gowns and holdings lances appear on the right. On the left, a bedouin leads his camels away. The inscription states: *Arabs of the tribe of Benisaid, Feb. 17th 1839*.
holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
keywords: khanjar

description: إن الشكل المختلف للخزف الأزرق والأبيض يبدو أنه تطور في كرمان : و النماذج الشكلية للشخوص كانت تحفر بتقنية السغرافيتو في زجاج أزرق مطلي بشكل ثخين. والرصيعتين المملوءتين بأرابيسك هما الزخرفة الوحيدة على الزبدية وتتجليان بشكل جميل عبر التباين اللوني المميز. وبعض القطع الباقية لهذه المجموعة من الخزف هي مميزة بسبب دقة شكل التزيين ويفترض أيضا أن الخلفية الزرقاء تمثل السماء.

en.name: Bowl
description: A special variant of blue-and-white ceramic seems to have evolved in Kerman: frugal patterns were incised in sgraffito technique into a thickly coated blue glaze. The two medallions filled with Arabesques are the sole ornaments on the bowl, beautifully enhanced through the distinct colour contrast. The few preserved pieces of this ceramic group are remarkable for their precise form of decoration. It is also assumed that the blue background represents the sky.

en.name: Tray with Oriental landscape

The different clothes of the man on the right who is turning his back may be identified with those of a Turkish warrior or janissary.
