en.name: Vase
short_description: A copper tin-coated enamelled vase decorated with birds, floral and Arabic script on a dark blue coloured base with orange, red and green. The Jordanian economy relied on trade and crafts. New waves of people began to settle in Jordan for the purpose of trade and crafts. This object reflects the diverse population composition of Jordan in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It also demonstrates personal attire, fashion, local costumes and rites.
holder: Jordan Folklore Museum, Department of Antiquities
keywords: Copper tin; coated; enamelled; birds; floral decoration; Arabic script
materials: Copper, tin niello; casting, carving and niello

en.name: Church of St. Francis, Oporto
names: Igreja Monumento de São Francisco, Oporto
description: A Gothic mendicant church with three aisles, covered with gilded carving and Baroque imagery. In the main body of the church the gradual installation of various altars and retables culminate in blanketing it entirely and changing it completely, giving it a totally Baroque décor. The carving and gilding awaken the senses; not even the ceiling veins can be seen as they are covered by rich carved ornamentation. This is due in part to a well-known characteristically Baroque programmatic principle: if the outside of the building corresponds to the body, the inside is the expression of the soul enriched by God's gifts.

A Gothic church, of the “mendicant” type that was commissioned by the order of St. Francis. It was built during the 13th and14th centuries and entirely covered in gilt carving in several stages throughout the 17th and 18th centuries.
artist: Order of St. Francis, the third order of the St. Francis Brotherhood from Oporto

Architectectural design: Francisco do Couto e Azevedo [n.d.]; sculptors: António Gomes [n.d.]; Filipe da Silva (active 1718–?); woodcarvers: Luís Pereira da Costa (active 1724–?), Manuel Carneiro Adão (active 1719–?), Manuel Pereira da Costa Noronha (active 1750–1751), Manuel da Costa Andrade (active 1740–1743), Francisco Pereira Campanhã (active 1764–?)
history: Installation of the altarpieces and the carving in general began in the 17th century and lasted until the end of the 18th. The presence of several period altarpieces and carving, mostly of the Baroque style from the first half of the 18th-century culminate in a harmonious visual impact. This variety  was caused by an  increase of orders because Oporto had a vibrant and wealthy bourgeoisie, organized in several brotherhoods, willing to  finance art works in this period. The Church of St Francis stands nowadays as a museum of northern carving. In the 19th century with the extinction of the religious orders and after a violent fire in 1833, right after the siege of Oporto, the convent started to decline, was burnt down and the church was used for instance as a Customs warehouse. The Church of St. Francis was classified as a National Monument in 1910, being now part of the Historic Centre of Oporto. It became an Unesco World Heritage in 1996 .
keywords: Gilt wood carving, Oporto, Order of St. Francis
tags: Gilt wood carving, Oporto, Order of St. Francis
partner: Institute for the Administration of Architectural and Archaeological Heritage -  IGESPAR

pt.name: *Igreja Monumento de São Francisco*
names: Igreja de São Francisco de Assis
description: Igreja gótica mendicante, de três naves, revestida, no período barroco, com talha dourada e imaginária barroca. Em S. Francisco do Porto assiste-se à gradual instalação, no corpo do templo, de vários altares e retábulos que virão a forrar inteiramente a igreja, transformando-a por completo e concedendo-lhe uma roupagem plenamente barroca. Deflagrando os sentidos através da talha e do seu douramento, nem mesmo as nervuras do tecto são deixadas à vista, sendo, pelo contrário, revestidas pela ornamentação rica da talha. De algum modo, isso deve-se a um princípio programático já conhecido e caracteristicamente barroco: se o exterior do edifício corresponde ao corpo, o seu interior é a expressão da alma, enriquecida pelos dons de Deus. Daí a sua densa ornamentação e, neste caso, a própria ocultação da sua estrutura arquitectónica, numa objectiva manifestação corpórea que, assim, é resgatada da sua condição material para passar à ordem espiritual das coisas.

Igreja gótica, do tipo “mendicante”, da Ordem de S. Francisco, erguida nos séculos XIII-XIV; revestimento integral de talha dourada durante os séculos XVII a XVIII, através de diversas campanhas de obras.
dates: Séculos XIII-XIV (estrutura); séculos XVII-XVIII (decoração em talha dourada)
artist: Ordem de S. Francisco; Ordem Terceira da Irmandade de S. Francisco, do Porto; irmandades e confrarias portuenses.

Arquitecto: Francisco do Couto e Azevedo [n.d.]; escultores: António Gomes [n.d.]; Filipe da Silva (activo 1718–n.d.); escultores: Luís Pereira da Costa (activo 1724–n.d.), Manuel Carneiro Adão (activo 1719–n.d.), Manuel Pereira da Costa Noronha (activo 1750–1751), Manuel da Costa Andrade (activo 1740–1743); entalhador: Francisco Pereira Campanhã (activo1764–n.d.).
history:
As campanhas de obras de instalação da retabulística e da talha em geral estendem-se desde inícios do século XVII até finais do século XVIII. Registe-se que, apesar da diversificação de encomendas e, até, da coexistência, em determinados períodos, de retábulos e talha de épocas e de estilos distintos, veio a dar-se como que uma espécie de unificação estilística, com uma concentração de encomendas na primeira metade do século XVIII. O facto tem a ver com o próprio fulgor da cidade do Porto num período chave de enriquecimento burguês, com diversas irmandades a intervirem com encomendas de prestígio. Como se percebe, a Igreja de S. Francisco actua, hoje, como um verdadeiro museu da talha dourada nortenha e da imaginária, com alguns dos seus principais autores ligados ao enriquecimento do templo.  
No século XIX, com a extinção das ordens religiosas e um violento incêndio ocorrido em 1833, logo a seguir ao cerco do Porto pelas tropas miguelistas, o convento entrou em declínio, foi incendiado e a igreja foi ocupada para diversos fins, como o de armazém da Alfândega da cidade.  
A Igreja de S. Francisco foi classificada como monumento nacional no ano de 1910 e, estando inserida no centro histórico da cidade do Porto, passou a ser Património Mundial da Unesco desde 1996.
keywords: Talha dourada, Porto, Ordem de São Francisco de Assis.
tags: Talha dourada, Porto, Ordem de São Francisco de Assis.

ar.name: قاع إناء.
description:
القطعة عبارة عن قاع إناء من الفخار المطلي بالمينا يزخرفه من الداخل رنك عصوي البولو الذي يرمز إلى رياضة البولو التي اهتم بها المماليك خاصة في عصر السلطان الناصر محمد بن قلاوون الذي حكم ثلاث مرات في السنوات 693 – 694هـ / 1294 – 1295م، و 698 – 708 هـ / 1299 – 1309م، و 709 – 741 هـ / 1309 – 1340 م. وأطلق على صاحب رنك عصوي البولو اسم "الجوكندار"، وهي كلمة من شقين: الأول هو "جوكن" ويعني بالفارسية عصوي البولو، والثاني "دار" وتعني حامل أو صاحب. ويظهر هذا الرنك على كثير من التحف الإسلامية المصنوعة من الفخار أو النحاس المكفت أو الزجاج، كما يظهر على الأنسجة وعلى أشياء أخرى. والرنك هو الشعار الذي يرمز لوظيفة معين. واستخدم السلاطين والأمراء الرنوك منذ القرن 12م على مبانيهم وتحفهم وأشيائهم الأخرى للدلالة على ملكيتهم لها. وقد انتهى نظام الرنوك الوظيفية بانتهاء عصر المماليك.  
  
ويعتبر الفخار المطلي بالمينا من المواد الأكثر استخداماً في صناعة القطع التي استخدمت بكثرة في بيوت أمراء المماليك. وربما يكون هذا هو السبب في كثرة استخدام الرنوك - إلى جانب الكتابات التي تحمل ألقاب الأمراء والرسومات الحيوانية والهندسية والنباتية - في زخرفة هذه القطع.

الرنك هو الشارة التي اتخذها السلاطين والأمراء على أدواتهم وعمائرهم، للدلالالة على وظائفهم. والرنك الموجود على هذه القطعة، المتبقية من قاع إناء فخاري، وعليه طبقة من المينا، يشير إلى أن صاحبه كان المشرف على لعبة الكرة والصولجان (الجوكندار).
keywords: إناء؛ رنك؛ فخار؛ مينا.
materials: عجينة فخار مائلة إلى الحمرة مغطاة ببطانة بيضاء طليت بالمينا البني.
tags: عجينة فخار مائلة إلى الحمرة مغطاة ببطانة بيضاء طليت بالمينا البني.

en.name: Fragment from a container.
description:
This piece appears to be the bottom of a glazed pottery container, which is decorated on the interior by two polo-sticks, symbolising polo, a sport that the Mamluks were deeply interested in, especially during the period of Sultan al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qalawun who ruled three times: AH 693–4 / AD 1294–5; AH 698–708 / AD 1299–1309; AH 709–41 / AD 1309–40. Amongst the Mamluk officers, the master of the two polo-sticks blazon was called 'al-Jokandar', 'Jokan' meaning in Persian (Farsi) two polo-sticks, and 'dar' meaning bearer or master. This blazon appears on many Islamic objects made from ceramic, inlaid copper, glass or textiles as well as other mediums. The blazon was an emblem symbolising a specific office and had been used by *amirs* and sultans since the AH 6th / AD 12th century on their buildings, possessions and other objects as a means of indicating their ownership of them. The system of office blazons came to an end with the fall of the Mamluk dynasty in AH 923 / AD 1517.  
Glazed pottery is considered to be the most prolific medium used to make objects for the residences of Mamluk *amir*s. This might be the reason for the abundant use of blazons – in addition to inscriptions which bear the titles of *amir*s and vegetal, animal and geometric motifs – in the decoration of such pieces as this.

The blazon is the symbol which sultans and amirs put on their possessions and buildings to indicate their official posts. The blazon on this fragment from the bottom of a clay vessel glazed with a layer of enamel indicates that its owner was the master of the polo game ('al-Jokandar').
keywords: Container; blazon; ceramic; glaze; pottery
materials: Reddish pottery paste; painted in white slip and glazed in brown.
tags: painted in white slip and glazed in brown.

es.name: Fragmento de recipiente.
description:
Este fragmento parece ser el fondo de un recipiente de cerámica vidriada, decorado por dentro con dos palos de polo que simbolizan este deporte, muy popular entre los mamelucos, sobre todo durante el sultanato de al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qalawun (r. 693-944 / 1294-95, 698-708 / 1299-1309 y 709-741 / 1309-1340). Entre los oficiales mamelucos, el propietario del blasón de los dos palos de polo era conocido como *al-yokandar*, porque en persa (farsi) *yokar* significa 'dos palos de polo' y *dar*, 'portador' o 'maestro''. Este blasón aparece en muchos objetos islámicos de cerámica, cobre con incrustaciones, vidrio, telas y otros materiales. Era un emblema que simbolizaba un cargo concreto y los emires y sultanes lo utilizaron desde el siglo VI / XII en los edificios, en sus pertenencias y en otros objetos para indicar que eran de su propiedad. El sistema de blasones asociados a los cargos dejó de usarse con la caída de la dinastía mameluca en 923 / 1517.  
La cerámica vidriada fue el material más utilizado para fabricar objetos destinados a las residencias de los emires mamelucos. Tal vez sea esta la razón de el uso de blasones fuera tan habitual (junto con inscripciones con los títulos de los emires y motivos vegetales, animales y geométricos) en la decoración de este tipo de piezas.

El blasón es el símbolo que sultanes y emires colocaban en sus posesiones y edificios para indicar sus cargos oficiales. El de este fragmento de un recipiente de cerámica vidriada indica que su propietario era un maestro de polo *(yokandar)*.
dates: Siglo IX de la Hégira / XV d. C.
keywords: Recipiente; blasón; cerámica; vidriado; alfarería.
materials: Cerámica rojiza coloreada con barbotina blanca y vidriada en color marrón.
tags: Cerámica rojiza coloreada con barbotina blanca y vidriada en color marrón.

fr.name: Fragment de récipient.
description: Ce tesson semble être le fond d'un récipient en poterie vernissée ; il est décoré, à l'intérieur, de deux cannes de polo, symbole d'un sport auquel s'intéressaient beaucoup les Mamelouks, en particulier sous le sultan al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qalawun, qui régna à trois reprises (693-694 H / 1294-1295 J.-C. ; 698-708 H / 1299-1309 J.-C. ; 709-741 H / 1309-1340 J.-C.). Parmi les dignitaires mamelouks, le détenteur du blason des deux cannes de polo était appelé *al-Jokandar*, *Jokan* signifiant en farsi “deux cannes de polo” et *dar* porteur ou maître. Ce blason est présent sur de nombreux objets islamiques en céramique, cuivre incrusté, verre, textiles et autres supports. Il symbolisait une charge spécifique et était utilisé par les émirs et les sultans depuis le VIe H (XIIe siècle J.-C.) sur leurs bâtiments et leurs biens pour indiquer leur propriété. Le système des blasons de charge disparut avec la dynastie mamelouke en 923 H / 1517 J.-C. La poterie vernissée était l'un matériaux les plus utilisés dans la fabrication d'objets usuels pour les résidences des émirs, d'où la présence abondante de blasons accompagnés d'inscriptions de titres et de motifs végétaux, animaux et géométriques sur ces objets.

Le blason est le symbole que les émirs et les sultans apposaient sur leurs biens et leurs bâtiments pour indiquer leurs fonctions officielles. Le blason sur ce fragment provenant du fond d'un récipient en terre vernissée avec une couche d'émail indique que son propriétaire était le maître du jeu de polo (*al-Jokandar*).
dates: IXe siècle de l’Hégire (XVe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: Récipients ; blasons ; céramiques ; vernis ; poterie
materials: Terre cuite rougeâtre peinte à la barbotine blanche et vernissée en brun.
tags: Terre cuite rougeâtre peinte à la barbotine blanche et vernissée en brun.

ar.name: تميمة ’عين الحسد‘.
description:
'عين الحسد'، تميمة زرقاء مصنوعة على شكل قرص من الزجاج الأزرق المقولب، ومزخرفة بسلسلة ملوَّنة من الدوائر متناقصة الحجم: الأصفر، فالأبيض، ثم نقطة سوداء في المركز. ربما تكون خرزة من ضمن نسق من الخرزات المشابهة، لأنها مثقوبة في أحد جوانبها كي تنظم في سلك. من المحتمل أن هذا النوع من 'العين' الزجاجية كان يركَّب على الملابس أو أغطية الرأس.  
تسمَّى العيون الزرق، بحسب المعتقد الإسلامي الشائع، عين الحسود؛ حيث يتقلدها المرء كي تطرد القوى السلبية وتعكسها على عيون الجناة الحاسدين، وبهذه الطريقة تحمي مرتديها من عواقب الحسد التي يُعتقد أنها تسبب المرض أو المصيبة.  
إن عيوناً كهذه يمكن أن تُصنع تقريباً على شكل هذه الخرزة، أو يمكن أن تُرسم بدقة ونوعية تدلاَّن على مهارة الصنع، حسبما وُجدت في مجوهرات الذهب أو الفضة؛ لكن النوعية ليس لها تأثير على القوة الحمائية. يعتقد أيضاً أن الخرزات الزرق البسيطة تلعب دوراً حمائياً مماثلاً، وتُستخدم أحياناً عوضاً عن عين الحسد.

من معتقدات مسلمي الشرق الأوسط الشعبية، أن العيون الزرقاء حسودة من جهة، وقادرة على ردع الحسد من جهة ثانية. وهذه العين الزجاجية الزرقاء تُحمل للوقاية من تأثيرات الغيرة والحسد، التي قد تفضي إلى فقدان موضوع الغيرة، أو إلى المرض، والكوارث.
holder: متحف وصالة فنون كيلفينغروف، متاحف غلاسكو.
dates: أواخر القرن الثالث عشر- أوائل الرابع عشر / أواخر التاسع عشر- أوائل العشرين.
keywords: حلية؛ قطعة ذات استعمال ديني؛ زخرفة تصويرية.

en.name: ‘Eye of envy’ amulet.
description:
A blue 'eye of envy' made of a moulded, blue glass disc decorated with a series of diminishing circles of yellow, then white, with a black spot at the centre. Probably a bead from a string of other similar beads, it has a hole though the side for threading. This type of glass 'eye' might also have been sewn on to garments and headdresses.  
  
Within Islamic popular belief blue eyes are thought to be envious eyes; the eye of envy is worn to repel such negative power by reflecting back to the perpetrator their own envy, thereby protecting the wearer from the effects of jealousy, thought to cause illness or disaster.  
  
Such eyes can be crudely made like this bead, or can be drawn with accuracy and quality of craftsmanship, as found in jewellery made of gold or silver; the quality does not affect the protective power. Plain blue beads are also thought to play a similar protective role, and are sometimes used in place of an eye of envy.

In popular Middle Eastern Islamic belief blue eyes are thought to be both envious and to have the ability to repel envy. This blue glass eye is worn to protect the bearer from the effects of jealousy, which may cause the loss of what is being envied or illness or disaster.
holder: Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum, Glasgow Museums.
dates: Hegira, late 13th–early 14th century / AD late 19th–early 20th century.
keywords: Jewellery; religious objects; figurative decoration; talisman

es.name: Amuleto “ojo de la envidia”.
description:
Este “ojo de la envidia” está realizado en un disco de vidrio azul moldeado y decorado con círculos concéntricos menguantes de color amarillo y blanco, y un punto negro en el centro. Se trata, probablemente, de una cuenta, ya que en un lado tiene un agujero para ser ensartado. Este tipo de ojos de vidrio se cosía también a prendas de vestir y tocados.  
Según una creencia popular islámica, los ojos azules eran “envidiosos”, y estos amuletos se llevaban precisamente para repeler tal poder negativo reflejando contra el envidioso su propia envidia y protegiendo de este modo al portador de las enfermedades y desastres que, se creía, causaban los celos.  
La calidad de su elaboración no determinaba su poder protector, por lo que estos ojos podían ser tanto piezas toscas (esta es un ejemplo) como objetos artesanalmente refinados (como los que adornan joyas de oro y plata). A veces se utilizaban cuentas de color azul liso en vez de estos ojos, ya que tenían el mismo poder protector.

Según una creencia popular de Oriente Medio, los ojos azules son al mismo tiempo “envidiosos” y protectores contra la envidia. Este ojo azul de vidrio se llevaba para proteger a su portador de los celos, que podían causar la pérdida de aquello por lo que se es envidiado, enfermedades o desastres.
holder: Galería de Arte y Museo Kelvingrove, Museos de Glasgow.
dates: Finales del siglo XIII–principios XIV de la Hégira / XIX-XX d. C.
keywords: joyería; objetos religiosos; decoración figurativa

fr.name: Amulette apotropaïque contre le mauvais œil (“œil bleu”).
description:
“Œil bleu” fait d'un disque de verre moulé bleu auquel se superposent deux disques de verre jaune et blanc de diamètres plus petits, le tout surmonté d'un point noir central. Il s'agit probablement d'une pièce appartenant à un collier composé d'éléments similaires puisqu'il présente un trou latéral pour le passage d'un fil. Ce type d'œil de verre pouvait également être cousu sur des vêtements ou des coiffures.  
Selon la croyance islamique populaire, les yeux bleus sont des yeux envieux. L'œil de l'envie ou œil bleu se porte pour se protéger de ce sentiment négatif en renvoyant à l'autre sa propre envie, et en protégeant ainsi le porteur des effets de la jalousie, qui pourrait provoquer l'arrivée d'une maladie ou d'un événement funeste.  
Ces “yeux” peuvent être de fabrication grossière, comme ce modèle, mais aussi dessinés avec précision et réalisés avec art comme dans certaines pièces de joaillerie en or ou argent. Leur pouvoir de protection n'est pas lié à la qualité de la fabrication. On trouve également des disques entièrement bleus qui devaient jouer un rôle similaire et pouvaient parfois remplacer l'œil de l'envie.

Dans la croyance islamique populaire du Moyen-Orient, les yeux bleus sont censés être à la fois envieux et avoir la capacité de repousser l’envie. Cet œil de verre bleu est porté pour protéger des effets de la jalousie, qui peut provoquer la perte de ce qui est envié, la maladie ou un évènement funeste.
holder: Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum, Glasgow Museums.
dates: Fin XIIIe-début XIVe siècle de l’Hégire (fin XIXe-début XXe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: bijoux ; objets religieux ; décoration figurative

en.name: Dar Bach-Hamba
short_description: Behind a beautiful arched door, marking the entrance to Dar Bach Hamba, lies a vestibule leading to a central patio. Today's *dar* has kept only its huge proportions, ground floor and first floor galleries and symmetrical distribution of doors and windows on the surrounding apartments. The paving, door and window frames, neo-classical columns, and central fountain in the great hall are all made from marble imported from Carrara. The wooden ceilings in the bedrooms are painted in an Italian style. A smaller courtyard on the first floor is covered by a glass roof. The bedrooms generally open out onto balconies, with magnificent wooden coffered ceilings decorated with a rich floral pattern.
history: The Bach Hamba family, a noble military family of Turkish origins, gave their name to their home which stood here until 1923. Dar Bach Hamba is therefore a reminder of Tunisia in the first decades of the 20th century. It became the home of the Bach Hamba brothers, Mohamed and 'Ali, who had been co-founders of a part of the Young Tunisians (al-Harakat al-Shabab al-Tunisi) and of the first Tunisian French-language newspaper, *Le Tunisien*. After having served as the headquarters of the Sœurs Franciscaines du Christ Roi, Dar Bach Hamba became, in the year 2000, the seat of a Mediterranean cultural centre - the Fondazione Orestiadi - whose headquarters are in Sicily. The current building also houses a museum with an impressive collection of ceramics, textiles and clothes, which are all evidence for the links between the various Mediterranean cultures.
keywords: Architecture; art; painting; stucco; mosaic; marble; ceramics
partner: Higher Institute for the Study of Contemporary History of Tunisia, University of Manouba

fr.name: Dar Bach-Hamba
short_description: Au-delà d’une belle porte arquée marquant l’entrée de Dar Bach-Hamba, le vestibule conduit au patio central. De son originalité initiale, celui-ci n’a conservé que ses grandes proportions avec galeries au rez-de-chaussée et à l’étage ainsi que la distribution symétrique des portes et des fenêtres des appartements qui l’entourent : deux pièces en T, une chambre simple et une salle d’apparat. La cour principale présente une ornementation tout en marbre de Carrare, dallage, encadrement de portes et fenêtres, colonnes à chapiteaux néo-classiques, vasque centrale… Les plafonds en bois peint des chambres sont de style italianisant. A l’étage, une cour de proportion réduite est couverte d’une verrière. Ses chambres sont largement ouvertes sur les terrasses avec un magnifique plafond à caissons en bois où s’enchevêtre un décor floral foisonnant.
history: Les Bach Hamba, dignitaires militaires d’origine turque, ont donné leur nom à la demeure qui a été la leur jusqu’à 1923. Dar Bach-Hamba est un lieu de mémoire de la Tunisie de la première décennie du XXe siècle. Elle fut en effet la demeure des frères Bach Hamba, Mohamed et Ali, co-fondateurs du parti Jeunes Tunisiens et du premier journal tunisien en langue française, *Le Tunisien*. Après avoir été le siège de la fondation des sœurs franciscaines, Dar Bach-Hamba est depuis l’an 2000 le siège d’un centre culturel pour la Méditerranée, la fondation Orestiadi, dont le siège est en Sicile. Le monument abrite un musée avec un bel échantillonnage de céramiques, tissages et costumes, et témoigne de l’étonnante parenté des cultures méditerranéennes.
partner: Institut Supérieur d’histoire contemporaine de la Tunisie, Université de la Manouba

en.name: Church of the Paulistas
names: Igreja de Santa Catarina; Igreja dos Eremitas de S. Paulo da Serra d’Ossa
description: An urban church of considerable dimensions and flanked by other convent buildings. The façade has two symmetrical towers and a great receding pediment in the Late Baroque style. Three great stone arches give access to a large vaulted porch. The plan is based on a Latin cross with a single nave and side chapels, transept and a chancel. The altars are decorated in carved and gilded woodwork. Despite rebuilding, the church is mainly a synthesis of Baroque and Rocaille features, although during reconstruction in 1763, Neo-Classical elements were introduced. The church houses a collection of Baroque paintings by André Gonçalves. The richly decorated high altar was one of the first to be built during the reign of King João V. Designed by the master carver Santos Pacheco in 1728 its monumental wooden structure is flanked by two Italian-inspired Solomon columns, and a Churrigueresque column adorned with angels. The Solomon columns resonate theatrically with the great sculptural work in the pediment. Together these features mark the transition of a new taste in gilt wood carvings that witnessed great thrones and frontispieces inspired by Bernini and Andrea Pozzo.

The Church was part of a convent founded in 1647 for the Order of The Eremites of St. Paulo da Serra de Ossa, known as the Paulistas. The plan, based on a Latin cross, incorporates a deep chancel and side chapels. The interior decoration is well known for the carved and gilded woodwork of the altarpieces and the stucco ceiling.
artist: Padre Mestre Fr. Diogo da Ponte (1647)

Architect unknown; woodcarver: Santos Pacheco de Lima (active 1728); stucco ceiling: António Pimenta Rolim (c. 1759/1851); stucco work: João Grossi  [n.d.], Toscanelli [n.d.]; painters: André Gonçalves (1685–1762), Francisco Vieira de Matos (known as Vieira Lusitano 1699–1783).
history: In 1647, under the initiative of Father Diogo da Ponte, the Church of the Paulistas was founded as part of a convent for the Order of the Eremits of St. Paulo da Serra d' Ossa (Paulistas). It was built on the site of the former Church of Santa Catarina dos Livreiros. Building began in 1654 but the structure was seriously damaged in the Lisbon earthquake of 1755, and building was resumed with a new façade and vaults of the nave. Even so, parts of the original church were preserved and incorporated into the newly built church.
keywords: Church; carved and gilded woodwork; João V style, stucco work, Lisbon
tags: João V style, stucco work, Lisbon
partner: Institute for the Administration of Architectural and Archaeological Heritage -  IGESPAR

pt.name: *Igreja dos Paulistas*
names: Igreja de Santa Catarina; Igreja dos Eremitas de S. Paulo da Serra d’Ossa
description: Igreja de grandes dimensões, de implantação urbana, tem à ilharga o que resta dos edifícios do convento da congregação. A fachada é de tipo “palaciano”, com duas torres simétricas e um grande frontão de recorte tardo-barroco recuado. Três grandes vãos de pedraria dão acesso a uma ampla galilé. No interior, a igreja apresenta planta em cruz latina com nave única e capelas laterais decoradas por altares de talha dourada. Apesar de muito alterada, e marcada pelo gosto *rocaille* - e, mesmo, por apontamentos de estilo neo-clássico, fruto da reconstrução, que se concluiu pouco depois de 1763 -, o edifício contém um conjunto de pintura barroca da autoria de André Gonçalves, de temática eremítica e em consonância com a vocação da congregação ali sediada. Na talha, destaca-se, pela riqueza do desenho, o retábulo do altar-mor, um dos primeiros no chamado “estilo joanino”, do tempo de D. João V, e da autoria do mestre entalhador Santos Pacheco (1728). Trata-se de uma monumental “*machina*” de lavor em madeira, com duas colunas salomónicas nas ilhargas, assentes em estípites com a figura de anjos. O uso da coluna salomónica associada ao remate do arco e frontão marca a passagem para um novo gosto de trabalho de talha em que predominam os grandes tronos e os frontispícios inspirados em Bernini e Andrea Pozzo.

A Igreja dos Paulistas pertencia a um convento, fundado em 1647 para a Ordem dos Eremitas de São Paulo da Serra d’Ossa, conhecidos como Paulistas. Tem uma planta em cruz latina, com capela-mor profunda e capelas colaterais. A sua notoriedade advém-lhe da decoração interior, com especial destaque para o revestimento de talha dourada dos altares e os estuques do tecto.
artist: Padre Mestre Frei Diogo da Ponte (1647).

Arquitecto desconhecido; entalhador português: Santos Pacheco de Lima (activo 1728); pintura do tecto sobre estuque: António Pimenta Rolim (c. 1759–1851); estuques: João Grossi [n.d.], Toscanelli [n.d.]; pintores portugueses: André Gonçalves (1692–1762) e Francisco Vieira de Matos (ou Vieira Lusitano 1699–1783).
history: A igreja foi fundada em 1647, por iniciativa do Padre Frei Diogo da Ponte, como parte de um convento destinado aos Eremitas da Ordem de S. Paulo da Serra d’Ossa, no lugar da Igreja de Santa Catarina dos Livreiros, entretanto destruída. A igreja, cujas obras se iniciaram em 1654, foi, por sua vez, gravemente danificada durante o Terramoto de 1755. A reconstrução do templo dotou-o de uma nova fachada e foram reerguidas as abóbadas da nave. Mesmo assim, parte do recheio foi preservado e reinstalado na nova igreja. A sua implantação confere-lhe uma certa discrição, característica das reedificações pós-terramoto, mas é evidente o efeito de surpresa quando uma fachada relativamente sóbria dá entrada para uma igreja de dimensões amplas e com uma decoração solene.
keywords: Igreja; talha dourada; estilo D. João V; trabalho sobre estuque; Lisboa.

en.name: Request for financial help to the Minister of the Interior by Filippo Codispoti, a former Italian migrant to Cairo, who had to flee Egypt with his family in 1882
short_description:
In this letter Filippo Codispoti explained to the Italian Minister of Interior that he was born in Reggio Calabria (a town in Southern Italy) and was 17 years old before he migrated to Egypt. After years of hard work he had been able to reach a comfortable position and was running a wine and liquor shop, while his son was working as a shoemaker, and his daily pay was five and a half lire.  
He further explained that the civil war in Egypt had forced him to flee the country together with his wife and three children, leaving all his belongings in Egypt. He was now penniless and reduced to utter misery, and asked the government for financial help.  
According to governmental statistics, in 1882 there were 18,665 Italians in Egypt. The number of foreigners in Egypt totalled 90,886.
partner: MIBACT | State Archives of Reggio Calabria

en.name: Stream of flowers
description: Kyohei Fujita (1921-2004) was born in Tokyo in 1921 and joined the Department of Crafts at the Tokyo Fine Arts School (now known as Tokyo University of the Arts) to study metal engraving. After graduating he joined the Iwata Glass Company, but left shortly after to pursue a career as an independent glass artist. In 1964, he created the glasswork *Rainbow Colors*, which opened doors to international criticism. Later on, following many years of trial and error, he exhibited his *Ornament Boxes* in 1973, adapting the traditional Japanese aesthetic to suit a more contemporary style, using glass, which was very well received by the public. The following year, he continued to develop this series of ornament boxes, which have become so characteristic of Kyohei Fujita’s glasswork. They were very well received in the West as they fused the contemporary aesthetic with that of the traditional Rinpa School.
holder: Technological Glass Museum. Royal Factory of Glass and Crystal of La Granja
keywords: Glass sculpture; Fujita; Japan; VICOINTER; Studio Glass; Glass sculpture; Valencia
partner: Technological Glass Museum. Royal Factory of Glass and Crystal of La Granja

es.name: Stream of flowers
description: Kyohei Fujita (1921-2004) nació en Tokio en 1921 y, en 1940, ingresó en el Departamento de Artesanía de la Escuela de Bellas Artes de Tokio (ahora Tokio Arts University) para estudiar grabado sobre metal. Después de graduarse, entró en la Compañía de Vidrio Iwata, pero pronto dejó esta empresa para seguir una carrera como artista de vidrio independiente. En 1964, realizó la obra en vidrio *Rainbow Colors*, que le abrió las puertas de la crítica internacional. Posteriormente, después de muchos años de ensayo y error, exhibió sus *Ornament Boxes* en 1973, adaptando la estética japonesa tradicional a una forma más contemporánea, utilizando el vidrio como medio y recibiendo una gran aceptación ente el público. Al año siguiente, continuó desarrollando esta serie de "cajas ornamentales" tan representativas del arte de vidrio de Kyohei Fujita. Fueron muy bien acogidas en Occidente al fundirse la estética contemporánea con la tradicional Escuela de Rimpa.

ar.name: مخطوطة وردة حديقة العجائب
description: هذه المخطوطة التي صنعت لنصر الدين شاه قاجار (حكم خلال 1264-1313) هي مخطوطة حديقة ورود العجائب وتتألف من مائة وتسعة عشر صفحة مخططة وكل منها ذات عشرة أسطر مرشوشة بالذهب (نستعليق) بيد شكر الله نعمة – نيجار واسم نصر الدين شاه قاجار مذكور في الصفحة التي تسبق آخر صفحة في المخطوطة و رسمه الشخصي مرسوم في الرصائع المتوسطة على الغلاف الأمامي والخلفي والتجليد يعكس اشتراك الموروث القديم والحداثة خلال العصر القاجاري وهو يتميز بالتشكيل المعتاد للأشكال النباتية الملفوفة بالذهب على خلفية داكنة والمرتبطة بشدة ببورتريهات الشاه من الطراز الأوربي .
dates: أرخت في شوال – ذو القعدة 1310 هجري / أبريل – مايو 1893

en.name: Manuscript of *Gulshan-i Raz* (The Rose Garden of Mysteries)
description: Made for Nasir al-Din Shah Qajar (r. 1264–1313 AH/1848–96), the manuscript *Gulshan-i Raz* (The Rose Garden of Mysteries) consists of one hundred and nineteen calligraphic pages, each with ten lines of gold-sprinkled *nasta‘liq* in the hand of Shukrallah Nameh-Nigar. The name of Nasir al-Din Shah Qajar is mentioned on the page preceding the last one in the manuscript, and his portrait is painted on the central medallions on the front and back exterior covers. The binding reflects the combination of tradition and modernity during the Qajar period. It features the customary composition of scrolling vegetal motif in gold on a dark background wedded to European-style portraits of the shah.
keywords: Work-on-paper; works-on-paper; manuscript; calligraphy; vegetal motif; portrait; figure
materials: Ink, opaque watercolour, and gold on paper; lacquer binding

de.name: Benediktinerabtei St. Theodor und Alexander
description: Die vom baukundigen Pater Christoph Vogt entworfene Stiftsanlage zeigt sich terrainbedingt nicht wie üblich als ein nach Osten ausgerichtetes Gebäude, sondern als ein von Süden nach Norden gestrecktes Rechteck, das in dieser Richtung zudem von einer Mittelachse durchzogen wird. Baulichen Ausdruck gewinnt dadurch die besondere Konstitution als benediktinisches Abteikloster und eigenstaatliches Reichsstift. Diese Dualität mit der Osthälfte als mönchischen, durch den Bibliothekstrakt in zwei gleiche Höfe unterteilten Konventbau und der um einen einzelnen Hof gruppierten Westhälfte mit außen vorgesetzter Schaufassade als weltlich-reichsfürstlichem Residenzbau erscheint durch das rahmende Bautengeviert gefasst und zugleich gewahrt. Die Abteikirche steht frei vor dem Nordtrakt, wobei der Chor an den Stiftsbau anschließt. Ihre Fassade mit den pompösen Säulen und hohen Türmen ist auf Fernwirkung konzipiert. Im Inneren verdichten sich kolossale Säulen und Pfeiler szenographisch zu einem Prospekt, dessen Mittel- und Zielpunkt der Hochaltar bildet.

Die Benediktinerabtei Ottobeuren, dominiert von ihrer gewaltigen spätbarocken Kirche mit delikatem Rokoko-Interieur, gehört zu den größten und prachtvollsten barocken Klosteranlagen Süddeutschlands. Die gerne als “Schwäbischer Escorial” bezeichnete ehemalige Reichsabtei war von jeher Zentrum von Wissenschaft und Kultur und findet ihren profanen Höhepunkt im repräsentativen Kaisersaal, der mit seinem Prachtaufwand diesem hohen Anspruch gerecht wird.
artist: Äbte Rupert II. Ness (reg. 1710-1740), Anselm Erb (reg. 1740-1767)
history: Gestiftet bereits 764 von einem Grafen namens Silach, war ein wichtiger historischer Wendepunkt für das niederschwäbische Benediktinerkloster Ottobeuren die Entwicklung zur landesherrlich souveränen Reichsabtei im 13. Jh. Das damit verbundene Herrschaftsgebiet mit einer Vielzahl von Dörfern sollte später die ökonomische Grundlage für jene wirtschaftliche und kulturelle Blüte bilden, die das Kloster in der 1. Hälfte des 18. Jhs. unter dem tatkräftigen Abt Rupert Neß erlebte. Als „kaiserlicher Erbkaplan“ betitelt suchte dieser, mit einer gewaltigen schloßähnlichen Klosteranlage seiner politischen Nähe zum Wiener Kaiserhof Ausdruck zu verleihen. Der kostspielige, von einer Legion lokaler und überregionaler Künstler ausgestattete Komplex strapazierte dermaßen die Finanzmittel der Abtei, dass die Kirche hintangestellt werden musste. Kurz vor seinem Tod beauftragte Abt Rupert noch den schwäbischen Baumeister Simpert Kramer mit dem Kirchenbau, doch übergab sein Nachfolger diesen 1743 dem berühmten Münchner Architekten Johann Michael Fischer, der den Prestigebau bis 1766 vollenden konnte.
keywords: Reichsabtei, Kloster, Benediktiner, Kaisersaal, Festssaal, Theater, Hochaltar, Taufstein, Deckenmalerei
tags: Reichsabtei, Kloster, Benediktiner, Kaisersaal, Festssaal, Theater, Hochaltar, Taufstein, Deckenmalerei

en.name: Benedictine Abbey of St. Theodor and St. Alexander
description: The monastery complex designed by Father Christoph Vogt is not built facing east as is common, but rather, appears as a rectangle stretched from south to north and is divided in the same direction by a middle axis. In this way the combination of a Benedictine abbey cloister and a sovereign imperial foundation is given a special architectonic expression. The duality shown with the eastern half as a monastery divided by the library wing into two equal courtyards, and the western half surrounding a single courtyard with an outward projecting main facade as a secular, princely residence building, simultaneously appears included and preserved due to the framing effect of the quadrant construction. The abbey church stands alone in front of the north wing and the choir connects to the monastery complex. Its facade with pompous columns and high towers is intended to be viewed from afar. Inside, the colossal columns and pillars intensify the perspective view, the focus of which is the high altar.

The Benedictine Abbey Ottobeuren, dominated by its massive Late Baroque church with delicate Rococo interior, belongs to the largest and most marvellous Baroque monastery complex of southern Germany. The former imperial abbey, often called the “Swabian Escorial”, has always been a centre of science and culture culminating in its representative Imperial Hall, which lives up to expectations, with an amazing display of splendour.
dates: 1711–1731: monastery building; 1717–1724: economy building; 1737–1766: church; 1739–1740: government building
artist: Abbots Rupert II Ness (gov. 1710–1740), Anselm Erb (gov. 1740–1767)

Monastery complex (selection), architecture: Father Christoph Vogt OSB (1648–1725), Simpert Kramer (1675–1753), Andrea Maini (b. 1683); stucco, among others: Johann Baptist Zimmermann (1680–1758), Andrea Maini (b. 1683), Cristoforo Volpini (d. 1733); frescos in the Imperial Hall, its forecourt and south stairwell: Karl Jakob Stauder (1694–1751/56); frescoes of the Theatre Hall and north stairwell of the Imperial Hall: Franz Josef Spiegler (1691–1757); ceiling paintings of the Benedictus Chapel, the Winter Abbey and the Prince’s Rooms: Jacopo Amigoni (1682–1752)  
Abbey church (selection), architecture: Simpert Kramer (1675–1753), Johann Michael Fischer (1692–1766); frescoes: Johann Jakob (1708–1783), Franz Anton Zeiller (1716–83/94); stucco and altar architecture: Johann Michael Feichtmayr (1696–1772); sculpture and design of the choir stalls: Johann Joseph Christian (1706–1777); joinery of choir stalls and confessionals: Martin Hörmann (1688–1782)
history: Founded in 764 by a count of the name Silach an important historical turning point for the Lower Swabian Benedictine Monastery Ottobeuren was the appointment to a sovereign Imperial Abbey in the 13th century. The land over which this rule extended included a multitude of villages, which later would be the financial basis for the economic and cultural expansion that the monastery experienced during the first half of the 18th century under the active Abbot Rupert Ness. Addressed as the “Hereditary Imperial Chaplain”, Abbot Rupert attempted to express his political closeness to the imperial court in Vienna with an enormous residence-like monastery. This expensive complex, on which a legion of local and trans-local artists worked, was such a strain on the finances of the abbey that the church building had to be delayed. Shortly before his death, Abbot Rupert commissioned the Swabian master builder Simpert Kramer for the construction of the church; however, in 1743, his successor transferred this responsibility to the famous architect Johann Michael Fischer from Munich, who was able to complete the prestigious building in 1766.
keywords: Imperial abbey; monastery; Benedictine Order; Imperial Hall; ceremonial hall; theatre; high altar; font; ceiling painting
partner: University of Munich, Institute of Art History

ar.name: سعدي، أبو عبدالله مشرف الدين بن مصلح (الدين)، بستان (حديقة الفاكهة)
description: سعدي، أبو عبد الله مشرّف الدين بن مصلح (الدين) (توفي 691هـ / 1292م)، ألّف كتاب البستان، وهو أول أعماله المنشورة. يضم الكتاب حكايات أخلاقية تتداخل فيها روايات عن أسفار المؤلف وتجاربه المتعددة، وقد أصبح لاحقًا أحد أهم أعماله. كُتبت هذه النسخة بخط النستعليق في تبريز نحو 937–947هـ / حوالي 1530–1540م. وتحتوي المخطوطة على خمس لوحات تصويرية تكاد تكون بصفحة كاملة. وتذكّر هذه اللوحات بأسلوب المدرسة التيمورية في هراة. وفي عام 1677، اقتُنيت المخطوطة في القسطنطينية مقابل 36 دوقية ذهبية.

en.name: Sa'di, Abu 'Abd-Allah Musharrif ad-Din b. Muslih (ad-Din), *Bustan* (Fruit Garden)
description: Sa'di, Abu 'Abd-Allah Musharrif ad-Din b. Muslih (ad-Din) (died 691 AH/ 1292 AD), wrote the *Bustan* (‘Fruit Garden’), which was his first published work. It contains ethical anecdotes incorporating the accounts of the author’s travels and his manifold experiences, and would later become one of his major works. This copy was written in *nasta’liq* script in Tabriz around 937-47 AH / c. 1530-40 AD. The manuscript contains five nearly full-page paintings. The paintings are reminiscent of the style of the Timurid school of Herat. In 1677, it was acquired in Constantinople for 36 gold ducats.
keywords: Bustan; painting; Safavid; Yusuf; Zulaikha
materials: Ink, opaque watercolour and gold on paper. Calligraphic *nasta'liq* script of 16 lines.
